**What you will learn:** Crochet a thick ribbed scarf with front-post and back-post double crochet, keep straight edges, and add a twisted fringe. **Skill level:** Beginner. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 22 cm wide and 180 cm long, plus a 12 cm fringe at each end. **Time:** one weekend, roughly 5 to 6 hours of relaxed crocheting.

Pick a soft bulky yarn for this project, because the scarf sits against your neck all day. Wool blends are the warmest choice, while acrylic blends are easier to wash and a good pick for a first scarf. Make a small gauge swatch before you start, and if your scarf comes out wider than 22 cm, go down half a hook size.

## Materials and Tools

![Chunky yarn, a large crochet hook, scissors and a tapestry needle arranged on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/chunky-ribbed-scarf-materials.webp)

Bulky weight yarn (#5), about 300 g or 3 skeins of 100 g; a 6.5 mm crochet hook; a tapestry needle; scissors; a tape measure. Optional: a book or a piece of card 15 cm wide for cutting the fringe to an even length.

Check the ball band before you buy: you need about 360 metres of bulky yarn in total. If your skeins are smaller, buy one extra so you do not run out halfway through the last rows.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), double crochet (dc), front-post double crochet (fpdc), back-post double crochet (bpdc), slip stitch (sl st). **Gauge:** 10 stitches and 7 rows measure 10 cm in the ribbing pattern, using a 6.5 mm hook. The ribbing pulls in slightly, so measure your swatch flat without stretching it.

To work a front-post double crochet, yarn over, insert the hook from the front around the post of the stitch below, and finish the double crochet as normal. For a back-post double crochet, insert the hook from the back around the post instead.

## The Pattern

Chain 26.

**Row 1:** Double crochet in the 4th chain from the hook, double crochet in each chain across. You should have 24 double crochet stitches, counting the turning chain as the first stitch.

**Row 2:** Chain 3 (counts as the first double crochet). Work 2 front-post double crochet around the next 2 stitches, then 2 back-post double crochet around the next 2 stitches. Repeat the 2 front-post and 2 back-post pairs across the row, and finish with a double crochet in the top of the turning chain. You should have 24 stitches.

**Rows 3 to 90:** Repeat Row 2. Always work front-post stitches around front-post stitches and back-post stitches around back-post stitches, so the ridges line up. Count your stitches every ten rows: if you have more than 24, you are adding a stitch at the edge; if you have fewer, you are skipping the last stitch. At the end of Row 90 the scarf should measure about 180 cm long.

![Close-up of chunky ribbed crochet texture in cream yarn with raised vertical ridges](https://cozyloops.site/assets/chunky-ribbed-scarf-stitch-closeup.webp)

Fasten off and weave in both ends with the tapestry needle, following the path of the stitches so the ends disappear inside the ribbing.

## Adding the Fringe

Cut 36 strands of yarn, each 30 cm long. Fold 3 strands in half and pull the loop through an edge stitch with the hook, then pull the ends through the loop and tighten gently. Repeat across both short ends, with 6 knots on each end, spaced evenly. Trim the fringe so the ends are level, and twist each knot a few times if you like a tidier finish.

## Styling and Care

Wear the scarf looped once around the neck with the ends hanging in front, or wrap it twice for very cold days. The ribbing grips a coat collar nicely, so it stays put without a pin.

Wash the scarf by hand in cool water with a mild detergent, press out the water in a towel, and dry it flat. Machine washing can felt wool blends and stretch the ribbing out of shape, so keep it out of the machine. Store the scarf folded, not hung, so the weight of the yarn does not stretch the rows over the summer.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does this scarf take to make?** Most beginners finish it in one weekend, in about 5 to 6 hours of crocheting.

**Can I make the scarf wider or narrower?** Yes. Add or remove stitches in multiples of 4, keeping the 2 front-post and 2 back-post rhythm. For a narrower scarf, chain 22 and work 20 stitches; for a wider one, chain 30 and work 28 stitches.

**What if my edges are wavy?** Wavy edges usually mean the turning chain is being worked into, or skipped, at the end of rows. Always finish the row with a double crochet in the top of the turning chain, and count your stitches every few rows until the edge stays straight.

**Can I use a different yarn weight?** You can, but the finished size and the yarn amount will change. With worsted weight yarn and a 5 mm hook, chain 34 for a similar width and work more rows to reach 180 cm.

title: Granny Stripe Crochet Scarf: A Colourful Classic for Winter
excerpt: Crochet a cheerful striped scarf with simple granny clusters in four colours — an easy classic for winter.
image_alt: Colourful granny stripe crochet scarf with coral, mustard, teal and cream stripes.
content:
The granny stripe is one of those crochet patterns that never goes out of fashion. It is a row of simple three-stitch clusters, repeated in cheerful stripes, and it turns a basic scarf into something people ask about. This granny stripe crochet scarf pattern uses four colours, a 5 mm hook and one easy row repeat, so it is a perfect second project for a beginner and a relaxing evening project for anyone else.

What makes the granny stripe special is how forgiving it is. The clusters sit in the spaces between the clusters below, so there are no fiddly stitches to count into, and the stripe sequence does the decorating for you. Change the colours and the whole scarf changes character: bright stripes for a playful look, soft pastels for spring, or deep autumn shades for a classic winter scarf.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Crochet the granny stripe stitch, change colours cleanly every two rows, and finish a scarf with a neat border and fringe. **Skill level:** Beginner. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 20 cm wide and 150 cm long, plus fringe. **Time:** one week of evenings, roughly 6 to 7 hours.

Choose four colours that look good together in a stripe. A good rule is two warm colours, one cool colour and one neutral: coral, mustard, teal and cream work well together, as do rose, sage, dusty blue and oatmeal. Use the same yarn brand and weight for all four colours so the stripes stay the same height.

## Materials and Tools

![Four balls of worsted yarn in coral, mustard, teal and cream with a crochet hook and scissors](https://cozyloops.site/assets/granny-stripe-scarf-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in 4 colours, about 100 g of each colour; a 5 mm crochet hook; a tapestry needle; scissors; a tape measure. Optional: stitch markers to mark the first cluster of a row while you learn the pattern.

Buy all four colours at once and check that the dye lots match within each colour.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), double crochet (dc), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Gauge:** 14 stitches and 8 rows measure 10 cm in the granny stripe pattern, using a 5 mm hook. The stripe rows are taller than plain rows, so the scarf grows quickly.

The granny stripe is built from clusters of 3 double crochet stitches worked into a chain space. The trick is to work into the space between clusters, not into the top of a stitch: push the hook under the chain space, yarn over and work the cluster there.

## The Pattern

Use Colour A for the first two rows, then change colour every two rows in this order: A, B, C, D, then repeat A, B, C, D until the scarf is long enough.

Chain 43.

**Row 1:** Work 3 double crochet in the 4th chain from the hook, skip 2 chains, work 3 double crochet in the next chain. Repeat the skip-2 and 3-double-crochet pattern across the row, and finish with 1 double crochet in the last chain. You should have 13 clusters and 1 double crochet at the end.

**Row 2:** Chain 3 (counts as the first double crochet). Work 3 double crochet in the first space between clusters, then 3 double crochet in each space across the row, and finish with 1 double crochet in the top of the turning chain. You should have 13 clusters.

**Rows 3 to 120:** Repeat Row 2, changing colour every two rows in the sequence A, B, C, D. After 120 rows the scarf should measure about 150 cm long. Do not worry if your row count is a little different: the important thing is the length, so measure the scarf flat every twenty rows.

![Close-up of granny stripe crochet with coral, mustard, teal and cream stripes](https://cozyloops.site/assets/granny-stripe-scarf-stitch-closeup.webp)

**Border:** With Colour D, work 1 round of single crochet evenly around all four edges, putting 3 single crochet in each corner stitch. Fasten off and weave in all remaining ends with the tapestry needle.

## Adding the Fringe

Cut strands of yarn 25 cm long, using all four colours. Fold 3 strands in half, pull the loop through a border stitch with the hook, then pull the ends through the loop and tighten. Space the knots evenly along both short ends, mixing the colours so the fringe echoes the stripes. Trim the ends level.

## Styling and Care

A striped scarf does the work of a whole outfit: wear it with a plain coat and let the colours show. Wrap it once with the ends in front for a casual look, or loop it twice and tuck the ends in on colder days.

Wash the scarf by hand in cool water and dry it flat so the stripes keep their shape. If you used acrylic yarn, you can machine wash on a gentle cold cycle, but still dry it flat: hanging a wet striped scarf can stretch the lighter rows unevenly. Store it folded with a lavender sachet to keep it fresh between winters.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I change colours without a messy edge?** Finish the last double crochet of the row with the new colour: work the stitch until two loops remain on the hook, then yarn over with the new colour and pull through. Cut the old yarn, leaving a 10 cm tail to weave in later.

**Can I use more or fewer than four colours?** Yes. Two colours make a bold classic stripe, and six colours make a scrap-busting rainbow.

**What if my clusters lean to one side?** Leaning clusters usually mean the turning chain is being counted as a cluster. Remember that the chain 3 at the start of the row counts as the first double crochet, and the last double crochet goes into the top of that chain, not into a space.

**How much yarn do I need in total?** About 400 g of worsted weight yarn, roughly 100 g per colour.

title: Ribbed Crochet Beanie: A Beginner Pattern in Adult Sizes
excerpt: Crochet a warm ribbed beanie with a stretchy brim and simple crown decreases, in adult sizes M and L.
image_alt: Ribbed crochet beanie in forest green wool with a folded brim and a pom-pom.
content:
A ribbed beanie is the hat every crocheter should make at least once. It uses the same two stitches as a ribbed scarf, it fits a wide range of heads thanks to the stretchy brim, and it works up in an evening or two. This ribbed crochet beanie pattern gives you two adult sizes, a clear crown decrease you can follow round by round,

The secret of a good beanie is the brim. Front-post and back-post double crochet stitches pull the fabric in, so the brim grips gently without squeezing, and the body sits comfortably over the ears.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Crochet a beanie in the round, work a ribbed brim, and shape the crown with even decreases. **Skill level:** Beginner. **Terminology:** US. **Finished sizes:** Adult M fits a head of 56 to 58 cm; Adult L fits 59 to 61 cm. **Time:** one or two evenings, roughly 3 to 4 hours.

Choose a soft worsted weight yarn for this hat, because it sits against the forehead and ears.

## Materials and Tools

![Two skeins of forest green worsted yarn, a crochet hook, a tape measure, a yarn needle and scissors](https://cozyloops.site/assets/ribbed-beanie-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4), about 100 g or 1 skein of 100 g; a 5 mm crochet hook; a stitch marker; a tapestry needle; scissors; a tape measure. Optional: a pom-pom maker or a piece of card for a yarn pom-pom.

One 100 g skein is enough for size M; buy a second skein in the same dye lot for size L.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), half double crochet (hdc), double crochet (dc), front-post double crochet (fpdc), back-post double crochet (bpdc), double crochet two together (dc2tog). **Gauge:** 14 stitches and 10 rounds measure 10 cm in half double crochet, using a 5 mm hook.

For a front-post stitch, insert the hook from the front around the post; for a back-post stitch, insert it from the back. To work a dc2tog, yarn over, pull up a loop in the first stitch, yarn over and pull through two loops, then repeat in the next stitch and pull through all three loops on the hook.

## The Pattern

Chain 64 for size M, or 72 for size L. Join with a slip stitch to the first chain, taking care not to twist the chain.

**Rounds 1 to 6 — ribbed brim:** Chain 3 (counts as the first double crochet). Work 2 front-post double crochet around the next 2 stitches, then 2 back-post double crochet around the next 2 stitches. Repeat the 2 front-post and 2 back-post pairs around, and join with a slip stitch to the top of the chain 3. You should have 64 stitches for size M, or 72 for size L.

![Close-up of a ribbed crochet beanie brim in forest green yarn](https://cozyloops.site/assets/ribbed-beanie-stitch-closeup.webp)

**Rounds 7 to 18 — body:** Chain 2 (does not count as a stitch). Work 1 half double crochet in each stitch around, and join with a slip stitch to the first half double crochet. Repeat this round 12 times in total.

**Crown decreases — size M (64 stitches):** Work in double crochet from here, and join each round with a slip stitch to the first stitch.

- Round 19: chain 3, work *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 6 stitches* around. You should have 56 stitches.
- Round 20: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 5 stitches* around. You should have 48 stitches.
- Round 21: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 4 stitches* around. You should have 40 stitches.
- Round 22: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 3 stitches* around. You should have 32 stitches.
- Round 23: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 2 stitches* around. You should have 24 stitches.
- Round 24: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next stitch* around. You should have 16 stitches.
- Round 25: dc2tog around. You should have 8 stitches.

**Crown decreases — size L (72 stitches):** Work Round 19 as *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 7 stitches* around, which leaves 64 stitches, then follow Rounds 20 to 25 exactly as written for size M.

Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail. Thread the tail through the remaining 8 stitches with the tapestry needle, pull gently to close the hole, and weave the end inside the crown.

## Finishing

Weave in the starting tail along the inside of the brim so it never shows. If you are adding a pom-pom, make one about 8 cm across and sew it firmly to the top of the crown with several passes of yarn, pulling each pass tight. Give the pom-pom a firm tug: it should not move at all.

Try the hat on: the brim should sit over the ears without leaving a mark. If it feels tight, go up half a hook size for the brim next time.

## Styling and Care

Wear the brim folded up for a classic fit, or unfolded for extra ear coverage on cold mornings.

Hand wash the beanie in cool water with a mild detergent, press out the water in a towel, and dry it flat over a bowl or a rolled towel so it keeps its shape. Machine washing can shrink wool blends and flatten the ribbing, so keep it out of the machine.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**My head measures between M and L. Which size should I make?** Make size M. The ribbed brim stretches by several centimetres, so size M fits heads from about 54 to 59 cm comfortably

**Can I make the beanie longer?** Yes. Add two extra body rounds before the crown decreases for a slightly slouchier fit, or add four extra rounds for a beanie that folds further over the ears.

**How do I stop the brim from stretching out?** Work the brim rounds with a firm, even tension and do not stretch the hat while it dries.

**Can I skip the pom-pom?** Yes, the hat looks just as good without one, and many people prefer a plain crown.

title: Slouchy Crochet Beanie: A Relaxed Fit with a Soft Drape
excerpt: A relaxed slouchy beanie with a ribbed brim and a soft draped crown, in DK yarn with a faux fur pom-pom.
image_alt: Slouchy crochet beanie in dusty rose yarn with a draped crown and a faux fur pom-pom.
content:
Some beanies hug the head, and some drape. This slouchy crochet beanie does the second: a ribbed brim that stays put, a longer body that folds softly at the back, and a crown that gathers into a gentle point under a fluffy pom-pom.

The slouch comes from length, not from looseness. This slouchy crochet beanie pattern is worked bottom-up in the round, so there is no seaming at all. The body is worked a few rounds longer than a fitted beanie, in soft DK yarn that drapes instead of standing up. Because the extra length is in the body, the brim still fits like a normal hat, so the beanie stays on in the wind.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Crochet a slouchy beanie with a ribbed brim, a longer draped body and even crown decreases. **Skill level:** Easy, suitable for a confident beginner. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** one size fits most adults, head 56 to 59 cm, about 28 cm long from brim to crown. **Time:** two evenings, roughly 4 to 5 hours.

Choose a soft DK yarn with a little drape for this hat. A wool blend or a soft acrylic both work well; a stiff cotton will not slouch, so save cotton for summer hats.

## Materials and Tools

![Two skeins of dusty rose DK yarn, a crochet hook, a faux fur pom-pom and a yarn needle on a knitted blanket](https://cozyloops.site/assets/slouchy-beanie-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3), about 120 g; a 4.5 mm crochet hook; a stitch marker; a tapestry needle; scissors; a tape measure. Optional: one faux fur pom-pom with a snap or ties, about 10 cm across.

You need about 300 metres of DK yarn, so buy two skeins if yours are 100 g.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), double crochet (dc), front-post double crochet (fpdc), back-post double crochet (bpdc), double crochet two together (dc2tog). **Gauge:** 16 stitches and 10 rounds measure 10 cm in double crochet, using a 4.5 mm hook.

The body of this hat is worked in plain double crochet, which is what gives it the soft drape.

## The Pattern

Chain 72. Join with a slip stitch to the first chain, taking care not to twist the chain.

**Rounds 1 to 5 — ribbed brim:** Chain 3 (counts as the first double crochet). Work 2 front-post double crochet around the next 2 stitches, then 2 back-post double crochet around the next 2 stitches. Repeat the 2 front-post and 2 back-post pairs around, and join with a slip stitch to the top of the chain 3. You should have 72 stitches.

**Rounds 6 to 24 — slouchy body:** Chain 3 (counts as the first double crochet). Work 1 double crochet in each stitch around, and join with a slip stitch to the top of the chain 3. Repeat this round 19 times in total. After Round 24 the hat should measure about 28 cm from the cast-on edge.

![Close-up of a slouchy crochet beanie crown in dusty rose yarn with a faux fur pom-pom](https://cozyloops.site/assets/slouchy-beanie-stitch-closeup.webp)

**Crown decreases:** Work in double crochet, joining each round with a slip stitch to the first stitch.

- Round 25: chain 3, work *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 7 stitches* around. You should have 64 stitches.
- Round 26: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 6 stitches* around. You should have 56 stitches.
- Round 27: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 5 stitches* around. You should have 48 stitches.
- Round 28: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 4 stitches* around. You should have 40 stitches.
- Round 29: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 3 stitches* around. You should have 32 stitches.
- Round 30: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 2 stitches* around. You should have 24 stitches.
- Round 31: *dc2tog, double crochet in the next stitch* around. You should have 16 stitches.
- Round 32: dc2tog around. You should have 8 stitches.

Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail. Thread the tail through the remaining 8 stitches, pull gently to close the hole, and weave the end inside the crown. Attach the pom-pom firmly to the top with several tight passes of yarn.

## Finishing

Weave in the starting tail along the inside of the brim. Put the hat on and push the crown gently to one side so the slouch falls naturally at the back; the extra length should fold softly rather than stick up.

Block the hat lightly if the stitches look uneven: soak it in cool water for ten minutes, press out the water in a towel, and dry it flat with the slouch arranged the way you want it to fall.

## Styling and Care

Wear the slouch at the back with the brim low over the forehead, and let the pom-pom sit slightly off-centre for a casual look. It also works indoors as a cosy layer on cold mornings.

Hand wash in cool water with a mild detergent and dry flat, keeping the slouch folded the way you like it. If your pom-pom is removable, take it off before washing and reattach it afterwards. Do not hang the hat to dry: the weight of the wet yarn will stretch the body out of shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How slouchy is this beanie, really?** The body is about 10 cm longer than a fitted beanie, so the crown folds softly at the back instead of sitting flat on the head.

**Can I make it for a smaller head?** Yes. Chain 64 instead of 72 and work the crown decreases starting at Round 25 with *dc2tog, double crochet in the next 6 stitches* for 56 stitches, then follow Rounds 27 to 32 as written.

**What if I do not want a pom-pom?** Leave it off: the gathered crown looks neat on its own.

**Can I use worsted weight yarn instead of DK?** You can, but use a 5 mm hook and expect a slightly heavier hat with a shorter slouch.

title: Snowman Amigurumi with Scarf and Top Hat
excerpt: Crochet a friendly snowman amigurumi with a no-sew scarf worked in the round and a stiffened top hat — a cheerful Christmas ornament.
image_alt: Handmade crochet snowman amigurumi with a red striped scarf and black top hat, standing on a wooden table.
content:
A snowman is the friendliest Christmas decoration you can crochet: three soft white balls, a carrot nose, a striped scarf and a top hat that actually stands up. This crochet snowman amigurumi pattern makes one snowman about 18 cm tall, with a no-sew scarf worked in the round — almost no sewing at the end. If you can work a single crochet sphere, you can make this snowman.

The scarf is the clever part: a ring worked in the round that slips over the neck, with a short tail joined by slip stitches. The top hat is stiffened with glue and water, so it holds its shape.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Three graduated spheres, a no-sew scarf in the round, a stiffened top hat, and invisible joining. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 18 cm tall, 9 cm wide. **Time:** one weekend, 4 to 5 hours.

Use smooth worsted yarn: texture hides the stitch definition that makes the snowballs neat. White is classic; the scarf and hat use little red and black.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of white, black, orange and red worsted yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, 9 mm safety eyes, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-snowman-amigurumi-scarf-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): white 80 g, black 20 g, red 20 g, orange a little for the nose; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; 9 mm black safety eyes; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker. Optional: white glue, water, a ribbon.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), double crochet (dc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), front-post double crochet (fpdc). **Gauge:** 18 stitches and 20 rounds measure 10 cm in single crochet with a 3.5 mm hook. Work tightly enough that the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

A front-post double crochet goes around the post of the stitch below; it makes the raised band at the base of the hat brim.

## The Pattern

Work the snowballs in a spiral, marking the first stitch of each round.

**Bottom snowball (white):** Rounds 1–6: 6 sc in a magic ring, then inc to 12, (sc, inc) to 18, (2 sc, inc) to 24, (3 sc, inc) to 30, (4 sc, inc) to 36. Rounds 7–12: sc around (36). Rounds 13–17: (4 sc, dec) to 30, (3 sc, dec) to 24, (2 sc, dec) to 18, stuff firmly, (sc, dec) to 12, dec to 6. Fasten off and close.

**Middle snowball (white):** As the bottom snowball through Round 5 (30), then Rounds 6–9 sc (30). Decrease: (3 sc, dec) to 24, (2 sc, dec) to 18, stuff, (sc, dec) to 12, dec to 6. Fasten off.

**Head (white):** Through Round 4 (24), then Rounds 5–8 sc (24). Round 9: (2 sc, dec) to 18. Stuff firmly. Round 10: (sc, dec) to 12. Round 11: dec to 6. Fasten off and close.

**Arms (make 2, dark brown or black):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Rounds 2–8: sc around (6). Stuff lightly, flatten the end, fasten off with a tail for sewing.

**Nose (orange):** Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 2 times (6). Round 3: sc around (6). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 2 times (8). Round 5: sc around (8). Fasten off with a sewing tail, stuffing the tip lightly.

**Scarf (red):** Chain 44, join with a slip stitch without twisting. Rounds 1–2: hdc around in red (44). Round 3: white hdc around (44). Round 4: red sc around (44). Fasten off. Tail: chain 12, work 6 rows of hdc (12), slip-stitch it to the ring along one short edge.

![Close-up of white single crochet snowman stitches and the black top hat brim with front-post stitches](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-snowman-amigurumi-hat-closeup.webp)

**Top hat (black):** Crown: Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: sc in back loop only (24) for the crisp crown edge. Rounds 6–9: sc around (24). Brim: Round 10: fpdc around (24). Round 11: (dc, inc) 12 times (36). Round 12: dc around (36). Fasten off. Stiffen with half-and-half glue and water, shaped over a jar, dried overnight.

**Assembly:** Sew the middle snowball to the bottom one, then the head on top. Slip the scarf ring over the neck first, so it is trapped in place and never needs sewing. Sew the arms to the middle snowball, angled upward. Attach the safety eyes between Rounds 6 and 7 of the head, 6 stitches apart, before stuffing it. Sew the nose below the eyes, and three small black buttons down the front — or crochet three tiny black circles (6 sc in a magic ring). Sew the hat on tilted, with a ribbon loop at the back for hanging.

## Styling and Care

Stand it on a shelf, mantel or windowsill, or hang it from a branch with the ribbon loop. It pairs with the penguin ornament already on the site and the gingerbread man in this set. Keep it out of direct sunlight and spot-clean with a damp cloth. Do not machine wash: the stiffened hat would lose its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I make the hat stand up?** Work the crown firmly, stuff it lightly, and brush it with half-and-half white glue and water. Shape it over a jar and dry overnight — it will hold all season.

**What stuffing keeps the snowman round?** Polyester toy stuffing, added in small pinches. Stuff the bottom ball firmly and the head slightly less firmly, so the face stays smooth.

**Can I hang it on the tree?** Yes — sew a short ribbon loop to the back of the hat before sewing the hat on. The snowman weighs very little, so a thin ribbon is enough.

**Can I make the snowman bigger?** Yes — chunky yarn with a 5 mm hook and the same counts makes a 24 cm snowman. You will need about twice as much white yarn, and 12 mm eyes suit the larger size.

title: Gingerbread Man Amigurumi: Free Pattern with Icing Stitches
excerpt: Crochet a gingerbread man amigurumi with embroidered icing stitches and sewn buttons, with a flat-back option for hanging on the tree.
image_alt: Handmade crochet gingerbread man amigurumi with white embroidered icing and red buttons.
content:
A gingerbread man is the quickest Christmas amigurumi you can crochet: one warm brown body, white icing lines, and three red buttons — ready for the tree the same evening you start him. This gingerbread man crochet pattern makes one doll about 16 cm tall, with embroidered icing, sewn buttons, and a flat-back option for the tree.

The icing is simpler than it looks: surface slip stitch pulls white yarn up through the front and chains along the surface. The buttons are French knots: two wraps of red yarn around the needle.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A joined-leg body, surface slip stitch icing, French knots, a flat-back version. **Skill level:** Beginner. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 16 cm tall, 10 cm wide at the arms. **Time:** one evening, roughly 3 hours.

Choose a warm medium brown — ginger or milk chocolate reads as gingerbread. White is only for the icing, so a small ball is enough.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of brown, white and red worsted yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, 8 mm safety eyes, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/gingerbread-man-amigurumi-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): brown 60 g, white 15 g, red a little for the buttons; a 3 mm crochet hook; 8 mm black safety eyes; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker. Optional: a ribbon and a steam iron.

For a set of four, buy two balls of brown.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), surface slip stitch for the icing, French knot for the buttons. **Gauge:** 20 stitches and 22 rounds measure 10 cm in single crochet with a 3 mm hook. Keep your tension firm so the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

To work a surface slip stitch, hold the white yarn behind the work, pull a loop up through the front, then step along the line and pull a new loop through the loop on the hook. Keep the stitches even and loose, so the line lies flat.

## The Pattern

**Legs (make 2, brown):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (2 sc, inc) 4 times (16). Rounds 4–5: sc around (16). Fasten off the first leg only — the second leg continues into the body.

**Body (brown):** Round 6: 16 sc around each leg, joining them into one round (32). Rounds 7–11: sc around (32). Round 12: (6 sc, dec) 4 times (28). Round 13: sc around (28). Round 14: (5 sc, dec) 4 times (24). Round 15: (4 sc, dec) 4 times (20). Stuff firmly. Round 16: (3 sc, dec) 4 times (16).

**Head (brown, continuing the body):** Round 17: (sc, inc) 8 times (24). Round 18: (2 sc, inc) 8 times (32). Round 19: (3 sc, inc) 8 times (40). Rounds 20–24: sc around (40). Round 25: (3 sc, dec) 8 times (32). Round 26: (2 sc, dec) 8 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 27: (sc, dec) 8 times (16). Round 28: dec 8 times (8). Fasten off and close.

**Arms (make 2, brown):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 3 times (9). Rounds 3–9: sc around (9). Stuff lightly, flatten the end, fasten off with a sewing tail. Sew them to the body at Round 13, angled downward.

**Eyes and smile:** Attach the 8 mm safety eyes between Rounds 21 and 22, 8 stitches apart, before stuffing the head. Embroider a smile in dark brown: a short curved line under the eyes.

![Close-up of white surface slip stitch icing and a red French knot button on a crochet gingerbread man](https://cozyloops.site/assets/gingerbread-man-amigurumi-icing-closeup.webp)

**Icing (white, surface slip stitch):** Work a wavy line around the head edge, like a hairline, then matching lines around each wrist and ankle, a swirl on the chest, and a line down each leg. Keep the lines loose, or the brown fabric puckers.

**Buttons (red, French knots):** Bring red yarn up through the front at Round 12, wrap it twice around the needle, and push the needle back down beside where it came up, holding the wraps as you pull through. Repeat at Rounds 10 and 14, evenly spaced down the body.

**Flat-back option:** Stuff lightly, lay the doll face-down on a towel, and press the back flat. Hold a steam iron a few centimetres above the back (never press it onto the yarn) for a few seconds, then leave the doll face-down until it cools. The front stays rounded and the back sits flat. Add a hanging loop: chain 12, slip stitch into a ring, and sew it to the top of the head.

## Styling and Care

Hang him on the tree, prop him next to the snowman from this set, or tie him to a present as a keepsake gift tag. A set of four in different browns looks like a fresh batch. Spot-clean with a damp cloth and keep him out of direct sunlight. Do not machine wash: the icing would loosen.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I embroider neat icing lines?** Keep the white yarn loose and take short steps — about one stitch long — between surface slip stitches. If the line puckers, unpick the last few stitches and redo them loosely. Practise on a spare swatch first.

**Will the flat-back version still stand?** It will lean, not stand. The flat-back version is for hanging on the tree or lying on a shelf. For a standing doll, skip the flat-back step and stuff firmly.

**What yarn gives a cookie colour?** A warm medium brown: ginger, milk chocolate, or light caramel. Avoid very dark browns (chocolate cake) and yellow-browns (a lion, not a cookie). Smooth yarn shows the icing best.

**Can I make a set in different sizes?** Yes — DK yarn with a 2.5 mm hook and the same counts makes a 12 cm mini, and chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook makes a 20 cm version. The icing and buttons stay the same in every size.

title: Christmas Angel Amigurumi with Lace Wings
excerpt: Crochet an heirloom-style Christmas angel amigurumi with shell-stitch lace wings and a wire halo ring wrapped in gold yarn.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas angel amigurumi with a cream dress, white lace shell-stitch wings and a gold wire halo.
content:
A Christmas angel turns a tree into an heirloom: soft cream lace, a gold halo, and wings that catch the light. This crochet Christmas angel pattern makes one angel about 20 cm tall, with shell-stitch lace wings and a wire halo ring wrapped in gold yarn.

The wings are small shell-stitch fans, stiffened with glue and water so they hold their shape. The dress is worked top-down in one piece, so there is almost no sewing. If you can work a double crochet shell, you can make this angel.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A top-down flared dress, shell-stitch lace fans, a wire halo wrapped in yarn, and invisible joining. **Skill level:** Easy to intermediate. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 20 cm tall, 12 cm wide across the wings. **Time:** one weekend, 5 to 6 hours.

Use smooth DK yarn in cream, white and gold.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream, white and gold DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, 6 mm safety eyes, scissors, a yarn needle, gold craft wire and white glue on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-angel-amigurumi-lace-wings-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3): cream 60 g, white 20 g, gold 15 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; 6 mm black safety eyes or black embroidery thread; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; 20 cm of thin gold craft wire; white glue and water for stiffening.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc), shell (5 dc in one stitch), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 22 single crochet stitches and 26 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Work tightly enough that the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

A shell is five double crochets in one stitch; three shells around a small ring make a fan.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch of each round. Head and arms are cream, wings white, hair and halo gold.

**Dress (cream):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–7: sc around (24). Round 8: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Rounds 9–10: sc around (30). Round 11: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 12–13: sc around (36). Round 14: (8 sc, inc) 4 times (40). Rounds 15–17: sc around (40). Round 18 (shell edge, cream or gold): *(skip 1 st, 5 dc in next st, skip 1 st, sc in next st)* repeat 10 times around. Fasten off.

**Head (cream):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–8: sc around (24). Round 9: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 10: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 11: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Hair (gold):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: sc around (24). Round 6 (curls): *(ch 5, sl st in next st)* repeat around. Sew the cap to the top of the head, curls framing the face.

**Arms (make 2, cream):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Rounds 2–7: sc around (6). Stuff lightly, flatten the end, and sew the arms to the dress at Round 6, angled upward, hands joined in prayer.

**Wings (make 2, white):** Round 1: ch 4, join with a slip stitch to form a ring. Round 2: ch 3 (counts as dc), 11 dc in the ring (12). Round 3 (shell fan): *(sc in next st, skip 1 st, 5 dc in next st, skip 1 st)* repeat 3 times. Fasten off with a long tail. Stiffen each wing with half-and-half glue and water, pinned flat overnight. Sew the ring edge to the back of the dress at Round 7, fanning outward.

![Close-up of a white crochet shell-stitch fan wing with five double crochets fanning into a scallop](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-angel-amigurumi-lace-wings-closeup.webp)

**Halo (gold):** Shape 20 cm of gold wire into a 6 cm ring, twisting the ends together. Chain 24, then work 24 sc around the wire ring to cover it in gold yarn. Sew a short gold stem (chain 6) to the top of the head and attach the ring so the halo floats just above the hair.

**Assembly:** Sew the head to the dress and the arms in place, hands joined. Attach the wings to the back. Add the safety eyes between Rounds 6 and 7 of the head, 5 stitches apart, before stuffing — or embroider them for a softer look. Embroider a small smile, add a chain-12 hanging loop to the back of the head, and tie a gold ribbon around the waist if you like.

## Styling and Care

Stand her on a mantel or shelf, hang her on the tree, or use her as a tree topper — a wooden skewer through the dress holds her upright. She pairs with the snowman and gingerbread man from this set. Spot-clean with a damp cloth; do not machine wash, or the stiffened wings will lose their shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I stiffen the wings?** Brush each wing with half-and-half glue and water, pin it flat, and dry overnight. Re-stiffen the same way if it softens.

**Can I make the dress longer?** Yes — add plain sc rounds between Rounds 15 and 17 before the shell edge; each adds about 1 cm.

**What size is the finished angel?** About 20 cm tall and 12 cm wide across the wings. Chunky yarn with a 4 mm hook makes a 26 cm angel.

**Can I hang the angel on the tree?** Yes — the chain-12 loop on the back of the head takes a thin ribbon or ornament hook.

title: Nutcracker Amigurumi: Free Crochet Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a tall nutcracker soldier amigurumi with a striped red jacket, clean colour changes and a no-sew tall hat.
image_alt: Handmade crochet nutcracker soldier amigurumi in a red jacket with gold trim, black tall hat and a gold yarn sword.
content:
A nutcracker is the soldier every Christmas tree needs: tall, straight, and splendid in a red jacket with gold trim. This crochet nutcracker pattern makes one soldier about 28 cm tall, with a striped jacket, a tall hat that slips on without sewing, and a soft yarn sword.

Each colour change is worked on the last yarn-over, so the join is invisible. The hat is a tall tube that fits snugly over the head, so there is no sewing at all. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this nutcracker.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Joined legs, clean colour changes, back-loop-only trim, and a no-sew hat. **Skill level:** Intermediate. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 28 cm tall, 12 cm wide. **Time:** one weekend, 6 to 7 hours.

Use smooth worsted yarn in red, black, white and gold.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, black, white and gold worsted yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, 10 mm safety eyes, scissors, a yarn needle and polyester stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/nutcracker-amigurumi-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): red 80 g, black 60 g, white 40 g, gold 20 g; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; 10 mm black safety eyes; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 18 single crochet stitches and 20 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work tightly enough that the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

To change colour, work the last stitch of the old colour until two loops remain, then pull the new colour through. The join sits at the back of the body, where it is never seen.

## The Pattern

Work the legs first, then join them into the body; the head continues from the body, so there is no wobbly neck seam.

**Legs (make 2, black):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–10: sc around (18). Stuff lightly; fasten off the first leg only.

**Body (striped jacket):** Round 11 (black): 18 sc around the second leg, then 18 sc around the first leg, joining them into one round (36). Rounds 12–13: sc around in black (36). Round 14 (white): sc around (36). Rounds 15–19 (red): sc around (36). Round 20 (gold): sc in back loop only around (36) — trim ridge. Rounds 21–23 (red): sc around (36). Round 24: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 25: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 26: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 27: (sc, dec) 6 times (12).

**Head (white, continuing the body):** Round 28: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 29: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 30–34: sc around (24). Round 35: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 36: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 37: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Face:** Attach the 10 mm safety eyes between Rounds 31 and 32, 6 stitches apart, before stuffing. Embroider a smile and a white moustache in surface slip stitch, and add three gold French knot buttons down the jacket.

**Hat (black, no-sew):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: sc in back loop only (24) — crown edge. Rounds 6–13: sc around (24). Round 14: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30) — brim flare. Round 15: sc around (30). Round 16 (gold): sc around (30) — hat band. Fasten off. Slip the hat over the head; it fits snugly and needs no sewing.

![Close-up of red, white and gold crochet stripes in single crochet with a clean colour change and a gold back-loop-only trim ridge](https://cozyloops.site/assets/nutcracker-amigurumi-closeup.webp)

**Arms (make 2, red with white cuff):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 3 times (9). Rounds 3–8: sc around in red (9). Rounds 9–10: sc around in white (9). Stuff lightly, flatten the end, and sew the arms to the body at Round 20, angled downward.

**Sword (gold blade, black handle):** Blade: chain 16, sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (15), turn, sc across (15). Handle: chain 6, sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (5), turn, sc across (5). Crossguard: chain 8, sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (7). Sew the handle to the blade and the crossguard between them. The sword is soft crochet with no wire inside, so it is safe for children; sew it to one hand or leave it loose to pose.

**Assembly:** Sew the arms to the body, slip the hat on, and sew the sword into one hand. The joined legs and firm stuffing keep him upright; if he leans, add more stuffing to the legs and press the base flat.

## Styling and Care

Stand him on a mantel or shelf beside the tree, next to the angel and snowman from this set. A pair in different jacket colours looks like a guard of honour. Spot-clean with a damp cloth; do not machine wash, or the hat will lose its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I change colours cleanly?** Finish the last stitch of the old colour with the new colour, pulling it through the final two loops. Keep the join at the back of the body.

**Is the hat sewn on?** No — the hat slips over the head and fits snugly. Add one small stitch at the back if he will be handled a lot.

**How tall is the finished nutcracker?** About 28 cm tall and 12 cm wide. DK yarn with a 3 mm hook makes a 22 cm version.

**Is the sword safe for children?** Yes — the sword is soft crochet with no wire inside and no hard parts.

title: Christmas Gnome Amigurumi with a Brushed Beard
excerpt: Crochet a Christmas gnome amigurumi with a brushed-yarn beard and three hat styles in one pattern — a festive friend for the mantel or tree.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas gnome amigurumi with a red pointed hat, pink nose and long fluffy white brushed beard, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
A Christmas gnome is the easiest festive friend you can crochet: a grey body, a red hat and a long white beard. This pattern makes one gnome about 20 cm tall, with a brushed-yarn beard and three hat styles — one body makes a whole family.

The beard is the clever part: plain acrylic yarn, brushed out with a pet slicker brush until it fluffs into fibres. It takes five minutes. If you can work a single crochet sphere, you can make this gnome.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A graduated body, a brushed acrylic beard and three hat styles. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 20 cm tall, 10 cm wide. **Time:** 3 to 4 hours.

Use smooth worsted yarn in grey, red and green; the white beard yarn must be acrylic — only acrylic brushes out into fibres.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of grey, red, green and white worsted yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, a pet slicker brush, safety eyes, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-gnome-amigurumi-beard-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): grey 60 g, red 40 g, green 20 g, white acrylic 20 g; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; a pet slicker brush.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 18 single crochet stitches and 20 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch: body grey, nose pink, beard white, hat red or green.

**Body (grey):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 7–13: sc around (36). Round 14: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 15: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 16: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 17: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 18: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Nose (pink):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–5: sc around (18). Round 6: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Stuff lightly, fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Beard (white acrylic):** Beard base: chain 14. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (13). Rows 2–7: ch 1, turn, sc across (13). Fasten off. Fringe: cut 25 strands of white acrylic, each 14 cm long. Fold each in half, pull the loop through a stitch along the bottom edge, then pull the ends through and tighten — a lark's head knot. Work 13 knots across the bottom, then 6 up each side.

![Close-up of the fluffy white brushed acrylic beard of a crochet Christmas gnome with a pink nose and a pet slicker brush beside it](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-gnome-amigurumi-beard-closeup.webp)

**Brushing the beard:** Pin the beard flat and brush from the top down in short strokes until the strands separate into soft fibres. Work in small sections, brushing each twice. Never brush wet yarn or back and forth — always brush in one direction. Trim the bottom edge straight when it is fluffy enough.

**Arms (make 2, grey or green):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Rounds 2–6: sc around (6). Stuff lightly, flatten, fasten off. Sew to the body at Round 10, angled slightly forward.

**Hat — three styles (red or green):**

Style A, tall floppy point: Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–7: sc around (24). Round 8: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Rounds 9–11: sc around (18). Round 12: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Rounds 13–16: sc around (12). Round 17: (sc, dec) 4 times (8). Rounds 18–20: sc around (8). Fasten off; add a chain-8 loop at the tip.

Style B, short rounded cap: Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–9: sc around (24). Round 10 (brim): sc in front loop only (24). Round 11: (sc, inc) 12 times (36). Fasten off.

Style C, wide brim: Work Style B through Round 9, then Round 10: (2 sc, inc) 8 times (32). Round 11: sc around (32). Round 12: (3 sc, inc) 8 times (40) — wide brim. Fasten off.

**Assembly:** Sew the nose to the front of the body at Round 12, centred, and the beard base just below it, fringe hanging down. Pull the hat low over the body so it covers the top edge of the beard base — the hat holds the beard in place. Sew the arms to the sides.

## Styling and Care

Stand him on a mantel, or hang him from a branch with a ribbon loop on the hat tip. Three gnomes in different hats and colours look like a little village. Spot-clean; do not machine wash, or the beard will felt and tangle.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I brush the beard without tangling?** Brush in short strokes from the top down, holding the beard flat. Pick knots out with the tip of the brush. Never brush wet yarn, and always brush in one direction.

**Which yarn brushes best?** Smooth, plain acrylic. Avoid cotton, which will not separate, and wool, which felts. Cheap acrylic brushes best.

**Can I make a female gnome?** Yes — replace the beard with two braids: knot strands at the sides of the face, plait them and tie with ribbon. Use the short cap (Style B) and a green or cream body.

**How tall is the finished gnome?** About 20 cm tall and 10 cm wide. Chunky yarn with a 5 mm hook makes a 26 cm gnome; DK yarn with a 3 mm hook makes a mini.

title: Elf Amigurumi with Pointed Hat and Jingle Shoes
excerpt: Crochet an elf amigurumi with a bendable pointed hat and curled-toe shoes with tiny jingle bells — a Christmas character with movement.
image_alt: Handmade crochet elf amigurumi with a bent red pointed hat, green tunic and red curled-toe shoes with gold jingle bells, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
An elf is the Christmas character with movement: a hat that bends, shoes that curl, bells that ring. This pattern makes one elf about 22 cm tall, with a bendable pointed hat and curled-toe shoes with tiny jingle bells.

A chenille stem hides inside the hat tip; slip stitches pull a chain into a spiral for the shoes. Both tricks take minutes. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this elf.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Joined legs, a bendable hat, curled-toe shoes with bells, and pointy ears. **Skill level:** Easy to intermediate. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 22 cm tall, 10 cm wide. **Time:** 4 to 5 hours.

Use smooth DK yarn in green, red and skin-tone. The bells are small gold jingle bells, 8 mm across, with a loop on top for sewing on firmly.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of green, red and skin-tone DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, two small gold jingle bells, safety eyes, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-elf-amigurumi-pointed-hat-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3): green 60 g, red 30 g, skin-tone 30 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; 8 mm black safety eyes; 2 small gold jingle bells (8 mm); polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; one chenille stem (pipe cleaner). Optional: pink embroidery thread for cheeks.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 20 single crochet stitches and 22 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Keep your tension firm so the stuffing does not show.

## The Pattern

Work the legs first, then join them into the body; the head continues from the body.

**Legs (make 2, green):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Rounds 3–6: sc around (12). Stuff lightly; fasten off the first leg only.

**Body (green tunic):** Round 7: 12 sc around each leg, joining them into one round (24). Rounds 8–12: sc around (24). Round 13 (red belt): sc around in red (24). Round 14: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 15: (sc, dec) 6 times (12).

**Head (skin-tone, continuing the body):** Round 16: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 17: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 18: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Rounds 19–23: sc around (30). Round 24: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Round 25: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 26: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 27: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Ears (make 2, skin-tone):** Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 2 times (6). Round 3: (2 sc, inc) 2 times (8). Round 4: sc around (8). Flatten and sew to the head at Round 20, point angled up.

**Arms (make 2, green with skin-tone hands):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (skin-tone). Rounds 2–3: sc around (6). Round 4 (green): sc around (6). Rounds 5–8: sc around (6). Stuff lightly, flatten, and sew to the body at Round 12, angled down.

![Close-up of red crochet elf shoes with curled-up toes tipped with tiny gold jingle bells](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-elf-amigurumi-pointed-hat-closeup.webp)

**Shoes (make 2, red):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–6: sc around (18). Toe curl: chain 8, then work 7 slip stitches back along the chain — the tight stitches pull it into a spiral. Sew the curl to the front of the shoe, pointing up, and sew a jingle bell to the tip. Round 7: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 8: sc around (12). Stuff lightly and sew to the bottom of each leg.

**Hat (red, bendable):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–7: sc around (24). Round 8: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Rounds 9–11: sc around (18). Round 12: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Rounds 13–15: sc around (12). Round 16: (sc, dec) 4 times (8). Rounds 17–18: sc around (8). Fasten off.

**Bending the hat:** Fold a chenille stem in half, twist it, and fold the cut ends back. Tuck it inside the hat tip, bend the tip to one side, and sew the hat to the head, pulled low over the ears.

**Face:** Attach the 8 mm safety eyes between Rounds 20 and 21, 6 stitches apart, before stuffing. Embroider a smile and two pink cheek circles.

**Assembly:** Sew the shoes to the legs, curls up, the ears to the head, the arms to the body, and the hat on top. Firm stuffing keeps him upright; if he leans, add stuffing to the legs and press the base flat.

## Styling and Care

Stand him on a mantel, hang him from the tree with a ribbon loop on the hat tip, or sit him on a shelf edge, legs dangling. He pairs with the gnome, snowman and gingerbread man. Spot-clean; do not machine wash, or the hat will lose its bend and the bells will rust.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I bend the hat point?** Fold a chenille stem in half, twist it, and tuck it inside the hat tip before sewing the hat on. Bend the tip — the stem holds the bend. Fold the cut ends back.

**Are the bells safe for children?** The bells are sewn on with several tight stitches through the bell loop, so they stay put. For children under three, leave them off or embroider them — a French knot in gold yarn reads as a bell and cannot come off.

**Can I make the elf sit?** Yes — stuff the legs lightly, sew them to the front of the body at Round 7 angled forward, and press the base flat. His curled shoes point up.

**How tall is the finished elf?** About 22 cm tall and 10 cm wide. Chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook makes a 28 cm elf.

title: Christmas Pudding Amigurumi Ornament
excerpt: Crochet a Christmas pudding amigurumi ornament with a drip-edge icing top, holly leaves and bobble berries — a festive friend for the tree or a gift tag.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas pudding amigurumi ornament with cream icing, green holly leaves and red bobble berries, with a red ribbon hanging loop, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
A Christmas pudding is the cosiest ornament you can crochet: a round brown pudding, cream icing dripping over the top, and a sprig of holly with three red berries. This pattern makes one pudding about 9 cm tall, with a hanging loop so it doubles as a gift tag tied to a present.

The icing is the clever part: a flat cream circle finished with a wavy drip edge, worked in one round. The holly leaves are two tiny pointed ovals, and the berries are three small bobbles. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this pudding.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A graduated sphere, a drip-edge icing top, pointed holly leaves and bobble berries. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 9 cm tall, 10 cm wide. **Time:** 2 to 3 hours.

Use smooth DK yarn in brown, cream, green and red; the brown should be a rich Christmas-pudding brown, not too dark, so the cream icing shows up against it.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of brown, cream, green and red DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, red ribbon, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-pudding-amigurumi-ornament-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3): brown 40 g, cream 15 g, green 10 g, red 10 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; red ribbon for the hanging loop.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), double crochet (dc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), bobble stitch (yarn over, insert hook, yarn over, pull up a loop, yarn over, pull through 2 loops — repeat 4 more times in the same stitch, yarn over, pull through all 6 loops on the hook). **Gauge:** 20 single crochet stitches and 22 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch: pudding brown, icing cream, leaves green, berries red.

**Pudding (brown):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 7–12: sc around (36). Round 13: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 14: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 15: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 16: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 17: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Icing top (cream):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Round 7 (drip edge): *single crochet in the next stitch, chain 3, slip stitch into the following stitch* — repeat around (18 drips). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Holly leaves (make 2, green):** Chain 7. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook, hdc in next, dc in next 2, hdc in next, sc in last (6). Turn to the other side of the foundation chain: sc, hdc, dc in next 2, hdc, sc (6). Fasten off. Pinch the centre of each leaf to fold it slightly along the middle vein.

**Berries (make 3, red):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: work 1 bobble stitch in each stitch (6 bobbles). Round 3: sc2tog 3 times (3). Fasten off, leaving a tail. Pull the tail through the centre to close the berry.

**Hanging loop:** Cut a 25 cm length of red ribbon. Thread it through the top of the icing, knot the ends together, and trim. For a gift tag, leave the loop long enough to tie a bow around a present.

![Close-up of the cream icing drip edge and green holly leaves with three red bobble berries on a brown crochet Christmas pudding](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-pudding-amigurumi-ornament-closeup.webp)

**Assembly:** Sew the icing circle to the top of the pudding at Round 13, so the drip edge hangs just over the brown. Sew the two holly leaves to the centre of the icing, crossing them slightly, then sew the three berries in a cluster where the leaves meet. Sew the ribbon loop to the top centre of the icing, hidden under the berries.

## Styling and Care

Hang it on the tree with the ribbon loop, or tie it to a present as a gift tag — it is sized to sit on top of a wrapped box without hiding the bow. A set of four in different browns looks like a little pudding family on a mantel garland. Spot-clean; do not machine wash, or the icing edge will lose its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How big is the finished pudding?** About 9 cm tall and 10 cm wide. Chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook makes a 13 cm pudding; DK yarn with a 3 mm hook is the ornament size.

**Can I make a set of four?** Yes — make four puddings in different browns (milk chocolate, dark chocolate, gingerbread, and white chocolate with red berries) and hang them in a row on a garland, or tie one to each present.

**What yarn weight hangs best?** DK holds its shape on a tree branch and is light enough not to pull the branch down. Chunky yarn is too heavy and sags the loop; 4-ply is light but the pudding comes out small.

**How do I attach it to a present?** Tie the ribbon loop in a bow around the present, or thread the loop through a gift-tag hole and knot it. The pudding sits flat on top of the box, so it will not roll off.

title: Candy Cane Amigurumi Doll: Free Crochet Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a candy cane amigurumi doll with jogless red-and-white stripes and a bendable hook — in two sizes, ornament and cuddly doll.
image_alt: Handmade crochet candy cane amigurumi doll with red-and-white stripes, a curved hook and a smiling face, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
A candy cane is the Christmas shape everyone recognises: clean red-and-white stripes, a neat hook at the top, and a smiling face. This pattern makes a candy cane in two sizes — a 15 cm ornament for the tree and a 25 cm cuddly doll for the mantel.

The stripes are the clever part: a jogless colour change worked with one slip stitch, so every stripe line is straight and every join is invisible. A chenille stem hidden inside the tube lets you bend the hook into shape. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this cane.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Jogless stripe changes, a bendable tube, and a striped doll in two sizes. **Skill level:** Easy to intermediate. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** ornament about 15 cm tall; doll about 25 cm tall. **Time:** 3 to 4 hours.

Use smooth worsted yarn in red and white; the red should be a bright post-box red so the stripes read clearly from across the room.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red and white worsted yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, 8 mm safety eyes, a chenille stem, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/candy-cane-amigurumi-doll-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): red 50 g (ornament) or 90 g (doll), white 50 g or 90 g; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; 8 mm black safety eyes; polyester stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; one chenille stem (pipe cleaner). Optional: pink embroidery thread for cheeks.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 18 single crochet stitches and 20 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch. Change colour every 2 rounds: 2 rounds red, 2 rounds white, and so on. To change colour, finish the last stitch of the old colour by pulling the new colour through the final two loops. Then slip stitch into the first stitch of the new round and continue in single crochet — the slip stitch sits behind the stripe line and hides the jog.

**Cane body:** Start in white. Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–21 (ornament) or 4–33 (doll): single crochet around (18), changing colour every 2 rounds. Stuff firmly as you go, a little at a time, so the tube stays even. Round 22 (ornament) or 34 (doll): (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 23 (ornament) or 35 (doll): dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Face:** Attach the 8 mm safety eyes between Rounds 10 and 11 (ornament) or Rounds 14 and 15 (doll), 6 stitches apart, on the straight part of the cane below the hook, before the stuffing is finished. Embroider a smile below the eyes and two pink cheek circles.

**Arms (make 2):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (red). Rounds 2–8: single crochet around (6), changing colour every 2 rounds to match the body stripes. Stuff lightly, flatten, and sew to the body at Round 8 (ornament) or Round 12 (doll), angled slightly down.

**Base (doll size only):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (white). Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Fasten off. Sew to the bottom of the cane so the doll stands on a shelf.

![Close-up of the neat jogless red-and-white stripes and curved hook of a crochet candy cane amigurumi doll](https://cozyloops.site/assets/candy-cane-amigurumi-doll-closeup.webp)

**Bending the cane:** Fold a chenille stem in half, twist it, and fold the cut ends back so no sharp wire shows. Tuck it inside the tube before the final decrease rounds, then bend the top 5 cm of the cane into a hook. The stem holds the bend. If the hook springs back, add a second stem.

**Assembly:** Sew the arms to the sides of the body and the base to the bottom (doll size), then check that the hook holds its curve. Firm stuffing keeps the cane straight; if it leans, add stuffing to the lower half and press the base flat.

## Styling and Care

Hang the ornament on the tree with a ribbon loop on the hook, or stand the doll on the mantel beside the stockings. He pairs with the snowman, the gingerbread man and the Christmas pudding. Spot-clean; do not machine wash, or the stripes will felt and the hook will lose its bend.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I avoid the stripe jog?** Finish the last stitch of the old colour with the new colour, then slip stitch into the first stitch of the new round before continuing. The slip stitch sits behind the stripe line, so the join is invisible from the front.

**Can I bend the cane?** Yes — a folded chenille stem tucked inside the tube before the final rounds lets you bend the top into a hook, and it holds the shape. Fold the cut ends back so no wire pokes through.

**Is it safe as a baby toy?** For children under three, embroider the eyes and smile instead of using safety eyes, leave the chenille stem out and stuff the cane firmly so it holds a gentle curve on its own, and check the sewing regularly.

**How tall is the finished candy cane?** The ornament is about 15 cm tall; the doll is about 25 cm tall. Chunky yarn with a 5 mm hook makes a 32 cm doll.

title: Polar Bear Amigurumi in a Santa Hat
excerpt: Crochet a chunky polar bear amigurumi in soft chenille yarn with a separate Santa hat and stitch-counted safety-eye placement for a perfectly symmetrical face.
image_alt: Handmade crochet polar bear amigurumi in white chenille yarn wearing a red Santa hat with white brim and pom-pom, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
A polar bear in a Santa Hat is the softest Christmas friend you can crochet: a chunky white bear, a red hat and a symmetrical face. This pattern makes one bear about 24 cm tall in cosy chenille yarn.

The face is the clever part: the eyes are placed by counting stitches, not guessing — 14 to the first eye, 8 more to the second. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this bear.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Chenille yarn and stitch-counted eye placement. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 24 cm tall, 14 cm wide. **Time:** 4 to 5 hours.

Use soft white and red chenille yarn; the white should be snowy white, not cream.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of white and red chenille yarn with a 4.5 mm crochet hook, 12 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and polyester stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/polar-bear-amigurumi-santa-hat-materials.webp)

Chenille yarn (#5 bulky): white 120 g, red 40 g; a 4.5 mm crochet hook; 12 mm safety eyes; stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; black embroidery thread.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 12 sc and 14 rounds measure 10 cm with a 4.5 mm hook. Work loosely — chenille splits if you pull it tight.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch: body, head and muzzle white; hat red with a white brim.

**Body (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 7–11: sc around (36). Round 12: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 13: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 14: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 15: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 16: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Head (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 7–11: sc around (36). Round 12: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 13: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 14: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 15: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 16: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Muzzle (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: sc around (18). Round 5: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Stuff lightly and fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Ears (make 2, white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–5: sc around (18). Flatten and fasten off.

**Arms (make 2, white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Rounds 3–7: sc around (12). Stuff lightly, flatten, and fasten off.

**Legs (make 2, white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–6: sc around (18). Stuff firmly, flatten, and fasten off.

**Santa hat (red, with white brim):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–7: sc around (24). Round 8: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Rounds 9–11: sc around (18). Round 12: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Rounds 13–15: sc around (12). Round 16: (sc, dec) 4 times (8). Rounds 17–18: sc around (8). Fasten off.

**Brim (white):** Chain 26, join with a slip stitch, work 3 rounds of sc (26), and sew to the base of the hat.

**Pom-pom (white):** Wrap white chenille around three fingers 30 times, tie the middle, cut the loops, trim into a ball, and sew to the hat tip.

![Close-up of the white chenille face of a crochet polar bear with 12 mm safety eyes placed symmetrically and a black embroidered nose](https://cozyloops.site/assets/polar-bear-amigurumi-santa-hat-closeup.webp)

**Face and assembly:** Attach the 12 mm safety eyes between Rounds 9 and 10 of the head, before stuffing: count 14 stitches from the start marker for the first eye, then 8 more for the second — 14 plus 8 plus 14 is 36, the full round, so the eyes sit exactly symmetrical. Sew the muzzle to the head front at Rounds 10–13, centred under the eyes; embroider a black oval nose and a small upside-down Y mouth. Sew the ears to the head top at Rounds 4–5, the arms to the body sides at Round 9, and the legs to the bottom, flat side down. Sew the head to the body, then pull the hat on low over one ear.

## Styling and Care

Stand him on the mantel in his Santa hat, or take the hat off for a plain polar bear. He pairs with the snowman and the robin. Spot-clean; do not machine wash.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Does chenille yarn shed?** A little, at first. Shake the finished bear outside and brush it once with a soft clothes brush; the loose fibres come off and the shedding stops. Never use a pet slicker brush.

**How do I place the eyes evenly?** Count, do not guess: 14 stitches from the start marker for the first eye, then 8 to the second, on a 36-stitch round. Place them before stuffing.

**Can I use worsted instead?** Yes — worsted with a 3.5 mm hook makes a firmer, smaller bear, about 18 cm tall, with the same counts. Use 10 mm safety eyes.

**How tall is the finished bear?** About 24 cm tall and 14 cm wide in chenille. Chunky yarn with a 5.5 mm hook makes a 30 cm bear; DK with a 3 mm hook makes a 16 cm mini.

title: Red Robin Amigurumi: A Christmas Bird
excerpt: Crochet a red robin amigurumi with a realistic red-breast colour-block panel and wire-free legs that let the bird sit upright on a shelf.
image_alt: Handmade crochet red robin amigurumi bird with a brown body and bright red breast panel, perched on a wooden branch beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
A red robin is the Christmas bird everyone recognises: brown body, bright red breast, cheerful face. This pattern makes one robin about 14 cm tall, with a realistic red-breast panel and sturdy little legs that let it sit upright on a shelf — no wire needed.

The breast is the clever part: a separate flat panel sewn onto the body, so the red blocking is crisp instead of a messy jogged stripe. The legs are short chain-stitch legs, and the flattened base does the balancing. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this robin.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Colour-block panel work and wire-free standing legs. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 14 cm tall, 9 cm wide. **Time:** 3 to 4 hours.

Use smooth DK yarn in brown, red and cream; the red should be a warm brick red, like a real robin's breast.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of brown, red and cream DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, 8 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and polyester stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/red-robin-amigurumi-christmas-bird-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3): brown 40 g, red 15 g, cream 10 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; 8 mm safety eyes; stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; black embroidery thread.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog). **Gauge:** 20 single crochet stitches and 22 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show; if it does, go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch: body and head brown, breast panel red, wings brown, tail brown, beak brown.

**Body (brown):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 7–10: sc around (36). Round 11: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 12: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 13: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 14: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 15: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Head (brown):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Rounds 6–9: sc around (30). Round 10: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Round 11: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 12: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 13: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Breast panel (red):** Chain 7. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (6). Rows 2–4: ch 1, turn, sc across (6). Row 5: ch 1, turn, dec, 2 sc, dec (4). Row 6: ch 1, turn, dec 2 times (2). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Wings (make 2, brown):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–6: sc around (18). Round 7: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Flatten and fasten off.

**Tail (brown):** Chain 9. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (8). Rows 2–6: ch 1, turn, sc across (8). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Beak (brown):** Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 2 times (6). Round 3: sc around (6). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Legs (make 2, brown):** Chain 8. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (7). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

![Close-up of the red breast panel sewn onto the brown body of a crochet robin, with neat stitching around the panel edge](https://cozyloops.site/assets/red-robin-amigurumi-christmas-bird-closeup.webp)

**Face and assembly:** Attach the 8 mm safety eyes between Rounds 6 and 7 of the head, 6 stitches apart, before stuffing. Sew the beak to the front of the head at Round 7, centred between the eyes, and outline it with black embroidery thread. Sew the breast panel to the front of the body, from Round 6 down to Round 12, wide end at the top — use small whip stitches around the edge and pull each stitch snug so the panel lies flat with no gaps. Sew the wings to the body sides at Rounds 7–9, angled slightly back, and the tail to the back at Round 11, pointing down. Sew the head to the body. Sew the legs to the bottom, 4 stitches apart and angled slightly forward, then press the base flat — the flat base and forward legs are what let the bird sit upright with no wire inside.

## Styling and Care
