Sit him on a mantel, a shelf edge or a windowsill, or tie a ribbon loop to his head and hang him on the tree. He pairs with the polar bear, the snowman and the Christmas pudding. Spot-clean; do not machine wash.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I join the breast panel neatly?** Sew it with small whip stitches around the edge, pulling each stitch snug, working from the centre of each side outward so the panel does not bunch. Pin it first, top and bottom.

**Will it stand on a shelf?** Yes — the base is pressed flat and the two legs are sewn 4 stitches apart, angled slightly forward, so the bird balances. If it tips forward, move the legs one stitch further forward; if it tips back, add more stuffing to the lower body.

**What size is it?** 14 cm tall and 9 cm wide. Chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook makes a 19 cm robin; 4-ply with a 2.5 mm hook makes a 10 cm mini.

**Can I hang it on the tree?** Yes — thread 20 cm of ribbon through the top of the head, knot the ends, and hang it from a branch. The robin is light enough for a thin ribbon.

title: Arctic Fox Amigurumi with a Winter Scarf
excerpt: Crochet a two-tone arctic fox amigurumi with a fluffy loop-stitch tail and a matching red scarf — a winter animal with a wearable accessory.
image_alt: Handmade crochet arctic fox amigurumi with a white body, grey-tipped ears, fluffy white tail and red scarf, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
An arctic fox in a winter scarf is the cosiest winter animal you can crochet: a white fox with grey-tipped ears, a fluffy loop-stitch tail and a little red scarf, about 20 cm tall.

The tail is the clever part: loop stitch worked in the round, so it comes out fluffy instead of smooth. The scarf is a simple half-double-crochet rectangle. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this fox.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Two-tone colour work, loop stitch in the round, and a matching scarf. **Skill level:** Easy to intermediate. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 20 cm tall sitting, 12 cm wide; scarf about 40 cm long. **Time:** 4 to 5 hours.

Use smooth DK yarn in white, grey and red; the white should be snowy white, not cream.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of white, grey and red DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, 10 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and polyester stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/arctic-fox-amigurumi-winter-scarf-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3): white 60 g, grey 15 g, red 25 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; 10 mm safety eyes; stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; black embroidery thread.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), loop stitch (insert the hook, wrap the yarn around your index finger, pull the loop through and finish the stitch). **Gauge:** 20 sc and 22 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch: body, head, muzzle, tail and legs white; ear tips grey; scarf red.

**Body (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Rounds 7–11: sc around (36). Round 12: (4 sc, dec) 6 times (30). Round 13: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 14: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 15: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 16: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Head (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Rounds 6–9: sc around (30). Round 10: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Round 11: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 12: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 13: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Muzzle (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–5: sc around (18). Round 6: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Stuff lightly and fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Ears (make 2):** Start in grey. Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 2 times (6). Change to white. Round 3: (2 sc, inc) 2 times (8). Round 4: sc around (8). Round 5: (2 sc, dec) 2 times (6). Flatten and fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Tail (white, loop stitch):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–6: loop stitch around (18), pulling each loop to about 2 cm. Round 7: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 8: loop stitch around (12). Round 9: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off with a sewing tail. Trim the loops even and fluff them with your fingers.

**Legs (make 4, white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Rounds 3–5: sc around (12). Stuff lightly, flatten, and fasten off.

**Scarf (red):** Chain 61. Row 1: hdc in 3rd ch from hook and across (59). Rows 2–3: ch 2, turn, hdc across (59). Fasten off. Fringe: cut 12 strands of red yarn, each 10 cm long, and knot 6 at each end. Trim even.

![Close-up of the fluffy white loop-stitch tail of a crochet arctic fox with a red scarf around its neck](https://cozyloops.site/assets/arctic-fox-amigurumi-winter-scarf-closeup.webp)

**Face and assembly:** Attach the 10 mm safety eyes between Rounds 7 and 8 of the head, 7 stitches apart, before stuffing. Sew the muzzle to the head front at Rounds 9–11 and embroider a small black nose and mouth line. Sew the ears to the head top at Rounds 3–4 and the legs to the bottom of the body, flat side down. Sew the head to the body and the tail to the back at Round 9, pointing up. Tie the scarf around the neck with one loose knot.

## Styling and Care

Sit him on a mantel with his red scarf, or hang him from a branch with a ribbon loop. He pairs with the polar bear, the snowy owl and the snowman. Spot-clean; do not machine wash, or the loop-stitch tail will mat.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I do the loop stitch tail?** Insert the hook, wrap the yarn around your index finger, pull the loop through and finish the stitch. Wrap every loop around the same finger so they match, work with the loops facing you, and trim them even.

**Can I make it in orange as a red fox?** Yes — use orange for the body and head, cream for the muzzle and tail tip, and dark brown ear tips. The same counts work, and a green scarf suits the red fox better than red.

**How long is the scarf?** About 40 cm long with a 10 cm fringe at each end, which fits with one loose knot. For a longer scarf, chain 81 instead of 61; for a shorter one, chain 41.

**How tall is the finished fox?** About 20 cm tall sitting and 12 cm wide, not counting the tail. Chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook makes a 26 cm fox; 4-ply with a 2.5 mm hook makes a 14 cm mini.

title: Snowy Owl Amigurumi Ornament
excerpt: Crochet a snowy owl amigurumi ornament with bobble-stitch feather texture and a hanging loop — a textured ornament rather than a smooth toy.
image_alt: Handmade crochet snowy owl amigurumi ornament with white bobble-stitch feathers, yellow beak and red ribbon hanging loop, beside a small Christmas tree.
content:
A snowy owl is the Christmas bird with texture: white feathers made from bobble stitches, a yellow beak, and a hanging loop so it doubles as a tree ornament. This pattern makes one owl about 13 cm tall, with feather rounds worked in bobbles instead of plain single crochet.

The feathers are the clever part: bobble stitches in alternate rounds, so the body has a soft, raised texture that reads as feathers. The smooth head makes the big eyes stand out. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this owl.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Bobble-stitch feather texture, a separate head, and a hanging loop. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 13 cm tall, 10 cm wide. **Time:** 3 to 4 hours.

Use smooth DK yarn in white, grey and yellow; the white should be snowy white, not cream.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of white, grey and yellow DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, 9 mm safety eyes, red ribbon, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/snowy-owl-amigurumi-ornament-materials.webp)

DK weight yarn (#3): white 50 g, grey 10 g, yellow 10 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; 9 mm safety eyes; stuffing; a tapestry needle; scissors; a stitch marker; red ribbon for the hanging loop; black embroidery thread.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), bobble stitch (yarn over, insert hook, yarn over, pull up a loop, yarn over, pull through 2 loops — repeat 4 more times in the same stitch, yarn over, pull through all 6 loops on the hook). **Gauge:** 20 sc and 22 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch: body and head white, wings white with grey tips, beak and feet yellow.

**Body (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: sc around (30). Round 7 (feather round): (sc, bobble stitch) 15 times (30). Round 8: sc around (30). Round 9 (feather round): (sc, bobble stitch) 15 times (30). Round 10: sc around (30). Round 11: (3 sc, dec) 6 times (24). Stuff firmly. Round 12: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Round 13: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 14: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Head (white):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Rounds 5–7: sc around (24). Round 8: (2 sc, dec) 6 times (18). Stuff firmly. Round 9: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Round 10: dec 6 times (6). Fasten off.

**Wings (make 2):** Start in white. Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–5: sc around (18). Change to grey. Round 6: (sc, dec) 6 times (12). Flatten and fasten off.

**Ear tufts (make 2, white):** Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 2 times (6). Round 3: sc around (6). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Beak (yellow):** Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring. Round 2: (sc, inc) 2 times (6). Round 3: sc around (6). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Feet (make 2, yellow):** Chain 5. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook and across (4). Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Hanging loop:** Cut a 20 cm length of red ribbon. Thread it through the top of the head, knot the ends together, and trim. For a shelf ornament, leave the loop off and press the base flat instead.

![Close-up of the white bobble-stitch feather texture on the body of a crochet snowy owl with a yellow beak](https://cozyloops.site/assets/snowy-owl-amigurumi-ornament-closeup.webp)

**Face and assembly:** Attach the 9 mm safety eyes between Rounds 5 and 6 of the head, 5 stitches apart, before stuffing. Sew the beak to the head front at Round 6, centred between the eyes, and outline each eye with black thread in a small circle. Sew the ear tufts to the head top, the wings to the body sides at Rounds 7–9, and the feet to the bottom, 4 stitches apart. Sew the head to the body, then sew the ribbon loop to the top centre of the head, between the ear tufts.

## Styling and Care

Hang it on the tree with the ribbon loop, or sit it on a mantel — it pairs with the arctic fox, the polar bear and the robin. A pair in different sizes looks like a little owl family. Spot-clean; do not machine wash, or the bobbles will lose their shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I keep the bobbles even?** Work every bobble with five yarn-overs in the same stitch, pull each loop to the same height, and push each finished bobble to the front before the next stitch. Keep your tension even across the feather rounds.

**Can I make a pair in different sizes?** Yes — make one in DK with a 3 mm hook (13 cm) and a second in chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook (18 cm), using the same counts. Use 12 mm eyes on the larger owl so the face stays in proportion.

**Will it hang straight?** Yes, if the loop is sewn exactly at the top centre of the head, between the ear tufts. If it tilts, move the loop one stitch toward the heavy side; light stuffing in the head also helps it balance.

**How big is the finished owl?** About 13 cm tall and 10 cm wide. Chunky yarn with a 4.5 mm hook makes an 18 cm owl; 4-ply with a 2.5 mm hook makes a 10 cm mini ornament.

title: Mini Christmas Stocking Garland: 8 Stockings in an Evening
excerpt: Crochet eight tiny stockings in an evening and string them on twine — a scrap-yarn garland for the tree, mantel or doorway.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas stocking garland with eight tiny red, green and cream stockings strung on twine above a wooden mantel.
content:
Eight tiny stockings on a length of twine is the fastest Christmas garland you can crochet: one evening, a handful of scrap yarn, and a mantel that looks like Christmas morning. Each stocking takes about twenty minutes, and because they are small, every colour change feels like a fresh start instead of a chore.

The clever part is the heel: a few short rows over half the stitches, then you pick up stitches along the sides and carry on in the round, so the stocking turns a proper corner without any seaming. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make this garland.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A short-row heel in miniature, a ribbed cuff, and stringing a garland. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** each stocking about 12 cm tall and 5 cm wide; garland about 180 cm long. **Time:** 20 to 25 minutes per stocking, about 3 hours for the whole garland.

Use worsted scraps in red, green and cream; a stocking takes so little yarn that oddments from other projects are enough.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, green and cream worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, jute twine, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-christmas-stocking-garland-crochet-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in red, green and cream: about 15 g per stocking, 120 g in total; a 4 mm crochet hook; 2 m of jute twine, 2 to 3 mm thick; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), decrease (dec: sc2tog), back loop only (BLO: work into the back loop of the stitch only). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rounds measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Work the cuff loosely so it stretches; work the leg and foot firmly so the stocking keeps its shape on the twine.

## The Pattern

Work one stocking at a time, then string all eight together. The colour plan below makes two of each combination, so the garland alternates neatly: 2 red body with a cream cuff, 2 green body with a cream cuff, 2 cream body with a red cuff, 2 red body with a green cuff. Work the cuff in the cuff colour and the rest in the body colour.

**Cuff:** Chain 18. Row 1: hdc in 3rd ch from hook and across (16). Rows 2–6: ch 2, turn, hdc in back loop only across (16). Fold the cuff in half with the right side out and slip stitch the short edges together to make a tube. Turn it so the seam sits at the back.

**Leg:** Join the body colour at the cuff seam. Rounds 1–5: sc around (16).

**Heel:** Work in rows over the next 8 stitches. Row 1: ch 1, sc in next 8 sts (8), turn. Row 2: ch 1, sc across (8), turn. Row 3: ch 1, sc 5, dec, turn (6). Row 4: ch 1, sc 4, dec, turn (5). Row 5: ch 1, sc 3, dec, turn (4). The heel bottom is 4 stitches wide.

![Close-up of a tiny handmade crochet Christmas stocking in red yarn with a cream ribbed cuff, showing single crochet stitches and the shaped heel](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-christmas-stocking-garland-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Foot:** Round 1: sc across the 4 heel stitches, pick up and sc 3 stitches along the heel side, sc across the 8 instep stitches, pick up and sc 3 stitches along the other heel side (18). Round 2: (7 sc, dec) twice (16). Rounds 3–7: sc around (16).

**Toe:** Round 8: (2 sc, dec) 4 times (12). Round 9: (sc, dec) 4 times (8). Round 10: dec 4 times (4). Fasten off and weave the yarn through the last 4 stitches to close the toe.

**Hanging loop:** Chain 12, slip stitch to the back of the cuff at the seam, and fasten off. Repeat for all 8 stockings, following the colour plan.

**Stringing:** Cut 2 m of twine. Tie a small loop knot 15 cm from one end for hanging. Tie each stocking to the twine by its hanging loop with a small knot, spacing the stockings 20 cm apart: the first at 15 cm, then every 20 cm, the last at 155 cm. Leave the remaining twine for the second hanging loop. Alternate the colours along the twine so no two neighbours match.

## Styling and Care

Hang the garland across a mantel, a doorway or the front of a bookshelf, and let it sag a little in the middle so the stockings sit at slightly different heights. It pairs with the granny-stripe tree skirt below the tree. Tuck a tiny treat or a rolled-up note into each stocking on Christmas Eve. Hand wash and dry flat; the twine will soften a little with use.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does one stocking take?** About 20 to 25 minutes once you have made the first one. The whole garland takes one evening, about 3 hours including stringing.

**What twine holds the weight?** Jute twine 2 to 3 mm thick. Eight small stockings weigh almost nothing, and a knot through each hanging loop stops the stockings sliding along the twine. If you fill the stockings with treats, use 3 mm twine.

**Can I number them for Advent?** Yes — embroider the numbers 1 to 8 on the cuffs for an eight-day countdown to Christmas. For a full 24-day Advent, make the garland three times and hang the three garlands side by side.

**Can I make them smaller or bigger?** Yes — DK yarn with a 3.5 mm hook makes a stocking about 10 cm tall, and chunky yarn with a 5 mm hook makes one about 15 cm tall. Use the same counts and check the first stocking against a ruler before making the rest.

title: Crochet Christmas Tree Skirt with Granny Stripes
excerpt: Crochet a flat-square Christmas tree skirt with granny stripes in three sizes, with a slit that slides around the trunk without lifting the tree.
image_alt: Handmade square crochet Christmas tree skirt with red, cream and green granny stripes lying flat around the base of a decorated Christmas tree.
content:
A tree skirt is the fame under the tree: it hides the stand, catches the needles, and gives the presents somewhere to sit. This one is a flat square built outward from a small centre opening, in granny stripes of red, cream and green, with a slit down one side so it slides around the trunk without anyone lifting the tree.

The clever part is the switch from rounds to rows: the centre is worked in the round as a small granny square, then you turn at the slit and work back and forth, so the opening runs from the centre hole all the way to the outer edge. If you can work a granny cluster, you can make this skirt.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A granny square worked in the round, switching to rows for a slit, a two-row stripe sequence, and sizing a flat square. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** tabletop 60 cm square, medium 90 cm square, full 120 cm square. **Time:** tabletop 4 to 5 hours, medium 7 to 8 hours, full 10 to 12 hours.

Choose your size before you start: measure the widest spread of the lowest branches and pick the skirt that reaches a little past them.

## Materials and Tools

![Large balls of red, cream and green worsted yarn with a 5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a yarn needle and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-christmas-tree-skirt-granny-stripes-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in red, cream and green: tabletop about 300 g, medium about 550 g, full about 800 g, roughly a third of each colour; a 5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker; a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc), granny cluster (3 dc worked into one chain space). **Gauge:** 12 dc and 6 rows measure 10 cm with a 5 mm hook. Work loosely — granny fabric should drape and lie flat, not stiffen into a board.

## The Pattern

**Stripe sequence:** Work 2 rows in each colour, repeating red, cream, green. Rounds 1–2 are red, Round 3 and Row 4 are cream, Rows 5–6 are green, Rows 7–8 are red, and so on. Change colour at the end of a row and carry the new colour up the slit edge.

**Centre (worked in the round):** Round 1: ch 4, join with a sl st to form a ring. Ch 3 (counts as dc), 2 dc in the ring, ch 2, (3 dc in the ring, ch 2) 3 times, join with a sl st to the top of the ch-3 (12 dc, 4 corner spaces). Round 2: sl st into the first corner space, ch 3, (2 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in the same corner space, 3 dc in the next side space, (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in the next corner space, and so on around — 2 groups per side. Round 3: work the same way, 3 groups per side. The centre square measures about 20 cm across, with a centre hole about 5 cm wide.

**Slit rows:** From Row 4, work in rows and turn at the slit — do not join the round. Each row: ch 3 (counts as dc), work 3 dc in each chain space along the side, (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in each corner space, and 3 dc in the last space before the slit; turn. Each row adds one group per side and about 5 cm to the total width.

**Rows per size:** Tabletop 60 cm: work Rows 4–11 (8 rows). Medium 90 cm: work Rows 4–17 (14 rows). Full 120 cm: work Rows 4–23 (20 rows). Lay the skirt flat and measure across the middle after every 3 rows, so you can stop early or add a row if your tension runs loose or tight.

![Close-up of granny cluster crochet stitches in red, cream and green stripes on a handmade Christmas tree skirt](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-christmas-tree-skirt-granny-stripes-closeup.webp)

**Ties:** At each slit edge, join red yarn and chain 40, then fasten off. Make one tie on each side of the slit. Tie the two ties in a bow around the trunk.

**Edging:** Join cream at a slit edge and work 1 row of sc evenly around the outer edge and along both slit edges. Fasten off and weave in all ends.

## Styling and Care

Slide the slit around the trunk, tie the bow loosely, and smooth the skirt flat so the stripes run straight. It pairs with the mini stocking garland above the mantel. Fold the skirt in quarters for storage, and it will lie flat again next year. Hand wash in cold water and dry flat; machine wash only on a gentle cycle if the yarn label allows it, in a laundry bag, and always dry flat so the square keeps its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I keep it lying flat?** Work loosely and check after every 3 rows. If the edges ruffle, go down half a hook size; if the centre cups upward, go up half a hook size. Pin the finished skirt damp and dry it flat.

**Which size fits my tree?** Measure the widest spread of the lowest branches. Tabletop 60 cm suits trees up to about 90 cm tall; medium 90 cm suits trees of 120 to 150 cm; full 120 cm suits trees of 180 cm and taller.

**Can I wash it?** Yes — hand wash in cold water and dry flat. Machine wash only on a gentle cycle if the yarn label allows it, in a laundry bag, and always dry flat so the square keeps its shape.

**What if my tree trunk is thicker than the centre hole?** The centre hole is only about 5 cm because the slit does the work: it opens from the hole to the outer edge, so the skirt wraps around any trunk. Tie the two ties loosely in a bow and let the skirt sit flat.

title: Star Garland for the Mantel: Free Crochet Pattern
excerpt: Crochet five-pointed stars with wooden bead centres and string them on twine — a gold and cream garland that drapes evenly across the mantel.
image_alt: Handmade crochet star garland with gold and cream five-pointed stars with wooden bead centres strung on twine across a wooden mantel.
content:
Five gold and cream stars on a length of twine is the simplest mantel garland you can crochet: no sewing, no fiddly joins, just seven stars and a piece of string. Each star is worked in the round from the centre out, so the points grow evenly, and a wooden bead sewn into the middle gives every star the same finished look.

The clever part is the spacing: stars strung 20 cm apart with a 15 cm tail at each end, so the garland drapes in a gentle curve instead of sagging or bunching. If you can work double crochet in the round, you can make this garland.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A five-point star worked in the round, a pointed edging, and stringing a garland with measured spacing. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** each star about 12 cm from point to point; garland about 150 cm long with 7 stars. **Time:** about 30 minutes per star, about 4 hours for the whole garland.

Use worsted yarn in gold and cream; one ball of each colour is enough for the whole garland.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of gold and cream worsted yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, wooden beads, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-star-garland-mantel-pattern-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in gold and cream: about 50 g gold and 40 g cream; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; 7 wooden beads, 12 mm; 2 m of jute twine, 2 mm thick; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Gauge:** 18 dc and 10 rows measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work the star rounds firmly so the points hold their shape; work the edging round loosely so it does not pull the points inward.

## The Pattern

Work one star at a time. Make 4 stars in gold and 3 stars in cream, so the colours alternate along the garland with gold at both ends.

**Round 1:** Chain 3 (counts as dc), work 9 dc in a magic ring, join with a slip stitch to the top of the chain-3 (10 dc).

**Round 2:** Chain 1, sc in the same stitch, *chain 3, skip 1 dc, sc in the next dc* four more times, chain 3, join to the first sc (5 sc and 5 chain-3 spaces).

**Round 3 (the points):** Slip stitch into the first chain-3 space, chain 3 (counts as dc), work (2 dc, chain 2, 3 dc) in the same space — the first point. Work (3 dc, chain 2, 3 dc) in each of the other 4 spaces, join to the top of the chain-3 (5 points, each 6 dc with a chain-2 tip).

**Round 4 (edging):** Chain 1, *sc in each of the next 3 dc, (sc, chain 2, sc) in the chain-2 tip space, sc in each of the next 3 dc* — repeat around all 5 points, join with a slip stitch to the first sc (40 sc and 5 chain-2 tip spaces). Fasten off and weave in the ends.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet five-pointed star in gold yarn with a wooden bead at its centre, showing double crochet points and chain spaces](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-star-garland-mantel-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Bead centre:** Sew one wooden bead to the centre front of each star, passing through the bead hole three or four times and knotting on the back, so the bead sits flat and does not wobble.

**Stringing:** Cut 2 m of twine. Tie a small loop knot 15 cm from one end for hanging. Thread the twine through the chain-2 tip of the top point of the first star and knot it behind the star so it cannot slide. Tie the rest the same way, 20 cm apart: the first at 15 cm, then 35, 55, 75, 95, 115 and 135 cm, leaving 15 cm at the far end for the second hanging loop. Alternate gold and cream so no two neighbours match.

## Styling and Care

Hang it across the mantel and let it sag a little in the middle so the stars sit at different heights. It pairs with the pinecone stitch table runner and the mini stocking garland. Keep it away from open flames and hot candles. Hand wash the stars in cool water and dry flat; unstring them first so the twine does not tangle.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I make the points sharp?** The (sc, chain 2, sc) in each tip in Round 4 pulls the two sides of the point into a corner. Then pin each point out on a towel and hold a steam iron above the work — never press the iron flat onto the yarn. The points stay sharp once the star cools.

**What beads are safe?** Use untreated natural wooden beads, 12 mm, with a hole wide enough for a yarn needle. Avoid painted or varnished beads: the finish can flake and may soften near fireplace heat. Above a working fire, keep the garland at least 30 cm above the mantel shelf.

**How long should the garland be?** This pattern makes a 150 cm garland with 7 stars, fitting a standard mantel of about 120 cm with a little drape at each end. Measure your mantel and add 30 cm: that is the twine length. Space the stars with (length minus 30) divided by (stars minus 1) — for 7 stars on 150 cm, that is 20 cm between stars.

**Why do my stars curl?** The points curl when Round 3 is worked too tightly. Go up half a hook size for Round 3 only, and work Round 4 loosely. If a finished star still curls, block it: pin it flat, points out, spray with water, and dry overnight. A star that curls after blocking was worked too tightly in Round 1 — remake it with a looser magic ring.

title: Pinecone Stitch Christmas Table Runner
excerpt: Crochet a lacy pinecone stitch table runner with a written stitch diagram and a blocking guide — the Christmas centrepiece for the dining table.
image_alt: Handmade crochet pinecone stitch table runner in ecru cotton lace laid on a wooden Christmas dining table with candles and pine branches.
content:
A table runner is the frame of the Christmas table: it sets the line down the middle, gives the candles somewhere to sit, and dresses an ordinary table. This one is worked in pinecone stitch, the old shell stitch that fans out like the scales of a pinecone, in ecru cotton.

The whole runner is just two rows repeated: a shell row and a mesh row. Once you have worked the first repeat, the rest is rhythm, and the stitch diagram below is written out in words so you can follow it row by row. If you can work double crochet, you can make this runner.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Pinecone (pineapple) shell stitch, a two-row mesh repeat, and blocking lace. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 100 cm long and 33 cm wide. **Time:** 8 to 10 hours.

Use ecru or deep-green cotton DK yarn; the stitch shows best in a solid, light colour.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of ecru cotton DK yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/pinecone-stitch-christmas-table-runner-materials.webp)

Cotton DK yarn (#3) in ecru: about 300 g, six 50 g balls; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure; rust-proof pins and a blocking mat.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Pinecone stitch:** 3 dc, chain 2, 3 dc, all in the same stitch or space — the shell fans out like the scales of a pinecone. **Gauge:** 20 dc and 10 rows measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work loosely: lace needs air, and a tight runner will not drape.

**Reading the chart in words:** the runner is a grid of 9 shells across. A shell row reads: 2 dc at the edge, then (shell, 2 dc) nine times. A mesh row reads: chain 5, then (dc in the next shell space, chain 2) nine times, then dc in the last stitch. The shell row works its shells into the first nine chain spaces; the tenth stays open at the edge so the sides stay straight.

## The Pattern

**Foundation:** Chain 68. Row 1: dc in the 4th chain from the hook and in each chain across (65 dc). Turn.

**Row 2 (shell row):** Chain 3 (counts as dc), dc in the next dc, *skip 2 dc, pinecone stitch in the next dc, skip 2 dc, dc in the next 2 dc* — repeat eight more times, so the row holds 9 shells and 20 dc. Turn.

**Row 3 (mesh row):** Chain 5 (counts as dc and chain 2), *dc in the chain-2 space of the next shell, chain 2* — nine times, dc in the last dc (11 dc and 10 chain-2 spaces). Turn.

**Row 4 (shell row):** Chain 3 (counts as dc), pinecone stitch in the first chain-2 space, *dc in the next dc, pinecone stitch in the next chain-2 space* — eight more times, dc in the next 2 dc. Work the shells into the first nine chain spaces only; leave the tenth open at the edge. The row holds 9 shells and 11 dc. Turn.

Repeat Rows 3 and 4 until the runner measures 100 cm from the foundation edge, about 100 rows. End on a mesh row so both ends match.

![Close-up of pinecone stitch crochet lace in ecru cotton yarn, showing the textured shell clusters and chain spaces](https://cozyloops.site/assets/pinecone-stitch-christmas-table-runner-closeup.webp)

**Edging:** Join the yarn at a corner. Chain 1, work sc evenly around the whole runner — about 1 sc per row end along the long sides and 1 sc per stitch along the short ends — with (sc, chain 2, sc) in each corner. Join to the first sc and fasten off. Weave in all ends.

**Blocking:** Lay the runner on a towel or blocking mat and pin it out to 100 cm by 33 cm, pulling the edge straight and pinning each point of the edging. Spray it with water until damp all through, then leave it flat for 24 hours until completely dry. Do not unpin it early: the lace sets its shape as it dries, and an unpinned runner will spring back narrower.

## Styling and Care

Lay it down the centre of the table with the same amount hanging over each end, and set the candles on it — never a bare flame directly on cotton. Hand wash in cool water, dry flat, then block it again lightly so the lace keeps its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is pinecone stitch hard for beginners?** No — the shell is just 6 double crochets and a chain in one space, and the runner is two rows repeated. The only new skill is counting: check after every shell row that you have 9 shells, and after every mesh row that you have 11 double crochets. If the count is wrong, undo one row, not ten.

**How do I block a runner?** Pin it out to 100 cm by 33 cm on a towel or blocking mat, pulling the edge straight and pinning each scallop point. Spray until damp and leave flat for 24 hours. Blocking turns a wavy strip of lace into a flat runner — do not skip it, and do not unpin it before it is fully dry.

**What size table does it fit?** The finished runner is 100 cm long and 33 cm wide, fitting a dining table of 120 to 160 cm with about 10 to 30 cm hanging over each end. For a longer table, keep working the two-row repeat until the runner is 20 cm shorter than the table. For a shorter table, stop the repeat earlier.

**Can I make it wider or narrower?** Yes — the width is set by the foundation chain. Each extra shell repeat adds 7 stitches, about 3.5 cm: chain 7 more and work one more shell in Row 2, and the mesh rows follow the same counts. To narrow it, chain 7 fewer and work one shell less. Keep the total a multiple of 7 plus 2, so the shell row still starts and ends with 2 double crochets.

title: Crochet Christmas Wreath with Poinsettias
excerpt: Crochet a Christmas wreath on a foam ring wrapped in green yarn, with three-dimensional poinsettia flowers, leaves and a gold bow — a door wreath that survives the whole season.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas wreath with red poinsettia flowers, green leaves and a gold bow on a front door.
content:
A crochet wreath on the front door says Christmas before anyone knocks: a green ring, three red poinsettias, leaves and a gold bow. It is built on a foam ring wrapped in single crochet, so it holds its shape all season and comes apart again in January.

The flowers are the clever part: two layers of petals, a small gold centre, and pointed leaves tucked behind each flower.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Wrapping a foam ring in single crochet, two-layer petal flowers, pointed leaves, and a pinch bow. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 32 cm across. **Time:** about 5 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of green, red and gold worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, a 30 cm foam ring, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-christmas-wreath-poinsettia-pattern-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in green, red and gold: green about 150 g, red 60 g, gold 20 g; a 4 mm crochet hook; a 30 cm foam ring; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker; pins for positioning the flowers.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), double crochet (dc). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Gauge is not critical — the ring sets the size — but work the flowers firmly so the petals hold their shape.

## The Pattern

**Wrap the ring (green):** Join the green yarn to the foam ring with a slip stitch around the ring. Work single crochet around the ring, passing the hook under the foam each time: insert the hook under the ring, yarn over, pull a loop through, yarn over, pull through both loops. Work about 140 sc around the full ring, pushing the stitches close together so no foam shows. Join with a slip stitch and fasten off. If foam still shows, work a second pass of sc into the gaps.

**Poinsettia (make 3, red):** Round 1: 5 sc in a magic ring (5). Join with a slip stitch to the first sc.

Round 2 (inner petals): *slip stitch in the next sc, chain 2, 3 dc in the same sc, chain 2, slip stitch in the same sc* — repeat in each of the 5 sc, so the round holds 5 small petals. Join with a slip stitch and do not fasten off.

Round 3 (outer petals): work behind the inner petals, into the back loop of each Round 1 sc: *slip stitch in the back loop of the next sc, chain 3, 4 dc in the same back loop, chain 3, slip stitch in the same back loop* — repeat in each of the 5 back loops, so the round holds 5 larger petals behind the first layer. Fasten off and weave in the ends.

**Flower centre (make 3, gold):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Round 2: increase around (12). Round 3: sc around (12). Fasten off with a sewing tail. Sew one centre to the middle of each flower with the tail.

**Leaf (make 6, green):** Chain 9. Row 1: slip stitch in the 2nd chain from the hook, sc in the next 2 chains, hdc in the next 2 chains, dc in the next 2 chains, (dc, chain 2, dc) in the last chain; then work down the other side of the foundation chain: dc in the next 2 chains, hdc in the next 2 chains, sc in the next 2 chains, slip stitch in the last chain. Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Bow (gold):** Chain 10. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (9). Rows 2–5: chain 1, turn, sc across (9). Fasten off. Pinch the rectangle in the middle and wrap gold yarn around it 6 times, knot at the back, and trim the ends to make two tails.

**Hanging loop:** Chain 30, slip stitch to the top of the wrapped ring, and fasten off.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet poinsettia flower in red yarn with a gold centre and green leaves, showing the layered double crochet petals](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-christmas-wreath-poinsettia-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Assembly:** Pin the flowers on first: one at the top centre, one lower left, one lower right. Tuck two leaves behind each flower, points outward, and pin them. Sew each flower to the ring with 3 or 4 stitches through the back of the flower and around the wrap. Sew the leaves the same way, one stitch at the base of each leaf. Sew the bow at the bottom centre of the ring. Hang it from the loop at the top, behind the top flower.

## Styling and Care

Hang it on a sheltered front door or an inside wall, bow at the bottom, top flower centred. It pairs with the bobble Christmas trees on the mantel. Keep it out of direct rain and strong sun. Spot-clean with a damp cloth; do not machine wash. Store it flat in a box with tissue paper between the flowers.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Will it survive outdoors?** On a covered porch, yes — worsted yarn and a foam ring cope with cold and a little damp. In heavy rain the foam soaks through, so bring it inside in a storm. Strong sun fades the red, so a shaded door is best.

**How do I attach the flowers?** Sew them, do not glue them. Use a yarn needle and the tails left on each flower and leaf, and take 3 or 4 stitches through the back of the flower and around the wrap. Pin everything in place first and check the spacing before you sew.

**Can I reuse the ring next year?** Yes — snip the wrap at the join, unwind the green yarn, and the foam ring comes out undamaged. Store the flowers flat and make a fresh wrap next year, in any colour. The same ring works for a spring wreath too.

**What if foam still shows through the wrap?** Push the stitches closer together as you work. If a gap is left, work a second round of single crochet into the spaces between the first round's stitches.

title: Bobble Christmas Trees, Set of 3
excerpt: Crochet three bobble-stitch Christmas trees in one pattern — 12, 18 and 24 cm tall — with bobble texture as the decoration and a star topper on each.
image_alt: Three handmade crochet Christmas trees in green with bobble stitch texture and cream star toppers, standing on a wooden mantel.
content:
Three little Christmas trees in a row are better than one: small, medium and tall, all in the same pattern, with bobble stitch decoration. The bobbles run all the way around each cone, and the trees share the first fourteen rounds — the medium adds two more, the tall two more again.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Bobble stitch, cone shaping by increasing in the round, and sizing one pattern three ways. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** small tree about 12 cm tall, medium about 18 cm, large about 24 cm, not counting the star. **Time:** about 2 hours for the small tree, 3 for the medium, 4 for the large.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of green and cream worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors, a yarn needle and polyester stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/bobble-christmas-trees-set-of-three-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in green and cream: green about 200 g (small 40 g, medium 60 g, large 100 g), cream 30 g; a 4 mm crochet hook; stuffing; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker; dried beans or rice for weight (optional).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), bobble stitch (yarn over, insert hook, yarn over, pull up a loop, yarn over, pull through 2 loops — repeat 4 more times in the same stitch, yarn over, pull through all 6 loops on the hook). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rounds measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Work tightly so the stuffing does not show.

## The Pattern

Work in a spiral, marking the first stitch. On bobble rounds, push each bobble to the front before the next stitch.

**Small tree (12 cm, green):** Round 1: 4 sc in a magic ring (4). Round 2: inc around (8). Round 3: (sc, inc) 4 times (12). Round 4 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 6 times (12). Round 6: (2 sc, inc) 4 times (16). Round 7 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 8 times (16). Round 9: (3 sc, inc) 4 times (20). Round 10 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 10 times (20). Round 12: (4 sc, inc) 4 times (24). Round 13 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 12 times (24). Rounds 5, 8, 11 and 14: sc around. Fasten off.

**Small tree base (green):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Round 4: (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24). Fasten off with a sewing tail. Stuff the tree firmly, then sew the base to Round 14 with the tail.

**Medium tree (18 cm, green):** Work Rounds 1–14 exactly as the small tree, then continue. Round 15: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 16 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 15 times (30). Round 18: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Round 19 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 18 times (36). Rounds 17 and 20: sc around. Fasten off.

**Medium tree base (green):** Work Rounds 1–4 as the small tree base, then Round 5: (3 sc, inc) 6 times (30). Round 6: (4 sc, inc) 6 times (36). Fasten off with a sewing tail. Stuff the tree firmly, then sew the base to Round 20.

**Large tree (24 cm, green):** Work Rounds 1–20 exactly as the medium tree, then continue. Round 21: (5 sc, inc) 6 times (42). Round 22 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 21 times (42). Round 24: (6 sc, inc) 6 times (48). Round 25 (bobble): (bobble, sc) 24 times (48). Rounds 23 and 26: sc around. Fasten off.

**Large tree base (green):** Work Rounds 1–6 as the medium tree base, then Round 7: (5 sc, inc) 6 times (42). Round 8: (6 sc, inc) 6 times (48). Fasten off with a sewing tail. Stuff the tree firmly, then sew the base to Round 26.

**Star topper (make 3, cream):** Round 1: 5 sc in a magic ring (5). Round 2: (slip stitch, chain 2, dc, chain 2, slip stitch) in each sc — 5 points. Fasten off with a sewing tail. Sew one star to the top of each tree with the tail.

**Trunk (make 3, cream):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Rounds 2–3: sc around (6). Fasten off with a sewing tail. Sew one trunk to the centre of each base before you sew the base to the tree.

![Close-up of bobble stitch texture on a green crochet Christmas tree, showing the raised bobbles in neat rows around the cone](https://cozyloops.site/assets/bobble-christmas-trees-set-of-three-closeup.webp)

**Weighting the trees:** Pack the stuffing firmly into the lower rounds and keep the top light. For extra weight, drop a small pouch of dried beans or rice inside the base. The trees should sit flat with no wobble.

## Styling and Care

Stand the three trees in a row on the mantel, tallest in the middle. They pair with the Christmas wreath on the door. Spot-clean with a damp cloth; do not machine wash. Store them upright in a box.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I make the bobbles pop?** Push each bobble to the front of the work before you make the next stitch, and keep your tension even — a bobble worked too tightly sinks back into the cone. If a finished bobble still sits flat, pull it forward from the front with the tip of your hook.

**Can I add lights?** Yes — battery-operated LED fairy lights only, never mains-powered lights or real candles. Wrap a short strand around the large tree and tuck the battery pack under the base. LEDs stay cool, so the yarn is safe.

**What stuffing keeps them upright?** Firm polyester stuffing, packed tightly into the lower rounds, with a flat base sewn on evenly. If a tree still leans, add more stuffing to the lower half and re-sew the base. A pouch of dried beans or rice inside the base adds weight at the bottom.

**Can I make a tree taller?** Yes — after any bobble round, add one increase round and one more bobble round: each pair adds about 6 cm. Grow the base circle to match the final round count, or the tree will not sit flat.

title: Scalloped Christmas Coasters: 30-Minute Crochet Gift
excerpt: Crochet a set of scalloped Christmas coasters in washable cotton — 30 minutes each, with a fanned scallop edge in a contrast colour.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas coasters in red, green and cream cotton yarn with scalloped edges, stacked on a wooden coffee table.
content:
A coaster is the smallest Christmas gift you can crochet: one evening, a few balls of cotton, and a set of six that looks shop-bought. Each coaster takes about thirty minutes, and because it is small, a colour change feels like a fresh start instead of a chore. Make a set of four for a stocking filler, or six for the Christmas table.

The clever part is the edge: a round of scallops in a contrast colour, five double crochets fanned into one stitch, so a plain circle turns into something that looks finished. If you can work single crochet in the round, you can make these coasters.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A flat circle worked in joined rounds, even increases, and a scallop edging. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** each coaster about 10 cm across. **Time:** about 30 minutes per coaster, about 3 hours for a set of six.

Use washable cotton worsted in red, green and cream; cotton is the point here, because it soaks up condensation instead of letting it pool.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, green and cream cotton worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/scalloped-christmas-coasters-crochet-materials.webp)

Cotton worsted yarn (#4) in red, green and cream: about 15 g per coaster, 90 g for a set of six; a 4 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), double crochet (dc). **Scallop:** 5 dc worked into one stitch. **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rounds measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Work firmly so the coaster lies flat and does not stretch under a mug.

## The Pattern

Work in joined rounds: chain 1 at the start of each round (it does not count as a stitch) and join with a slip stitch at the end of each round. Work one coaster at a time.

**Round 1:** 8 sc in a magic ring, join (8).

**Round 2:** Chain 1, 2 sc in each sc around, join (16).

**Round 3:** Chain 1, (sc, inc) 8 times, join (24).

**Round 4:** Chain 1, (2 sc, inc) 8 times, join (32).

**Round 5:** Chain 1, (3 sc, inc) 8 times, join (40).

**Round 6:** Chain 1, (4 sc, inc) 8 times, join (48).

**Round 7:** Chain 1, sc around, join (48).

**Round 8 (scallop edging):** Join the contrast colour with a slip stitch. Chain 1, *(skip 1 sc, 5 dc in the next sc, skip 1 sc, slip stitch in the next sc)* — repeat 12 times around, join with a slip stitch to the first slip stitch. The round holds 12 scallops. Fasten off and weave in the ends.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet Christmas coaster in red cotton yarn with a cream scallop edging, showing single crochet stitches and the fanned double crochet scallops](https://cozyloops.site/assets/scalloped-christmas-coasters-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Colour plan for a set of six:** make 2 red coasters with a cream edge, 2 green coasters with a cream edge, and 2 cream coasters with a red edge, so the set alternates on the table. For a set of four, make one of each colour combination plus one extra red.

**Making a set:** work all the coaster bodies first, then do all the scallop rounds in one go — changing colour once per coaster is faster than changing it six times. Stack the finished coasters and tie them with a ribbon for a gift.

## Styling and Care

Set them on the coffee table with the scallops showing, or stack them beside the teapot. They pair with the Christmas placemats with a holly motif on the dining table. Hand wash or machine wash cold on a gentle cycle, and dry flat so the circle keeps its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Will cotton coasters absorb spills?** Yes — that is why they are cotton. Cotton soaks up condensation and drips instead of letting them pool on the table. Wring a wet coaster out and lay it flat to dry. Acrylic will not absorb the same way, and it can soften near a very hot mug.

**How do I wash them?** Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle, or hand wash in cool water. Dry flat; a tumble dryer on low is fine, but the coaster may shrink a little on the first wash, so pin it back to 10 cm across while it is still damp.

**Can I make a matching placemat?** Yes — use the same increase pattern and keep going. Work out to 13 rounds (96 stitches, about 20 cm across) for a small mat, or to 16 rounds (120 stitches, about 25 cm across) for a full placemat, then finish with the same scallop edging in a contrast colour. The counts are the same: each increase round adds 8 stitches.

**Why does my coaster curl up at the edge?** The scallop round pulls the edge inward if it is worked too tightly. Work the 5 double crochets loosely, or go up half a hook size for Round 8 only. If a finished coaster still curls, block it: pin it flat, spray with water, and dry overnight.

title: Christmas Placemats with a Holly Motif
excerpt: Crochet Christmas placemats with a holly motif in filet crochet — the chart written out row by row, no chart reading needed, in washable cotton.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas placemat in cream cotton with a green holly sprig and red berries in filet crochet, laid on a wooden dining table.
content:
A placemat is the frame of a place setting: it marks where the plate goes, catches the crumbs, and gives the Christmas table its colour. This one is worked in filet crochet — a grid of open meshes with a holly sprig drawn in filled blocks — in washable cotton, so it survives the washing machine after Christmas dinner.

The clever part is that there is no chart to read: the holly is written out row by row below, so you follow it like a recipe. If you can work double crochet and chains, you can make this placemat.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Filet crochet mesh, filled blocks, reading a chart written as text, and a two-colour border. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 40 cm wide and 25 cm tall. **Time:** about 4 to 5 hours per placemat.

Use cotton DK in cream, green and red; the motif shows in the lace, and the green and red pick out the holly.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream, green and red cotton DK yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-placemats-holly-motif-crochet-materials.webp)

Cotton DK yarn (#3) in cream, green and red: cream about 120 g, green 20 g, red 15 g per placemat; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Open mesh:** chain 2, dc in the next dc. **Filled block:** 2 dc in the chain-2 space, dc in the next dc — the mesh turns solid. **Gauge:** 20 dc and 10 rows measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work evenly: a tight row makes the placemat narrower than the row below it.

## The Pattern

The placemat is 27 meshes wide and 25 rows tall. The turning chain counts as the first mesh of each row, so count your meshes after every row.

**Foundation:** Chain 85.

**Row 1:** Dc in the 4th chain from the hook, *(chain 2, skip 2 chains, dc in the next chain)* 27 times — 27 open meshes. Turn.

**Rows 2–8:** Chain 5 (counts as dc and chain 2), *(dc in the next dc, chain 2)* 26 times, dc in the last dc — 27 open meshes. Turn after each row.

**The holly chart, rows 9–17:** work the filled blocks in green for the stem and leaves, and in red for the berries. Change colour at the start of each filled block and carry the unused colour loosely behind the work. Open meshes stay in cream.

Row 9: 12 open, 2 filled, 13 open — the stem base, meshes 13–14.

Row 10: 9 open, 2 filled, 1 open, 2 filled, 2 open, 2 filled, 9 open — leaf bases 10–11 and 17–18, stem 13–14.

Row 11: 8 open, 3 filled, 1 open, 2 filled, 1 open, 3 filled, 9 open — leaves 9–11 and 16–18.

Row 12: 7 open, 4 filled, 1 open, 2 filled, 1 open, 4 filled, 8 open — leaves 8–11 and 16–19.

Row 13: 8 open, 3 filled, 1 open, 2 filled, 1 open, 3 filled, 9 open — leaves 9–11 and 16–18.

Row 14: 9 open, 2 filled, 1 open, 2 filled, 2 open, 2 filled, 9 open — leaves 10–11 and 17–18.

Row 15: 9 open, 1 filled, 2 open, 2 filled, 3 open, 1 filled, 9 open — leaf tips 10 and 18.

Row 16: 12 open, 2 filled, 13 open — stem 13–14.

Row 17: 11 open, 1 filled, 1 open, 1 filled, 1 open, 1 filled, 11 open — three red berries 12, 14 and 16.

**Rows 18–25:** Work as Row 2 — 27 open meshes. Turn after each row. Do not fasten off after Row 25.

![Close-up of filet crochet in cream cotton yarn with a green holly leaf and red berries in filled blocks, showing the open mesh and solid double crochet blocks](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-placemats-holly-motif-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Border:** Join green at a corner. Round 1: chain 1, work sc evenly around the whole placemat — 1 sc per row end along the long sides, 1 sc per stitch along the short ends — with (sc, chain 2, sc) in each corner. Join to the first sc. Round 2: join red and work one more round the same way. Fasten off and weave in all ends.

**Making a set:** work all the placemats in cream first, then do the borders in one go. A set of four takes a weekend; a set of six covers the Christmas table.

## Styling and Care

Lay one at each place with the holly sprig centred above the plate, berries at the top. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat. If the corners curl, pin the placemat flat while it is still damp.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is filet crochet hard?** No — it is only double crochet and chains: an open mesh (chain 2, dc) and a filled block (2 dc in the space, dc in the next dc). The chart is written out row by row, so there is nothing to decode. Count the meshes after each row and you will catch a mistake in one row, not ten.

**What size is one placemat?** About 40 cm wide and 25 cm tall, which fits a dinner plate of about 27 cm with room at the sides for cutlery. To make it wider, add one mesh at a time: each extra mesh adds about 1.5 cm, and the foundation chain is 3 chains per mesh plus 4 — for 30 meshes, chain 94.

**Can I make it in one colour?** Yes — work everything in cream, including the border. The holly shows, because the filled blocks read as solid lace against the open mesh — and one colour is faster.

**How do I keep the edges straight?** Count the meshes after every row: there should always be 27. The turning chain counts as the first mesh, and the last dc of the row is easy to miss — if the count drops to 26, the sides start to slant inward. Mark the first and last mesh with stitch markers until the rhythm feels natural.

title: Christmas Cutlery Holders: Tree and Stocking
excerpt: Crochet two Christmas cutlery holders in one evening — a green tree holder with a cream star and a red stocking holder with a cream cuff — that turn each place setting into a small display.
image_alt: Handmade crochet Christmas cutlery holders in green and red yarn with a cream star and holly leaf, holding a knife, fork and spoon on a festive dining table.
content:
A place setting feels finished when the cutlery has a home of its own: a little crochet pocket in Christmas colours, holding the knife, fork and spoon upright on the plate. This pattern makes two holders in one evening — a green tree holder with a cream star and a red stripe, and a red stocking holder with a cream cuff and a holly leaf. Alternate them around the table and every place looks dressed for Christmas.

The holders are simple pockets: a flat panel worked in single crochet, folded in half and seamed up the sides, with the appliques sewn on last. If you can work single crochet in rows, you can make these — the star and leaf are worked separately and sewn on, so there is nothing fiddly in the main piece.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A flat panel folded into a pocket, seaming, a striped colour change, and two small appliques. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** each holder about 7.5 cm wide and 9 cm tall. **Time:** about 1 hour per holder, about 2 hours for the pair.

Use washable worsted yarn in red, green and cream; cotton or acrylic both work.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, green and cream worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-cutlery-holders-tree-stocking-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in red, green and cream: about 30 g per holder, 60 g for the pair; a 4 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), half double crochet (hdc), double crochet (dc). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Count your stitches at the end of every row so the two sides match.

## The Pattern

Both holders start the same way: a flat panel 12 stitches wide and 32 rows long, folded in half and seamed. At this gauge 12 stitches measure 7.5 cm — wide enough for a knife, fork and spoon side by side.

**Tree holder panel (green with a red stripe):** Chain 13. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (12). Rows 2–10: chain 1, turn, sc across (12) in green. Rows 11–13: chain 1, turn, sc across (12) in red. Rows 14–32: chain 1, turn, sc across (12) in green. Fasten off.

**Stocking holder panel (red):** Chain 13. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (12). Rows 2–32: chain 1, turn, sc across (12) in red. Fasten off.

**Seaming (both holders):** Fold the panel in half with the wrong side facing out, matching the two short ends at the top. Slip stitch through both layers along each long side, from the fold to the top edge, then turn the pocket right side out — the seam sits inside. The pocket is now 16 rows tall, about 9 cm.

**Star applique (make 1, cream):** Round 1: 5 sc in a magic ring (5). Round 2: (slip stitch, chain 2, dc, chain 2, slip stitch) in each sc — 5 points. Fasten off with a sewing tail and sew the star to the front of the tree holder, near the top.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet cutlery holder in green yarn with single crochet stitches and a cream crochet star applique, showing the pocket seam](https://cozyloops.site/assets/christmas-cutlery-holders-tree-stocking-closeup.webp)

**Cuff (stocking holder only, cream):** Join cream at the top edge of the pocket. Round 1: work sc evenly around the top opening — 12 sc along each side (24). Rounds 2–3: sc around (24). Fasten off. Fold the cuff down over the outside of the pocket.

**Holly leaf applique (make 1, green):** Chain 9. Row 1: slip stitch in the 2nd chain from the hook, sc in the next 2 chains, hdc in the next 2 chains, dc in the next 2 chains, (dc, chain 2, dc) in the last chain; then work down the other side of the foundation chain: dc in the next 2 chains, hdc in the next 2 chains, sc in the next 2 chains, slip stitch in the last chain. Fasten off with a sewing tail.

**Berries (make 3, red):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Pull the ring tight and fasten off with a sewing tail. Sew the leaf to the front of the stocking holder, below the cuff, with the three berries in a cluster beside it.

**Making a set:** work all the panels first, then seam them, then sew on all the appliques in one go. A set of four takes an evening; a set of eight covers a full Christmas table.

## Styling and Care

Stand one holder on each plate with the cutlery inside, star and leaf facing out. They pair with the scalloped coasters on the coffee table and the holly placemats on the dining table. Machine wash cold and dry flat; the appliques are sewn on, not glued, so they stay put. Reshape the pocket while it is still damp.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Will cutlery fit inside?** Yes — the pocket is 7.5 cm wide and 9 cm tall, and a standard knife, fork and spoon sit side by side inside it. For chunky handles, add 2 stitches to the foundation chain (14 stitches, about 8.75 cm wide) and work the same 32 rows.

**Can I wash them?** Yes. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat. The star, leaf and berries are sewn on, not glued, so they survive the wash. Reshape the pocket while it is damp so it dries square.

**How many should I make?** One per place setting. Make the pair first to check the fit, then a set of 4 for a small table or 6 to 8 for a full Christmas dinner. Alternate the tree and the stocking around the table.

**Can I make them in other colours?** Yes — any worsted yarn in Christmas colours works. Keep the body and the applique in contrast so the star and the leaf show: a cream body with a red star, or a green body with a cream cuff.

title: Crochet Candle Covers for the Mantel
excerpt: Crochet ribbed candle covers in three sizes for LED flameless pillar candles — cranberry with a cream edging, for the mantel. LED candles only, never a real flame.
image_alt: Three handmade crochet ribbed candle covers in cranberry red yarn with cream edging on glowing LED flameless pillar candles on a wooden mantel.
content:
A row of candles on the mantel is the fastest way to make a room feel like Christmas — and a ribbed crochet cover turns a plain white LED candle into part of the decoration. This pattern makes three covers, one for each standard LED pillar size, in cranberry with a cream edging. The front-post and back-post ribbing stretches to hug the candle and springs back when you slip it off.

**Safety first — LED candles only:** these covers are for battery-operated LED flameless candles only. Never use them with a real candle, a tea light, or any open flame. Yarn is flammable, and a cover must never sit near a flame or heat source. Even for a photograph, do not put a lit candle inside a crochet cover.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Working in the round, front-post and back-post ribbing, and a contrast edging. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** small 20 cm around × 9 cm tall; medium 20 cm × 13 cm; large 26 cm × 13 cm. **Time:** about 1 hour for the small cover, 1.5 hours for the medium or large.

Use worsted yarn in cranberry and cream; a smooth yarn shows the ribs best — avoid fluffy or bouclé yarn.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cranberry red and cream worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors, a yarn needle and a tape measure, with two white LED flameless pillar candles beside them on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-candle-covers-mantel-pattern-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in cranberry and cream: cranberry about 60 g (small), 80 g (medium), 100 g (large); cream about 15 g per cover; a 4 mm hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker; three LED flameless pillar candles (sizes below).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc), front-post double crochet (fpdc: work a dc around the post of the stitch below, from the front), back-post double crochet (bpdc: the same, from the back). **Gauge:** 14 dc and 10 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. The ribbing stretches, so the cover is worked smaller than the candle: about 20 cm around unstretched for a 7.5 cm candle, about 26 cm for a 10 cm candle.

## The Pattern

Work in the round without turning: join each round with a slip stitch, chain 2 to start the next (the chain does not count as a stitch), and mark the first stitch.

**Small cover (fits an LED candle 7.5 cm across and 10 cm tall):** Chain 28 and join into a ring without twisting the chain. Round 1: chain 2, dc around, join (28). Rounds 2–7: chain 2, (fpdc, bpdc) 14 times, join (28). Round 8: join cream, chain 1, sc around, join (28). Fasten off. Bottom edging: join cream at the foundation edge and work 1 round of sc (28). Fasten off. The cover is about 9 cm tall, so the top centimetre of candle shows.

**Medium cover (fits an LED candle 7.5 cm across and 15 cm tall):** Work as the small cover, but with 10 ribbing rounds (Rounds 2–11) and the cream edging as Round 12 — about 13 cm tall.

**Large cover (fits an LED candle 10 cm across and 15 cm tall):** Chain 36 and join into a ring, then work as the medium cover with 36 stitches throughout — (fpdc, bpdc) 18 times per ribbing round — about 13 cm tall.

![Close-up of front-post and back-post ribbed crochet in cranberry red yarn on a candle cover, showing the raised vertical ribs and a cream single crochet edging round at the top](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-candle-covers-mantel-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Optional stripe:** work one ribbing round in cream — Round 5 for the small cover, Round 7 for the medium and large — for a thin cream line around the middle.

**Fitting check:** try the cover on the candle before the edging rounds — it should stretch snugly and sit flat. If it is loose, go down half a hook size; if it will not stretch over the candle, add 2 stitches to the foundation chain (about 1.4 cm around).

## Choosing flameless candles

Buy LED pillar candles in the diameter the cover was made for: 7.5 cm for the small and medium covers, 10 cm for the large. Look for a flickering flame effect and a remote with a timer. Battery candles take AA or AAA batteries; rechargeables charge by USB. Check the height on the box — a 10 cm candle in a medium cover leaves 5 cm of bare candle showing.

## Styling and Care

Stand the three covers in a row on the mantel, tallest in the middle, glowing tops above the edging. They pair with the pinecone stitch table runner. Keep the covers away from radiators, open fires and any real flame — they are yarn, and they belong on LED candles only. To wash, slip the cover off the candle, hand wash cold, reshape and dry flat. Do not machine wash or tumble dry.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Are they safe with real candles?** No — never. These covers are for LED flameless candles only. Yarn is flammable, so a crochet cover must never go near a real flame, a tea light, or a lit candle — not even for a photograph. If you want real candles on the mantel, use bare glass holders with nothing crocheted near them.

**What sizes fit standard LED candles?** The small cover fits a 7.5 cm LED candle 10 cm tall, the medium fits 7.5 cm by 15 cm, and the large fits 10 cm by 15 cm. Measure your candle's diameter first — it is printed on the box. Between sizes, make the larger cover; the ribbing takes up the slack.

**Can I make them in other colours?** Yes — any worsted yarn works. A cream body with a cranberry edging inverts the look, and forest green with a cream edging matches the cutlery holders. Very dark colours are fine too: the light comes from the candle top above the cover, not through the yarn.

**How do I wash them?** Slip the cover off the candle first, then hand wash cold and dry flat, reshaping the ribs while the cover is damp. Do not machine wash or tumble dry — the ribbing stretches out and does not spring back.

title: Mini Advent Stockings: 24 Tiny Stockings to Crochet
excerpt: Crochet twenty-four tiny numbered advent stockings in one reusable garland — each holding a chocolate or a note, pinned to a ribbon on the wall.
image_alt: Handmade crochet mini advent stockings in red, green, cream and gold yarn with number tags, pinned in a row along a ribbon garland on a wall.
content:
An Advent calendar you crochet once and bring out every December is the kind of Christmas tradition that starts small: twenty-four tiny stockings, each holding a chocolate or a folded note, pinned in a row along a ribbon on the wall. Children hunt for today's number each morning. When December ends, the stockings fold into a box and wait for next year.

Every stocking is the same tiny pattern — a toe-up tube with a ribbed cuff and a hanging loop — so once you have made one, the other twenty-three are pure rhythm. Work them in four repeating colours, number them with card tags, and hang them on two metres of ribbon.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Toe-up shaping in the round, a ribbed cuff worked in back loops only, and numbering and hanging a garland. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** each stocking about 3 cm wide and 7 cm tall, not counting the loop. **Time:** about 20 minutes per stocking, about 8 hours for the full set of twenty-four.

Use worsted weight yarn in red, green, cream and gold; scraps work well, because each stocking takes only about 10 g.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, green, cream and gold worsted yarn, scissors, a yarn needle, a length of ribbon and small card number tags on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-advent-stockings-24-crochet-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in red, green, cream and gold: about 10 g per stocking, 240 g for the full set, 60 g of each colour; a 3.5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker; 2 m of wide ribbon; 24 small wooden pegs; 24 card number tags and twine.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), back loop only (blo: work into the back loop of the stitch only). **Gauge:** 18 sc and 20 rounds measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook. Work tightly so the stocking holds its shape when it hangs. A DK yarn on the same hook makes a smaller stocking and chunky yarn makes a bigger one — the stitch counts stay the same.

## The Pattern

Work in the round without turning, marking the first stitch of each round. Make one stocking first to check the size, then work the rest in batches.

**Toe:** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Round 2: increase around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). The toe is a flat circle about 3 cm across.

**Foot and leg:** Rounds 4–10: sc around (18). Seven straight rounds make a tube about 5 cm tall — foot and leg in one piece, with no heel to shape. At this size no heel turn is needed: the stocking hangs straight from its loop, and the rounded toe and cuff still make it read as a stocking.

**Cuff:** Join cream at the top of the leg. Rounds 11–14: sc in the back loop only around (18). Working in the back loop only makes a ribbed band that looks like a folded cuff. Fasten off and weave in the ends.

**Hanging loop:** Join yarn at the back of the cuff. Chain 12, slip stitch into the next stitch of the cuff, and fasten off. The loop is about 3 cm long — long enough to slip over a peg or straight onto the ribbon.

![Close-up of a tiny handmade crochet advent stocking in red yarn with a cream ribbed cuff, showing single crochet stitches and the back-loop ribbing](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-advent-stockings-24-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Numbering:** Tie one card tag to each stocking's loop with a short length of twine, numbers 1 to 24. Or chain-stitch the number onto the cuff in a contrast colour before you add the loop, keeping the digits small enough to fit the 3 cm cuff.

**Hanging the garland:** Fix 2 m of ribbon to the wall with two small hooks, leaving a gentle sag in the middle. Peg one stocking every 8 cm — twenty-four stockings at 8 cm intervals fill 192 cm, so the set fits with a little room at each end. Hang them in number order, left to right.

**Colour plan:** Work six stockings in each colour — red, green, cream and gold — all with a cream cuff, so the row reads as one set. Alternate the colours along the ribbon: red, green, cream, gold, then repeat.

**Making the set:** Work assembly-line style — all twenty-four toes first, then all the legs, then all the cuffs and loops. Four stockings an evening finishes the set in six evenings.

## Styling and Care

Fill each stocking with a small chocolate, a wrapped sweet or a folded note — nothing heavier, or the loop stretches. Hang the garland on 1 December and take each day's stocking down as it is opened. After Christmas, empty the stockings, machine wash cold, dry flat, and fold the set into a box with the ribbon and tags. The same set returns every December.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does the full set take?** About 8 hours of crocheting — around 20 minutes per stocking — plus an hour for numbering and hanging. Worked four an evening, the set is done in six evenings, so start in mid-November and the garland is ready for 1 December.

**What fits inside each stocking?** A small chocolate, a wrapped sweet, a folded note, a tiny toy or a coin. The opening is about 3 cm across and the pocket about 5 cm deep, so anything flat and light fits — nothing heavy, or the loop stretches and the stocking sags.

**How do I number them?** Tie a card tag numbered 1 to 24 to each hanging loop with twine — the simplest method, and the tags come off for washing. Or chain-stitch the number onto the cuff in a contrast colour. Number them before you hang them, and hang them in order along the ribbon.

**Can I use a different yarn weight?** Yes — the stitch counts stay the same and only the size changes. DK makes a smaller stocking, about 2.5 cm wide; chunky makes a bigger one, about 4 cm wide. Keep all twenty-four in the same yarn weight, or the row looks uneven.

title: Crochet Gift Tags with Mini Motifs
excerpt: Crochet gift tags with mini star, tree and bell motifs — ten minutes each, in cotton scraps — that double as tree ornaments after the gift is opened.
image_alt: Handmade crochet gift tags in red, green, cream and gold cotton yarn shaped as a star, a tree and a bell, tied to wrapped Christmas presents.
content:
A gift tag you crochet is a small kindness twice over: it marks the present, and when the paper is gone the tag stays — slipped onto the tree as an ornament, or kept for next year. Three little motifs — a star, a tree and a bell — cover every present under the tree, and each one takes about ten minutes from cotton scraps.

The trick is cotton, not acrylic: cotton holds its shape, takes ink for a name, and stiffens with a light spray of starch. Work assembly-line style — all the stars, then all the trees, then all the bells — and a batch of twenty is an evening's work.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Small motifs worked in the round and in rows, a bell with a flared skirt, and a chain loop for tying. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** each tag about 4 to 5 cm across, not counting the loop. **Time:** about 10 minutes per tag, about 3.5 hours for a batch of twenty.

Use cotton DK scraps in red, green, cream and gold; cotton holds its shape and takes a pen for the name.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, green, cream and gold cotton DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, scissors, a yarn needle and a fine-tip fabric pen on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-gift-tags-mini-motifs-pattern-materials.webp)

Cotton DK yarn (#3) in red, green, cream and gold: about 5 g per tag, 100 g for a batch of twenty; a 3 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a fine-tip fabric pen; spray starch (optional).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), decrease (dec: sc2tog), double crochet (dc). **Gauge:** 20 sc and 22 rows measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Gauge is not critical — a slightly bigger or smaller motif still works as a tag — but keep your tension even so the motifs match in size.

## The Pattern

Work one motif at a time; each gets a chain loop for tying, added last.

**Star (make as many as you like, cream or gold):** Round 1: 5 sc in a magic ring (5). Round 2: (slip stitch, chain 2, dc, chain 2, slip stitch) in each sc — 5 points. Fasten off. The star is about 4 cm across.

**Tree (green):** Chain 2. Row 1: 2 sc in the 2nd chain from the hook (2). Row 2: chain 1, turn, inc, sc (3). Row 3: chain 1, turn, inc, sc, inc (5). Row 4: chain 1, turn, inc, sc 3, inc (7). Row 5: chain 1, turn, sc across (7). Row 6 (trunk): chain 1, turn, skip 2 sts, sc in the next 3 sts (3). Row 7: chain 1, turn, sc across (3). Fasten off. The tree is about 5 cm tall.

**Bell (red or gold):** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Round 2: inc around (12). Round 3: (sc, inc) 6 times (18). Rounds 4–5: sc around (18). Round 6 (skirt): (2 sc, inc) 6 times (24).
