Fasten off. **Clapper:** Round 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6). Round 2: (sc, inc) 3 times (9). Round 3: (sc, dec) 3 times (6). Fasten off and sew the clapper to the centre of the bell's underside. The bell is about 4 cm tall.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet gift tag in cream cotton yarn shaped as a star, showing single crochet stitches and the pointed double crochet tips](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-gift-tags-mini-motifs-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Tying loop (every tag):** Join yarn at the top of the motif. Chain 20, slip stitch into the same stitch, and fasten off. The loop is about 5 cm long — thread it through a bow or a gift's ribbon to tie the tag on, or slip it over a branch to hang the tag on the tree.

**Writing the name:** Write the name on the back with a fine-tip fabric pen — cotton takes ink cleanly and will not smudge once dry. Or chain-stitch the first initial onto the back with a yarn needle. Write the name before tying the tag to the gift, and let the ink dry for a few minutes.

**Making a batch of twenty:** Work assembly-line style — all the stars, then all the trees, then all the bells, then all the loops. Seven stars, seven trees and six bells make a mixed batch of twenty. At about ten minutes a tag, the batch takes about three and a half hours — one evening.

## Styling and Care

Tie one tag to each present with its loop, name facing out. After the gift is opened, slip the loop over a branch and the tag becomes a tree ornament. Cotton tags wash — hand wash cold and dry flat — but spot-clean a tag with a pen-written name, or the ink fades. A light spray of starch stiffens the motifs so they hang flat.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I write a name on them?** With a fine-tip fabric pen on the back — cotton takes ink cleanly and dries without smudging. Or chain-stitch the first initial onto the back with a contrast colour. Write the name before tying the tag to the gift, and give the ink a few minutes to dry.

**Can I make a batch of 20?** Yes — that is how they are meant to be made. Work assembly-line style: all the stars, then all the trees, then all the bells, then all the loops. Seven stars, seven trees and six bells make twenty, in about three and a half hours.

**What yarn holds its shape?** Cotton DK — stiff enough to hold a motif flat, and it takes a pen for the name. Acrylic is softer and the motifs curl at the edges; if acrylic is all you have, spray the finished tag with starch and press it flat while it dries.

**Can I use them as ornaments after the gift is opened?** Yes — that is the point. Slip the tying loop over a branch and the tag hangs on the tree. The star and the bell hang best; the tree needs its loop at the very top so it hangs straight.

title: Crochet Balaclava Hood: Beginner Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a beginner balaclava hood from the crown down in chunky yarn — a face opening worked in rows, a ribbed neck, and a matching-sweater pairing idea.
image_alt: A person wearing a handmade chunky crochet balaclava hood in cream wool with a ribbed neck, outdoors in winter.
content:
A balaclava is the warmest thing you can crochet for winter: a hood, a hat and a scarf in one piece, with only your face showing. This beginner version is worked from the crown down in half double crochet, with a face opening worked in rows and a ribbed neck that sits flat on your shoulders — no shaping tricks, no seams, just rounds, rows and one join.

The way to wear it this winter is simple: one colour, chunky yarn, and a matching sweater in the same yarn so the set reads as an outfit. Wool or a mohair blend is warm enough for a January walk; cotton works for a cool spring morning instead.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Increasing in the round, working a face opening in rows, rejoining in the round, and front-post ribbing. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** adult fits a 56–58 cm head, about 55 cm around, 34 cm from crown to neck edge. **Time:** about 4 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream chunky wool yarn with a 6 mm crochet hook, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-balaclava-hood-beginner-pattern-materials.webp)

Chunky weight yarn (#5) in wool or a mohair blend: about 150 g for the adult size, 100 g for teen, 200 g for large; a 6 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), half double crochet (hdc), increase (inc: 2 hdc in one stitch), front-post half double crochet (fphdc: work a hdc around the post of the stitch below, from the front), back-post half double crochet (bphdc: the same, from the back). **Gauge:** 12 hdc and 9 rows measure 10 cm with a 6 mm hook. Check your gauge before Round 5 — the crown rounds set the size.

## Sizes

| Size | Head | Crown stitches | Face opening | Face rows | Yarn |
|---|---|---|---|---|--- |
| Teen | 52–54 cm | 60 | 16 sts | 9 | about 100 g |
| Adult | 56–58 cm | 66 | 18 sts | 10 | about 150 g |
| Large | 60–62 cm | 72 | 18 sts | 11 | about 200 g |

Work the adult size; teen and large change only where noted.

## The Pattern

Work in the round without turning unless the pattern says turn, marking the first stitch of each round.

**Crown:** Round 1: 6 hdc in a magic ring (6). Round 2: increase around (12). Rounds 3–11: increase 6 stitches evenly each round — (hdc, inc) 6 times (18), (2 hdc, inc) 6 times (24), (3 hdc, inc) 6 times (30), (4 hdc, inc) 6 times (36), (5 hdc, inc) 6 times (42), (6 hdc, inc) 6 times (48), (7 hdc, inc) 6 times (54), (8 hdc, inc) 6 times (60), (9 hdc, inc) 6 times (66). Teen stops at Round 10 (60 stitches); large adds Round 12: (10 hdc, inc) 6 times (72).

**Straight rounds:** Rounds 12–15 (adult): hdc around (66) — 4 rounds. Teen: Rounds 11–14 (60 stitches). Large: Rounds 13–16 (72 stitches). These four rounds take the hood from the crown down to brow level.

**Face opening:** Turn the work. Row 1: chain 2, turn, hdc across 48 stitches, leaving the front 18 stitches unworked. Rows 2–10: chain 2, turn, hdc across (48). Teen: work 44 stitches for 9 rows, leaving 16 unworked. Large: work 54 stitches for 11 rows, leaving 18 unworked. The opening is about 15 cm wide and 11 cm tall, from brow to chin.

**Neck:** Join the yarn at the bottom edge of the hood. Round 1: hdc around the full circle — 48 stitches across the back plus 18 stitches across the front bottom edge (66). Rounds 2–7: hdc around (66) — 6 rounds, about 7 cm of neck. Rounds 8–10 (ribbing): (fphdc, bphdc) around (66) — 3 rounds. Fasten off.

![Close-up of half double crochet stitches and front-post ribbing in cream chunky wool yarn on a crochet balaclava hood](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-balaclava-hood-beginner-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Face edging:** Join yarn at the top corner of the face opening. Round 1: work single crochet evenly around the opening — 18 stitches across the top, 1 sc in the end of each of the 10 rows down each side, and 18 across the bottom, about 56 sc in all. Round 2: sc around. Fasten off. The edging frames the face and stops the opening stretching.

**Matching sweater idea:** a simple half double crochet sweater in the same yarn and colour turns the balaclava into half of a set — wear them together on the coldest days, and the balaclava on its own with any coat the rest of the week.

## Styling and Care

Pull the hood on first, then your coat, so the ribbed neck sits inside the collar. If the neck rides up to your chin, work one more plain round before the ribbing next time. Hand wash wool or mohair cold and dry flat; a cotton version can go in the machine on cold, gentle.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Will it fit over glasses?** Yes. The face opening is about 15 cm wide and 11 cm tall on the adult size, so glasses sit inside it comfortably. Put the balaclava on first, then your glasses, and the arms pass through the opening without catching. If your frames are very wide, work the large size — the opening is a row taller.

**How warm is it?** Very — chunky wool around the whole head and neck, with the ribbed neck sealing out drafts, is warmer than a hat and scarf together. It is comfortable on a cold winter walk with a coat. A mohair blend is warmer still; cotton is noticeably cooler, which is why it suits spring rather than deep winter.

**Can I make it in cotton for spring?** Yes — use the same stitch counts with a chunky cotton. Cotton stretches less than wool, so check your gauge: if it is stiff, go up half a hook size so the crown still measures 55 cm around.

**How do I wash it?** Follow the yarn label. Wool and mohair: hand wash cold, press out the water in a towel, and dry flat. Cotton: machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat. Never tumble dry wool — the crown felts and shrinks.

title: Twisted Ear Warmer Headband: Free Crochet Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a twisted ear warmer headband in an hour — one rectangle, one twist join, in three widths and three head sizes.
image_alt: A person wearing a handmade twisted crochet ear warmer headband in rust-red worsted yarn, the twist at the front centre.
content:
An ear warmer is the fastest winter win in crochet: one rectangle, one twist, one seam, and you have a headband that keeps your ears warm without flattening your hair. The twist is the whole trick — it gathers the fabric at the front so the band sits flat, stays put, and looks like it took far longer than an hour.

This one comes in three widths and three head sizes, so the same pattern makes a narrow band for a run, a medium one for the school run, and a wide one for a cold market morning. Make a few in different colours and they stack into a market stall in an afternoon.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A flat rectangle worked in rows, the twist join, and sizing with negative ease. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** adult medium about 56 cm around and 10 cm wide. **Time:** about 1 hour.

Use worsted yarn in any colour you like; a smooth yarn shows the half double crochet texture, and a soft one matters because this sits against your forehead and ears.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of rust-red worsted yarn with a 5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/twisted-ear-warmer-headband-crochet-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): about 50 g per headband; a 5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), half double crochet (hdc). **Gauge:** 14 hdc and 10 rows measure 10 cm with a 5 mm hook. The band is worked about 2 cm shorter than the head it fits — that negative ease is what holds it in place, so do not add extra length to be safe.

## Sizes

Measure around your head just above the eyebrows and over the ears, with the tape snug. Then pick the row from the table — and if you fall between sizes, make the smaller one, because the band stretches.

| Size | Head | Foundation chain | Stitches per row | Finished length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Child | 50 cm | chain 70 | 68 hdc | about 48.5 cm |
| Teen | 54 cm | chain 74 | 72 hdc | about 51.5 cm |
| Adult | 57 cm | chain 80 | 78 hdc | about 55.5 cm |

Pick a width too: narrow 8 rows (8 cm), medium 10 rows (10 cm), wide 12 rows (12 cm). The medium width suits most adults; the narrow one is best for running, and the wide one is the warmest.

## The Pattern

Work in rows, turning at the end of each row. The numbers below are for the adult size; the child and teen sizes change only the foundation chain and the stitch count per row.

**Band:** Chain 80. Row 1: hdc in the 3rd chain from the hook and across (78). Rows 2–10: chain 2, turn, hdc across (78). That is 10 rows for the medium width — work 8 rows for narrow, or 12 rows for wide. Fasten off, leaving a tail about 30 cm long for seaming.

![Close-up of half double crochet stitches and the twisted seam at the front of a rust-red crochet ear warmer headband](https://cozyloops.site/assets/twisted-ear-warmer-headband-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Twist join:** Lay the band flat with the right side up. Bring the two short ends together. Fold one end in half, top edge to bottom edge, so it makes a small loop. Slip the other end into that loop, so the two ends interlock like a C — this is the twist. Whip stitch through all four layers across the width of the band with the tail, taking care to catch every layer. Turn the band right side out and the twist sits at the front centre, gathered and flat.

**Flower (optional):** Round 1: 5 sc in a magic ring (5). Round 2: (slip stitch, chain 2, dc, chain 2, slip stitch) in each sc — 5 points. Fasten off with a sewing tail and sew the flower over the twist, or sew a button there instead. The flower hides the seam and marks the front.

**Making a set:** work all the bands first, then do all the twist joins in one go — the join is the only fiddly part, and it gets faster each time. Three bands in three widths make a good market set: narrow, medium and wide in the same yarn.

## Styling and Care

Wear the twist at the front centre, over or under your hair — over hair shows the twist off, under hair holds it flatter. The band should sit just above the eyebrows and fully cover the ears; if it creeps up, it is too loose and you need the next size down. Hand wash cold and dry flat, or machine wash cold on gentle if your yarn allows it, and reshape the twist while it is still damp.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I measure my head?** Wrap a tape measure around your head just above the eyebrows and over the tops of your ears, keeping it snug — not tight, not loose. Read the number and find your row in the size table. Measure twice: a centimetre off the tape is a centimetre off the fit.

**Will the twist stay in place?** Yes. The seam goes through all four layers of the interlocked ends, so the twist is locked by the stitching, and the band's negative ease holds it against your head. If the band slides, the problem is the size, not the twist — make the next size down.

**Can I add a flower?** Yes — the five-petal flower in the pattern sews over the twist and marks the front of the band. A button works the same way, or a small crocheted leaf. Sew it through the twist itself, not just the top layer, so it cannot flop forward.

**Can I make it in a child's size?** Yes — the child row in the size table fits a 50 cm head: chain 70, 68 hdc per row, and the same three widths. For a toddler with a 48 cm head, chain 65 and work 63 hdc per row, and use the narrow width so the band does not cover their eyes.

title: Fingerless Gloves with Ribbed Cuffs
excerpt: Crochet fingerless gloves with a ribbed cuff and a thumb gusset worked stitch by stitch — warm hands, free fingertips, phone-friendly.
image_alt: A person wearing handmade rust-red fingerless crochet gloves with ribbed cuffs, holding a steaming mug of coffee in the snow.
content:
A pair of fingerless gloves is the winter accessory that earns its keep every day: warm hands, free fingertips, and a pattern you can finish in an evening. The ribbed cuff holds them on, the thumb gusset is worked stitch by stitch, and the fingers stop just below the knuckles — so you can type and text without taking them off.

This pattern makes a proper pair: the gusset is mirrored on the second glove so the thumbs fall on opposite sides. Work the medium size as written, or pick your row from the size table.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A ribbed cuff in front-post and back-post stitches, a thumb gusset increased stitch by stitch, and separating the thumb from the hand. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** medium fits a 19 cm hand, about 16 cm long from cuff to fingertips. **Time:** about 2 hours per glove, about 4 hours for the pair.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of rust-red and cream DK yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/fingerless-gloves-ribbed-cuffs-crochet-materials.webp)

DK yarn (#3) in rust-red: about 100 g for the pair, 50 g per glove; a 4 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc), increase (inc: 2 sc in one stitch), front-post double crochet (fpdc: work a dc around the post of the stitch below, from the front), back-post double crochet (bpdc: the same, from the back). **Gauge:** 18 sc and 20 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook.

## Sizes

Measure around your hand just below the knuckles. Small and large change only the starting chain and the gusset width.

| Size | Hand | Cuff chain | Gusset stitches | Thumb stitches | Yarn per pair |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small | 17 cm | chain 30 | 11 | 13 | about 80 g |
| Medium | 19 cm | chain 34 | 13 | 15 | about 100 g |
| Large | 21 cm | chain 38 | 15 | 17 | about 120 g |

## The Pattern

Work in the round, joining each round with a slip stitch; the starting chain does not count as a stitch. Mark the first stitch. The numbers below are for the medium size.

**Cuff:** Chain 34 and join into a ring without twisting the chain. Round 1: chain 3, dc around, join (34). Rounds 2–5: chain 3, (fpdc, bpdc) around, join (34) — 4 rounds of ribbing, about 4 cm tall. The ribbing pulls in, so the cuff measures smaller than your wrist and stretches to fit.

**Hand:** Rounds 6–14: chain 1, sc around, join (34) — 9 rounds, about 4.5 cm of palm before the thumb starts.

**Thumb gusset:** The gusset grows by 2 stitches every other round, on one side only — keep the increases in the same place so it forms a neat triangle.

Round 15: chain 1, sc 16, inc, sc, inc, sc 15, join (36). Round 16: chain 1, sc around, join (36). Round 17: chain 1, sc 16, inc, sc 3, inc, sc 15, join (38). Round 18: chain 1, sc around, join (38). Round 19: chain 1, sc 16, inc, sc 5, inc, sc 15, join (40). Round 20: chain 1, sc around, join (40). Round 21: chain 1, sc 16, inc, sc 7, inc, sc 15, join (42). Round 22: chain 1, sc around, join (42). Round 23: chain 1, sc 16, inc, sc 9, inc, sc 15, join (44). The gusset is now 13 stitches wide.

**Separate the thumb:** Round 24: chain 1, sc 16, chain 2, skip the 13 gusset stitches, sc 15, join (33 stitches: 31 sc plus the 2-chain bridge). The bridge becomes the web between thumb and hand.

**Fingers:** Rounds 25–31: chain 1, sc around, join (33) — 7 rounds, about 3.5 cm. Fasten off and weave in the ends. The fingers end just below the knuckles, so your fingertips stay free.

![Close-up of a handmade rust-red fingerless crochet glove showing the ribbed front-post and back-post cuff and the thumb gusset opening](https://cozyloops.site/assets/fingerless-gloves-ribbed-cuffs-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Thumb:** Join yarn at the gusset. Round 1: sc in each of the 13 gusset stitches, then 2 sc in the chain-2 bridge (15). Rounds 2–4: chain 1, sc around, join (15) — 3 rounds, about 2.5 cm. Fasten off; the thumb is open at the tip, like the fingers.

**Second glove:** Work the same glove, but mirror the gusset — sc 15 first, then the increase sequence, then sc 16 — so the thumb falls on the other side. Everything else is identical.

## Styling and Care

Wear them with the cuff over your wrist and the gusset at the base of the thumb. They pair with the twisted ear warmer headband and the chunky cowl. Hand wash cold and dry flat, or machine wash cold on gentle, and reshape the cuff while it is still damp.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I size the thumb hole?** The thumb opening is 15 stitches on the medium — about 8 cm around. If your thumb is wider, work one more increase round before separating (gusset 15, thumb 17); if narrower, stop one round earlier (gusset 11, thumb 13).

**Will they fit over a watch?** Yes — the ribbed cuff stretches about 2 cm, so a slim watch fits under a medium cuff. For a chunky watch, work the large cuff (chain 38) even if the hand is medium; the ribbing still pulls in above the watch.

**Can I make them longer?** Yes — add 2 rounds to the hand before the gusset (Rounds 6–16 instead of 6–14) for longer fingers, or 2 more ribbing rounds for a longer cuff. Keep the gusset rounds the same, or the thumb ends up in the wrong place.

**Can I make them in one colour?** Yes — one colour shows the ribbing best. A contrast cuff works too: change colour at Round 1 of the hand section.

title: Chunky Cowl with a Button Closure
excerpt: Crochet a one-skein chunky cowl with a button closure — no sewing the join — in two heights, neck warmer or full cowl.
image_alt: A person wearing a handmade chunky cream crochet cowl with a large wooden button closure, outdoors in the snow.
content:
A cowl with a button closure is the cleverest winter make in this calendar: no sewing the join, no fiddling with a seam — you wrap it around your neck and fasten one big button. It is a true one-skein project in the shorter height, and the taller version folds over into a proper cowl that keeps out the wind.

Work it flat in rows, in half double crochet with one openwork row for texture. The buttonhole is worked near the end, and the button is sewn at the other end with a thread shank.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Working flat in rows, a chain-space openwork row, a buttonhole row, and sewing on a button with a thread shank. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** neck warmer about 60 cm around and 18 cm tall; full cowl about 70 cm around and 27 cm tall. **Time:** about 3 hours for the neck warmer, about 4 hours for the full cowl.

## Materials and Tools

![A ball of cream chunky yarn with a 6.5 mm crochet hook, one large round wooden button, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/chunky-cowl-button-closure-crochet-materials.webp)

Chunky weight yarn (#5) in cream: about 100 g for the neck warmer, about 150 g for the full cowl; a 6.5 mm crochet hook; 1 large button, about 2.5–3 cm across; a yarn needle; scissors; a stitch marker.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), half double crochet (hdc). **Gauge:** 11 hdc and 8 rows measure 10 cm with a 6.5 mm hook. The cowl is worked lengthways, so the chain sets the height and the rows set the length around your neck — check your row gauge, because it decides the fit.

## The Pattern

Work in rows, turning at the end of each row; the chain 2 at the start of each row counts as the first half double crochet. The numbers below are for the neck warmer; the full cowl changes only where noted.

**Neck warmer:** Chain 22. Row 1: hdc in the 3rd chain from the hook and across (20). Rows 2–23: chain 2, turn, hdc across (20).

**Openwork row:** Row 24: chain 2, turn, (hdc in the next stitch, chain 1, skip 1 stitch) 10 times — 10 hdc and 10 chain spaces, 20 positions. Row 25: chain 2, turn, hdc in each hdc and each chain-1 space (20).

**Continue:** Rows 26–45: chain 2, turn, hdc across (20).

**Buttonhole row:** Row 46: chain 2, turn, hdc 8, chain 2, skip 2 stitches, hdc 10 — 20 positions, with a 2-chain gap in the middle. Row 47: chain 2, turn, hdc across, working 2 hdc in the chain-2 space (20). Row 48: chain 2, turn, hdc across (20). Fasten off. The cowl is 48 rows long, about 60 cm around.

**Button:** Sew the button at the opposite end, centred on the edge of Row 1, with a thread shank: sew over a matchstick, then remove it and wrap the thread around the stitches underneath, so the button stands about 3 mm proud and the buttonhole closes without puckering.

![Close-up of a handmade chunky cream crochet cowl showing half double crochet stitches and a buttonhole with a large round wooden button fastened through it](https://cozyloops.site/assets/chunky-cowl-button-closure-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Full cowl:** Chain 32. Row 1: hdc in the 3rd chain from the hook and across (30). Rows 2–27: chain 2, turn, hdc across (30). Row 28 (openwork): chain 2, turn, (hdc in the next stitch, chain 1, skip 1 stitch) 15 times — 15 hdc and 15 chain spaces, 30 positions. Row 29: chain 2, turn, hdc in each hdc and each chain-1 space (30). Rows 30–53: chain 2, turn, hdc across (30). Row 54 (buttonhole): chain 2, turn, hdc 13, chain 2, skip 2 stitches, hdc 15 — 30 positions. Row 55: chain 2, turn, hdc across, working 2 hdc in the chain-2 space (30). Row 56: chain 2, turn, hdc across (30). Fasten off and sew the button on as above. The full cowl is 56 rows, about 70 cm around, and folds over at the top.

**Wearing it:** Wrap the cowl once around your neck and fasten the button at the side or the front. The full cowl folds down over the button, so the button hides and the top edge rolls softly.

## Styling and Care

Wear the neck warmer flat for a neat collar, or pushed up over your chin — the button holds it either way. It pairs with the fingerless gloves and the balaclava hood. Hand wash cold and dry flat; chunky yarn holds water, so press it in a towel first and never hang it up wet.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How many skeins do I need?** One 100 g skein of chunky yarn — about 100 m — makes the neck warmer with yarn to spare. The full cowl takes about 150 g, so buy a second skein or a 150 g ball.

**Will the button hold?** Yes. The buttonhole is worked in half double crochet, which is firm, and the thread shank lets the button sit through the hole without pulling the fabric. If it slips out, work the buttonhole with chain 1 instead of chain 2, or sew a second button inside as a backup.

**Can I make it in a child's size?** Yes — chain 16, Row 1: 14 hdc, then work 40 rows, about 50 cm around, with the buttonhole at Row 38 (hdc 6, chain 2, skip 2, hdc 6), then Rows 39–40 plain. Use a button about 2 cm across.

**Can I make it in two colours?** Yes — work the openwork and buttonhole rows in a contrast colour for two stripes that frame the texture. Or keep one colour and sew on a wooden button in a darker shade.

title: Crochet Headscarf with a Lace Edge
excerpt: Crochet a triangle headscarf with a shell-stitch lace edge and long cord ties — three ways to wear it, in breathable DK cotton.
image_alt: A woman wearing a handmade cream crochet headscarf with a shell-stitch lace edge, tied under the chin, outdoors in a garden.
content:
A crochet headscarf is the accessory that keeps coming back: a triangle of soft cotton that holds your hair on a windy day, shades your neck in summer, and ties three different ways — under the chin, at the nape, or as a bandana. It is worked from the point up in double crochet, with a shell-stitch lace edge and long cord ties, and you can finish it in an evening.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Increasing a triangle evenly, a shell-stitch lace edge, and cord ties worked back with slip stitch. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 47 cm wide and 31 cm deep, with two ties about 27 cm long. **Time:** about 3 hours.

Use DK cotton or a cotton-linen blend — cotton holds the lace edge crisply and breathes in warm weather.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream and sage-green DK cotton yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-headscarf-lace-edge-pattern-materials.webp)

DK cotton or cotton-linen blend yarn (#3): about 100 g in one colour, or 70 g main colour and 30 g contrast for the lace edge; a 4 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Shell:** 5 dc worked into one stitch. **Gauge:** 18 dc and 9 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. The triangle grows by 3 stitches every row, so check your gauge after Row 10 — if the triangle is much wider than 17 cm at that point, go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

Work from the point at the top down to the long edge, turning at the end of every row. The chain 3 at the start of each row counts as the first double crochet.

**Row 1:** Chain 4, 3 dc in the 4th chain from the hook (4).

**Row 2:** Chain 3, 2 dc in the first stitch, dc in each of the next 2 stitches, 2 dc in the last stitch (7).

**Row 3 onwards:** Chain 3, 2 dc in the first stitch, dc across to the last stitch, 2 dc in the last stitch. Each row adds 3 stitches: Row 10 has 31 stitches, Row 20 has 61, and Row 28 has 85. Work 28 rows in all. The triangle is now about 47 cm across the long edge and about 31 cm deep from point to edge. Do not fasten off.

**Ties:** At the corner where you finished Row 28, chain 55, then slip stitch in the 2nd chain from the hook and in each chain back to the corner, and slip stitch into the corner stitch. Fasten off. The cord is about 27 cm long and lies flat because it is worked back in slip stitch. Join yarn at the other top corner and work the second tie the same way.

![Close-up of a shell-stitch lace edge in cream cotton yarn on a crochet headscarf, showing the fanned double crochet shells and single crochet between them](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-headscarf-lace-edge-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Lace edge:** Join yarn at the point. Work 1 sc in the end of each row along the first slanted side (28 sc), 3 sc in the corner stitch, then 1 sc in the end of each row down the second side (28 sc). Do not turn. Shell round, worked back along the same sides: sc in the first sc, *skip 2 sc, 5 dc in the next sc, skip 2 sc, sc in the next sc; repeat from * to the point, ending with a shell in the last stitch — 5 shells along each side. Fasten off and weave in the ends.

**Three ways to tie it:** Under the chin — fold the long edge over your forehead, cross the ties under your chin and knot them at the nape. At the nape — wear the point at the back and knot the ties low behind your neck. As a bandana — fold the triangle in half lengthways and tie the ends at the nape, lace edge showing at the front.

## Styling and Care

Wear it with the lace edge framing your face and the point at the back, or turn it around so the point falls over one shoulder. It pairs with the winter shawl with pockets in cold weather and with a linen dress in summer. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat; pin the lace edge flat while it is damp so it holds its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I tie it so it stays?** Tie it under the chin for the firmest fit — the knot sits under your jaw and the triangle cannot slide back. For the nape tie, cross the cords once before knotting so they grip, and tuck the knot under the point. A couple of bobby pins through the folded edge and your hair hold it on a windy day.

**What yarn is best in summer?** Cotton or a cotton-linen blend. Cotton breathes, takes dye well, and the shell edge stays crisp in the heat. Linen blends are cooler still and soften beautifully, though they have less stretch — check your gauge, because a linen blend can work up a little narrower. Avoid wool for summer: it is too warm and the lace edge felts if it is washed hot.

**Can I make it smaller for a child?** Yes — work 22 rows instead of 28, which gives a triangle about 37 cm wide and 24 cm deep, and shorten the ties to chain 45. The same lace edge works, with 22 single crochet along each side and 4 shells instead of 5. For a toddler, work 18 rows and chain 40 ties.

**How do I wash it?** Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat, reshaping the triangle and pinning the lace edge while it is damp. Cotton can go in the dryer on low, but it shrinks a little on the first wash, so flat drying is safer. Do not iron the shells flat — steam them lightly from the wrong side if they need it.

title: Winter Shawl with Pockets: Free Crochet Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a pocket shawl in double crochet — 150 cm wide with pockets placed by your arm length, plus an optional fringe.
image_alt: A person wearing a handmade rust-red crochet pocket shawl with hands tucked into the pockets, outdoors in the snow.
content:
A pocket shawl is the wearable blanket that readers actually finish: a big rectangle of double crochet that drapes over your shoulders and keeps your hands warm in two deep pockets. The pockets are placed by your arm length, so they sit exactly where your hands fall, and the optional fringe finishes the short ends.

The trick is the size: wide enough to wrap right around you, long enough to cover your lap when you sit, and pockets deep enough for a phone or cold hands. Work it in one colour, or stripe it with leftover yarn.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A large rectangle in double crochet, pocket panels sewn on, placement by arm length, and an optional knotted fringe. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 150 cm wide and 71 cm long, pockets about 20 cm wide and 23 cm tall, fringe about 15 cm. **Time:** about 12 hours for the shawl, plus 1 hour per pocket and 1 hour for the fringe.

Use worsted yarn in any colour you like; a smooth yarn shows the double crochet texture and slides easily over a sweater.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of rust-red and cream worsted yarn with a 5.5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/winter-shawl-with-pockets-crochet-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): about 600 g in total — about 500 g for the shawl, about 35 g per pocket, about 30 g for the fringe; a 5.5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Gauge:** 12 dc and 7 rows measure 10 cm with a 5.5 mm hook. The shawl is a big piece, so check your gauge after Row 5 — if it is much wider than 75 cm at that point, the finished shawl will swallow you, so go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

Work the shawl body first, then the two pockets, then sew the pockets on and add the fringe last.

**Shawl body:** Chain 182. Row 1: dc in the 4th chain from the hook and across (180). Rows 2–50: chain 3, turn, dc across (180). Work 50 rows in all — the shawl is now about 150 cm wide and about 71 cm long. Fasten off and weave in the ends.

**Pocket (make 2):** Chain 26. Row 1: dc in the 4th chain from the hook and across (24). Rows 2–16: chain 3, turn, dc across (24) — each pocket is about 20 cm wide and 23 cm tall. Fasten off, leaving a tail about 60 cm long for sewing. Work 1 round of sc around the top edge of each pocket (24 sc) so the opening keeps its shape.

![Close-up of double crochet stitches and a sewn-on pocket in rust-red worsted yarn on a crochet shawl, showing the pocket seam and the straight top edge](https://cozyloops.site/assets/winter-shawl-with-pockets-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Pocket placement:** Lay the shawl flat, right side up. Measure your arm from shoulder to wrist — that is where your hands fall when the shawl is on. Pin each pocket with its bottom edge that far up from the short end, centred across the width (about 65 cm from each long edge).

| Arm length (shoulder to wrist) | Pocket bottom from the short end |
|---|---|
| Under 55 cm | 15 cm |
| 55–65 cm | 20 cm |
| Over 65 cm | 25 cm |

**Sewing the pockets on:** Sew each pocket to the shawl along the two sides and the bottom with small whip stitches through both layers, using the long tail — leave the top edge open. Take small, even stitches about 5 mm apart so the seam lies flat and the pocket cannot gap. Sew through the tops of the stitches, not between them, so the seam does not show on the right side.

**Fringe (optional):** Cut 180 strands of yarn, each 30 cm long. Fold one strand in half, push the loop through the first stitch of a short end from the wrong side, pull the two ends through the loop and tighten — a lark's head knot. Work 1 strand in every second stitch along each short end (90 strands per end). The fringe hangs about 15 cm. Trim the ends straight.

## Styling and Care

Wear it over your shoulders with the pockets at the front, or wrap it once around your neck like a giant scarf. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat — press it in a towel first and never hang it up wet, or it stretches.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long should the shawl be?** About 71 cm long and 150 cm wide, as written — that covers your shoulders and your lap when you sit. If you are petite, work 44 rows instead of 50 (about 63 cm long); if you are tall, work 56 rows (about 80 cm). Keep the width at 180 stitches either way, or the pockets will not sit centred.

**Are the pockets deep enough for a phone?** Yes — each pocket is about 20 cm wide and 23 cm tall, and a phone is about 16 cm tall, so it fits with room to spare. A paperback, a skein of yarn, or gloves fit too. The single crochet round around the top edge stops the opening stretching, so the phone does not slide out when you bend over.

**Can I skip the fringe?** Yes — the shawl is finished without it. Work 1 round of single crochet along each short end instead (180 sc per end) for a clean edge that stops the double crochet curling. The fringe is decoration only; leaving it off saves about an hour and 30 g of yarn.

**How do I stop the pockets sagging?** Sew them with small, close whip stitches through both layers, and do not overload them — a phone and a hand is fine, a full water bottle is not. The single crochet round around the top edge firms the opening so the pocket keeps its shape. If a pocket still sags, sew a second row of stitches 5 mm inside the first.

title: Granny Square Vest: Free Crochet Pattern (Sizes S–XL)
excerpt: Crochet a structured vest from just 12 classic granny squares — full S–XL size chart, join-as-you-go, and shaped armholes and neckline.
image_alt: A woman wearing a handmade red, cream and sage green granny square vest over a white T-shirt, outdoors in a garden.
content:
A granny square does not have to become a blanket. Twelve squares, joined edge to edge, make a structured vest you can wear over a shirt all winter — the granny-square revival as wearable fashion, not a throw for the sofa. This one is built from just twelve classic squares, with a full size chart from S to XL and a join-as-you-go option, so there is no pile of seams to sew at the end. Unlike the site's summer-tops guide, which leaves the sizing adaptable, this is a single structured garment with exact square counts and shaped armholes and neckline.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** The classic granny square, join-as-you-go, and armhole and neckline shaping. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** size S: back 40 cm wide, 60 cm long. **Time:** about 8 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red, cream and sage green worsted yarn with a 5 mm crochet hook, scissors and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/granny-square-vest-free-crochet-pattern-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in three colours — A red, B cream, C sage green: about 350 g in total for size S (A about 50 g, B about 100 g, C about 200 g); a 5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle and scissors.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Cluster:** 3 dc worked into one space. **Gauge:** one square worked to Round 5 measures about 15 cm across, and each round adds about 2.5 cm.

## Sizes

The numbers below are for size S; the other sizes change only the round count of each square.

| Size | To fit bust | Square rounds | Square size | Back width | Length | Yarn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S | 86–91 cm | 7 | 20 cm | 40 cm | 60 cm | about 350 g |
| M | 96–101 cm | 8 | 22 cm | 44 cm | 66 cm | about 400 g |
| L | 106–111 cm | 9 | 25 cm | 50 cm | 75 cm | about 450 g |
| XL | 116–121 cm | 10 | 27 cm | 54 cm | 81 cm | about 500 g |

## The Pattern

**The square (make 12):** Each round adds one cluster per side: Round 1 has 4 clusters (12 dc), Round 7 has 28 (84 dc).

Round 1: Chain 4 and join to form a ring. Chain 3 (counts as a dc), 2 dc in the ring, chain 2, (3 dc in the ring, chain 2) 3 times, join to the chain-3. (4 clusters, 12 dc.)

Round 2: Slip stitch to the first corner space. Chain 3, then work (3 dc, chain 2, 3 dc) in each corner space. (8 clusters, 24 dc.)

Round 3: Chain 3, work (3 dc, chain 2, 3 dc) in each corner and 3 dc in each side space. (12 clusters, 36 dc.)

Rounds 4–7: Continue, adding one cluster per side each round — R4: 2 per side (16 clusters, 48 dc); R5: 3 (20, 60); R6: 4 (24, 72); R7: 5 (28, 84). Stop at your size: M R8 (32, 96), L R9 (36, 108), XL R10 (40, 120).

**Colour plan:** Rounds 1–2 in colour A, Rounds 3–4 in colour B, Round 5 to the end in colour C. Change colour at the start of a round.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet granny square in red, cream and sage green yarn, showing the classic three double-crochet clusters and chain corners](https://cozyloops.site/assets/granny-square-vest-free-crochet-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Layout:** Lay the twelve squares flat — the back panel is 2 squares wide and 3 tall (6 squares), and each front panel is 1 square wide and 3 tall (3 squares each).

**Joining:** Join the squares as you go: on the last round of each new square, work the side that touches a finished square with a slip stitch into the matching stitch of its neighbour — chain 1, slip stitch into the next stitch of the finished square, chain 1 — instead of a plain chain space, and at the corners, chain 1, slip stitch into the neighbour's corner, chain 1.

**Shaping:** Seam each front panel to the back panel up the sides for two squares, leaving the top square open as the armhole. Seam the top edges together for the outer two-thirds, about 13 cm on size S, leaving the centre open as the neckline, about 14 cm wide. Work 1 round of single crochet around each armhole and 2 rounds around the whole outer edge in colour C, plus 1 round around the neckline.

## Styling and Care

Wear it open over a shirt or a tee, or close it at the waist with a brooch or a tie. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat, reshaping the squares while the vest is damp.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I size the squares?** By the round count in the size table — each round adds about 2.5 cm, so a size S square has 7 rounds and measures about 20 cm. Check one square at Round 5: if it measures more than 16 cm across, go down half a hook size.

**Can I use scrap yarn?** Yes — that is the point of a granny vest. Keep the same three-colour plan on every square so the vest reads as one garment, and use the same yarn weight throughout, or the squares will not match in size.

**How do I join the squares invisibly?** Join as you go with slip stitches, matching stitch for stitch along the shared edge, and the join disappears into the last round. If you sew, whip stitch through the back loops only with a matching colour.

**What if I am between sizes?** Work the larger square size and take the side seams in by one cluster on each side, or work the smaller size and add one round of double crochet around the whole vest as a border. The vest is worn open, so the back width is the measurement to get right.

title: Spiral Crochet Sweater: A Beginner's Guide
excerpt: Crochet a spiral colourwork sweater in continuous double crochet — no-tangle yarn management, a split yoke, and sewn-in sleeves.
image_alt: A person wearing a handmade cream, rust red and teal spiral-striped crochet sweater, outdoors in a park.
content:
A spiral sweater looks far harder than it is. The stripes wind around the body because the whole sweater is worked in one continuous spiral — no joining rounds, no seams in the body, just double crochet round after round, changing colour every two rounds. The only trick is keeping three balls of yarn from tangling — see below. This version keeps it beginner-friendly: a straight body, a split yoke, and sewn-in sleeves.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Working in a continuous spiral, colour changes without joining, splitting a tube for the yoke, sewing in sleeves. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** size S, body about 96 cm around and 58 cm long. **Time:** about 15 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream, rust red and teal DK yarn with a 4.5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/spiral-crochet-sweater-beginner-guide-materials.webp)

DK yarn (#3) in three colours — A cream, B rust red, C teal: about 400 g in total for size S (A about 200 g, B about 100 g, C about 100 g); a 4.5 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle, scissors and stitch markers; three small bags or bowls.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Decrease:** dc2tog (yarn over, pull up a loop in each of the next 2 stitches, yarn over, pull through all 3 loops). **Gauge:** 16 dc and 9 rows measure 10 cm with a 4.5 mm hook.

## Sizes

Numbers below are for size S; other sizes change only the stitch counts.

| Size | To fit bust | Body stitches | Body to underarm | Sleeve start | Yarn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S | 86–91 cm | 154 | 38 cm (34 rows) | 56 | about 400 g |
| M | 96–101 cm | 170 | 40 cm (36 rows) | 60 | about 450 g |
| L | 106–111 cm | 186 | 42 cm (38 rows) | 64 | about 550 g |
| XL | 116–121 cm | 202 | 44 cm (40 rows) | 68 | about 600 g |

## The Pattern

**Body:** Chain 154 and join without twisting. Round 1: chain 3 (counts as a dc), dc in each chain around — 154 dc. Do not join: mark the first dc and keep working in a continuous spiral, moving the marker up each round.

**The spiral:** Change colour every 2 rounds — 2 in A, 2 in B, 2 in C, then back to A — joining the new colour at the marker. Keep the marker at the side so the steps sit under the arm.

**No-tangle yarn management:** Keep each ball in its own bag or bowl, feeding from the top, and work from the centre-pull end of one ball and the outside end of the next.

Work until the body measures 38 cm — 34 rounds on size S — then fasten off.

![Close-up of spiral colourwork crochet in cream, rust red and teal DK yarn, showing double crochet stitches in diagonal stripes](https://cozyloops.site/assets/spiral-crochet-sweater-beginner-guide-closeup.webp)

**Yoke — front:** Count off 77 stitches for the front and 77 for the back. Join yarn at the start of the front. Rows 1–12: chain 3, dc across (77), turn. Row 13: chain 3, dc 25 (26 stitches), turn — the left shoulder. Rows 14–17: chain 3, dc across, working a dc2tog at the neck edge each row — 25, 24, 23, 22. Fasten off. Work the right shoulder the same from the other edge. The centre 25 stitches stay unworked — that is the neckline.

Other sizes: shoulders 30 (M), 34 (L) or 38 (XL) stitches wide, decreasing 1 at the neck edge on each of the last 4 shoulder rows.

**Yoke — back:** Rows 1–13: chain 3, dc across (77), turn. Row 14: chain 3, dc 25 (26), turn — the left shoulder. Rows 15–18: chain 3, dc across, decreasing 1 at the neck edge each row, to 22. Fasten off. Work the right shoulder the same. The back neckline starts one row later, so it sits higher. Whip stitch the front shoulders to the back shoulders, 22 stitches each, through the back loops only.

**Sleeves (make 2):** Chain 58 and join without twisting. Round 1: chain 3, dc in each chain around (56 dc). Work the same spiral and colours as the body. Decrease 2 stitches on every 6th round — a dc2tog on opposite sides on Rounds 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 — tapering from 56 stitches to 44. Work 40 rounds, about 44 cm, then 4 rounds of single crochet for the cuff (44 stitches). Fasten off. (M: 60 to 48; L: 64 to 52; XL: 68 to 56.) Sew each sleeve into its armhole, easing the fuller sleeve top evenly around the opening.

**Neckline:** Work 1 round of single crochet evenly around the neck opening in colour A.

## Styling and Care

Wear it with jeans. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat — never hang it up wet, or the spiral stretches out of shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I stop the yarns tangling?** Give each ball its own bag or bowl, work from the centre-pull end of one and the outside end of the next, and lift the work every few rounds so the balls spin themselves untangled. Fasten off each colour when its two rounds are done — carried floats tangle and catch.

**Is it really beginner-friendly?** Yes — the whole sweater is double crochet, and the only new skills are working in a spiral and decreasing at the neckline. There is no increasing, no short rows and no body shaping.

**What sizes does it cover?** S to XL, for busts from 86 to 121 cm, with the body about 5 cm larger than the bust it fits. Between sizes, make the smaller one — double crochet stretches.

**Can I make it with 2 colours instead of 3?** Yes — alternate A and B every 2 rounds and the spiral still shows; use about 250 g of A and 150 g of B for size S.

title: Crochet Polo Shirt: A Modern Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a modern polo shirt in single crochet — short-row collar, button placket, men's and women's sizes S–XL, with a short-sleeve option.
image_alt: A woman wearing a handmade cream crochet polo shirt with a collar and button placket, outdoors in a garden.
content:
A crochet polo shirt makes handmade look smart: a collared shirt in breathable cotton, with a button placket and a short-row collar. It is worked in single crochet, the densest stitch, so the collar keeps its shape. It comes in men's and women's sizes S to XL, with long sleeves and a short-sleeve option.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Single crochet fabric, a short-row collar, a button placket, and set-in sleeves. **Skill level:** Intermediate. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** size S: 96 cm around, 56 cm long. **Time:** about 14 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream and navy cotton DK yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, three buttons, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-polo-shirt-modern-pattern-materials.webp)

Cotton DK yarn (#3) in two colours — A main, B contrast for the collar and bands: about 400 g of A and 50 g of B for size S, plus 50 g of A per size up; a 4 mm hook; three 1.5 cm buttons; a yarn needle, scissors and a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Decrease:** sc2tog (pull up a loop in each of the next 2 stitches, yarn over, pull through all 3 loops). **Gauge:** 18 sc and 22 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Check your gauge after 10 rows — if 10 stitches measure over 5.5 cm, go down half a hook size.

## Sizes

Numbers are for size S; other sizes change only the stitch counts.

| Size | Bust (women) | Chest (men) | Body stitches | Length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S | 86–91 cm | 91–96 cm | 172 | 56 cm |
| M | 96–101 cm | 101–106 cm | 192 | 58 cm |
| L | 106–111 cm | 111–116 cm | 208 | 60 cm |
| XL | 116–121 cm | 121–126 cm | 228 | 62 cm |

## The Pattern

Work the back and front panels separately, flat in rows, then seam them.

**Back panel:** Chain 87. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (86). Rows 2–120: chain 1, turn, sc across (86). Shape the neck on the last 3 rows: work the first 20 stitches for 3 rows, fasten off, skip 46, join yarn and work 3 rows of 20 for the second shoulder.

**Front panel:** Chain 87. Rows 1–88: sc across (86). Split for the placket: Row 89: sc 43, turn, and work this half only. Rows 90–111: decrease 1 at the neck edge every row (43 to 20). Rows 112–123: sc across (20). Fasten off. Join yarn at the centre and work the right half the same.

Other sizes: split after row 93 (M), 97 (L), 101 (XL); halves 48, 52, 57 stitches, decreasing 26, 28, 30 rows to shoulders of 22, 24, 27; back neck skips 52, 56, 60 stitches.

**Seams:** Sew the shoulders (20 stitches each side) and the side seams from the hem to the underarm (75 rows on size S).

**Sleeves (make 2):** Chain 37. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (36). Rows 2–3: sc in the back loop only for a ribbed cuff. Increase 2 stitches every 4th row, one at each end, 22 times, to 80 stitches. Rows 89–99: sc across (80); the sleeve is about 45 cm long. Fasten off, sew the sleeve seam, then sew each sleeve into its armhole, easing the top evenly around the opening. Other sizes: M 38 to 84 (23 increases); L 40 to 88 (24); XL 42 to 92 (25 increases, 100 rows).

**Placket bands:** Work 3 rows of sc along each slit edge. Rows 1–2: sc 35. Row 3 (left band only): sc 5, (chain 2, skip 2, sc 8) 3 times for three buttonholes; the right band stays plain sc. Sew the three buttons on the right band opposite the buttonholes.

![Close-up of a crochet polo collar with short-row shaping and a button placket with three buttons, in cream cotton yarn, showing single crochet stitches](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-polo-shirt-modern-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Collar:** Join yarn at the top of the left placket band. Row 1: sc evenly around the neck opening — up the left slope, across the back neck, down the right slope — about 96 stitches on size S. Turn. Short rows across the back: work 68 stitches, turn, then 64, 60, 56, 52, turning each time. Each row leaves a few stitches unworked at each end, so the collar stands taller at the back. Row 7: sc across all stitches. Row 8: sc back across. Row 9: join colour B and sc across for a neat edge. Fasten off.

## Styling and Care

Wear it with jeans or chinos. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat, reshaping the collar while damp so it stands up. Do not iron the collar flat — steam it lightly from the wrong side.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I shape the collar?** With short rows: each row is 4 stitches shorter than the last, so the back of the neck gets more rows than the ends — that is what makes it stand up at the back. The exact turning stitch does not matter; keep the unworked stitches roughly even at both ends.

**What yarn keeps the collar crisp?** Cotton DK — it holds a fold and does not go limp the way a soft acrylic or wool blend does. The contrast edge round firms the outer edge. Wash cold and dry flat; a tumble-dried collar will flop.

**Can I make it short-sleeved?** Yes — work the sleeves for 40 rows instead of 99: chain 41, work 40 stitches, increase 2 stitches every 2nd row, 16 times, to 72 stitches. The short sleeve is about 18 cm long. (Other sizes: M 42 to 74, L 44 to 76, XL 46 to 78.)

**What if my collar flops forward?** Work the short rows as written — a collar worked straight across has nothing holding it up. Check that you used cotton, not a drapey yarn, and work the contrast edge round slightly tighter. Steam the collar while damp and pin it upright until it dries.

title: Granny Square Cardigan with Pockets
excerpt: Crochet a longline granny square cardigan with real inset pockets — 42 squares joined as you go, drop shoulders, and deep pockets.
image_alt: A woman wearing a handmade sage green and cream granny square cardigan with hands in the pockets, outdoors in autumn.
content:
A granny square cardigan is the cosy layer the vest leaves you wanting: the same squares, joined as you go, but longline with sleeves and real inset pockets — a bag behind a slit opening in each front panel, not appliqued patches. Unlike the site's granny vest, a sleeveless twelve-square garment, this is a longline cardigan of forty-two squares with drop shoulders.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** The classic granny square, join-as-you-go, inset pockets, and drop-shoulder sleeves. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** size S: 95 cm around, 90 cm long. **Time:** about 20 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of sage green and cream worsted yarn with a 5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/granny-square-cardigan-pockets-crochet-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in two colours — A main, B contrast for the last round and the edging: about 1,000 g of A and 100 g of B for size S, plus 100 g of A per size up; a 5 mm hook; a needle, scissors and a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc). **Cluster:** 3 dc in one space. **Gauge:** one square to Round 5 measures about 15 cm across; each round adds about 2.5 cm. For sleeves and bags, 14 dc and 8 rows measure 10 cm.

## Sizes

Numbers are for size S; other sizes change only the square counts.

| Size | To fit bust | Squares (back / each front) | Body around |
|---|---|---|---|
| S | 86–91 cm | 18 / 12 | 95 cm |
| M | 96–101 cm | 24 / 12 | 110 cm |
| L | 106–111 cm | 30 / 12 | 125 cm |
| XL | 116–121 cm | 36 / 12 | 140 cm |

The fit is relaxed and oversized, with 10–20 cm of positive ease — size down if you prefer less.

## The Pattern

**The square (make 42 on size S):** Each round adds one cluster per side: 4 clusters (12 dc) on Round 1, 20 (60 dc) on Round 5. Round 1: Chain 4, join into a ring. Chain 3 (counts as a dc), 2 dc in the ring, chain 2, (3 dc in the ring, chain 2) 3 times, join. Rounds 2–5: slip stitch to a corner, work (3 dc, chain 2, 3 dc) in each corner and 3 dc in each side space — R2: 8 clusters (24 dc); R3: 12 (36); R4: 16 (48); R5: 20 (60). Rounds 1–4 in A, Round 5 in B.

![Close-up of granny squares joined as you go with a pocket opening in the front panel, in sage green and cream yarn, showing the classic three double-crochet clusters](https://cozyloops.site/assets/granny-square-cardigan-pockets-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Layout:** Lay the squares flat: back 3 wide and 6 tall, each front 2 wide and 6 tall.

**Joining:** Join the squares as you go: on the last round of each new square, join each side to its finished neighbour with slip stitches (chain 1, slip stitch into the matching stitch, chain 1) instead of a plain chain space. Or sew: whip stitch through the back loops only. Make three panels first, then join them at the shoulders.

**Shoulders:** Seam each front's outer square to the back's outer squares, 15 cm each side. The remaining back top edge is the neckline — wide by design, drawn in by the edging.

**Side seams:** Sew the side seams from the hem up 4 square rows (60 cm), leaving the top 2 rows (30 cm) open as the armholes.

**Sleeves (make 2):** Chain 53. Row 1: dc in the 4th chain from the hook and across (50). Rows 2–3: dc in the back loop only for a ribbed cuff. Increase 2 stitches every 2nd row, one at each end, 17 times, to 84 stitches, then work even to row 38. The sleeve is about 47 cm long, 60 cm around at the top. Fasten off, sew the seam, then sew each sleeve into its armhole. Other sizes: M 52 to 86; L 54 to 88; XL 56 to 90.

**Pockets (make 2 bags):** Chain 31. Row 1: dc in the 4th chain from the hook and across (28). Rows 2–18: chain 3, turn, dc across (28), making a bag about 20 by 22 cm. When joining the fronts, leave the join between square rows 2 and 3 unworked for one square's width (15 cm) in each front's outer square: the pocket opening, 30 cm above the hem. Sew a bag behind each opening on three sides, then work 1 round of sc around it.

**Edging:** Work 2 rounds of sc in colour B around the outer edge. On the first round, work 2 stitches together every 4th stitch across the back neckline to draw it in, and 1 round of sc around each cuff.

## Styling and Care

Wear it open, or close it with a belt. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat — never hang it up wet, or it stretches. Reshape the pockets while damp, pushing the bags flat.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long is the longline version?** 90 cm from shoulder to hem — six squares tall. Shorten it with 5-square panels (75 cm); lengthen it with 7 (105 cm) — allow about 150 g of yarn per extra row.

**Are the pockets big enough?** Yes — the opening is 15 cm wide and the bag 20 by 22 cm, so a phone, keys and hands fit. The single crochet round around the opening stops the slit stretching.

**How do I stop it stretching?** Use worsted with a 5 mm hook — a bigger hook makes a looser fabric that grows. The seams and the edging stabilise the shape. Always dry it flat, never hang it up wet, and do not overload the pockets.

**What if my squares come out different sizes?** Check your gauge: one square to Round 5 should measure 15 cm. If yours are bigger, go down half a hook size; if smaller, go up. Block every square to 15 cm before joining — pin it out, steam lightly, let it dry.

title: Crochet Co-ord Set: Shorts and Crop Top
excerpt: Crochet a matching shorts-and-crop-top set in cotton DK — mesh top, solid shorts with a drawstring waist, one shared stitch and a full size chart.
image_alt: A woman wearing a handmade cream crochet co-ord set — mesh crop top and shorts with a drawstring waist — outdoors in summer.
content:
A matching set is the easiest outfit decision you will make all summer: one stitch pattern, one yarn, two pieces that work together or on their own. This co-ord set pairs a mesh crop top with solid shorts — the top is mesh all over, and the shorts carry a mesh band at each leg hem, so the set reads as one garment. It is worked in breathable cotton DK, with a drawstring waist and a full size chart from S to XL.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Mesh stitch, working in the round, and a folded drawstring casing. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** size S: top about 96 cm around and 30 cm long; shorts about 95 cm around the hip, inseam about 12 cm. **Time:** about 10 hours.

Use cotton DK in two colours — a main for the body of each piece and a contrast for the bands and straps. Cotton holds the mesh crisply and breathes in warm weather.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream and sage green cotton DK yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and cotton cord on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-coord-set-shorts-crop-top-materials.webp)

Cotton DK yarn (#3) in two colours — A main cream, B contrast sage green: about 500 g in total for size S (A about 350 g, B about 150 g); a 4 mm hook; a yarn needle, scissors, a tape measure; about 120 cm of cotton cord for the drawstring, or a chain-stitched cord.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc), half double crochet (hdc). **Mesh:** dc, chain 1, skip 1 stitch. **Gauge:** mesh — 7 meshes (14 stitches) and 8 rows measure 10 cm; solid hdc — 16 stitches and 11 rows measure 10 cm. Check your gauge after 5 rounds.

## Sizes

| Size | To fit bust | Top meshes | Top around | Shorts hip stitches | Shorts hip |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S | 86–91 cm | 67 | about 96 cm | 152 | about 95 cm |
| M | 96–101 cm | 74 | about 106 cm | 164 | about 103 cm |
| L | 106–111 cm | 81 | about 116 cm | 180 | about 112 cm |
| XL | 116–121 cm | 88 | about 126 cm | 192 | about 120 cm |

## The Pattern

**Top (size S):** Chain 134 and join without twisting. Round 1: chain 3 (counts as a dc), dc in each chain around (134). Round 2: chain 4 (counts as dc and chain 1), skip 1, dc, *chain 1, skip 1, dc; repeat from * around — 67 meshes. Join to the third chain of the starting chain-4. Rounds 3–24: repeat the mesh round — 24 mesh rounds in all, about 30 cm long. Round 25: sc around (134) and fasten off.

**Top edging:** Work 1 round of sc in colour B around the bottom edge (134 sc).

**Straps (make 2):** Chain 60. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (59). Work 2 more rows of sc (59) and fasten off. Each strap is about 33 cm long and 2 cm wide. Sew one end to the front top edge and the other to the back, about 12 cm apart on each side.

![Close-up of mesh crochet stitches in cream cotton yarn, showing the open diamond mesh and double crochet](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-coord-set-shorts-crop-top-closeup.webp)

**Shorts (size S):** Chain 152 and join without twisting. Rounds 1–4: chain 2 (counts as an hdc), hdc around (152). This is the waistband — fold the top 2 rounds inside and whip stitch them down, leaving a 3 cm gap at the back for the drawstring. Rounds 5–22: hdc around (152), 18 rounds in all — the body is now about 16 cm deep.

**Legs:** Round 23: divide in half. Work 76 hdc and join to the first stitch of the round — the left leg. Work 12 rounds of hdc (76 stitches, about 11 cm), then a mesh band: work 2 mesh rounds (38 meshes each), then 1 round of sc. Fasten off. Work the right leg the same from the remaining 76 stitches.

**Drawstring:** Cut 120 cm of cotton cord, or chain 200 and slip stitch back. Thread it through the casing and knot the ends.

## Styling and Care

Wear the set together, or split it up — top over jeans, shorts with a plain tee. The mesh top is open by design, so wear it over a camisole or a bralette. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat; pin the hem straight while it is damp so the mesh holds its shape.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I size the shorts?** By your hip measurement — the table gives the hip for each size, and the drawstring waist cinches down to fit waists well below the hip size. Measure around the fullest part of your hips; between sizes, size down — the drawstring takes up the slack.

**Is the top lined?** No — the mesh is open by design, and lining it would lose the airy feel that makes it a summer top. Wear it over a camisole, a bralette, or a fitted vest. For more coverage, work the first 10 rounds in solid double crochet, then switch to mesh.

**What yarn is best for summer?** Cotton DK — it breathes, takes dye well, and the mesh stays crisp in the heat. A cotton-linen blend is cooler still, though it has less stretch, so check your gauge. Avoid wool for summer — it is too warm — and avoid a slippery acrylic, which sags.

**Can I make the top longer?** Yes — add mesh rounds before the final sc round. Eight mesh rounds add about 10 cm, so add 4 rounds for 5 cm longer, and allow about 30 g of extra yarn per 5 cm. Keep the straps the same length.

title: Heart Granny Square Shrug: 14 Squares, One Sweater
excerpt: Crochet a shrug from just 14 heart granny squares — heart centres, a 7-by-2 layout, sleeves formed by the fold, sized by your square.
image_alt: A woman wearing a handmade cream and dusty pink heart granny square shrug with sleeves, outdoors in spring.
content:
A shrug from fourteen squares is the fastest sweater-shaped thing you will ever crochet: no body shaping, no set-in sleeves, just a rectangle of heart granny squares that folds into sleeves. The heart sits in the centre of every square, framed in a contrast colour, and the sizing comes from the square itself — one more round per square grows the whole shrug. Unlike the site's granny vest (sleeveless, twelve squares) and the longline cardigan (forty-two squares, inset pockets), this is a short open shrug: fourteen squares, sleeves from the fold.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A heart motif, squaring a motif, join-as-you-go, and folding a rectangle into a shrug. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** size M: about 105 cm wide, sleeves about 30 cm, body opening about 45 cm. **Time:** about 12 hours.

Use worsted in two colours — hearts and frames — so the motif reads clearly.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream and dusty pink worsted yarn with a 5 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure and a yarn needle on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/heart-granny-square-shrug-crochet-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4) in two colours — A dusty pink for the hearts, B cream for the frames: about 600 g in total for size M (A about 200 g, B about 400 g); a 5 mm hook, a yarn needle, scissors, a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc), double crochet (dc), treble crochet (tr). **Cluster:** 3 dc in one space. **Gauge:** one square to Round 6 measures about 15 cm across; each round adds about 2 cm. Check one square at Round 5 — if it measures more than 13.5 cm across, go down half a hook size.

## Sizes

| Size | Square rounds | Square size | Body opening | Sleeve length | Total width |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S | 5 | about 13 cm | about 39 cm | about 26 cm | about 91 cm |
| M | 6 | about 15 cm | about 45 cm | about 30 cm | about 105 cm |
| L | 7 | about 17 cm | about 51 cm | about 34 cm | about 119 cm |

## The Pattern

**The square (make 14):** Work the heart in colour A, then the frame in colour B.

Round 1 (A): Make a magic ring. Chain 3 (counts as a dc), 2 dc in the ring, chain 2, 3 tr in the ring, chain 2, 1 tr in the ring — the point — chain 2, 3 dc in the ring, chain 2, 3 tr in the ring, chain 2, join to the top of the chain-3. (13 stitches, 5 chain-2 spaces: two lobes at the top, one point at the bottom.)

Round 2 (A): Chain 1, sc in each stitch and 2 sc in each chain-2 space, 2 sc in the point stitch — 24 sc. Join.

Round 3 (B): Join B in any sc. Chain 3 (counts as a dc), dc in the next 4 sc, (2 dc, chain 2, 2 dc) in the next sc — the first corner. *Dc in the next 5 sc, (2 dc, chain 2, 2 dc) in the next sc; repeat from * twice more. Join. (12 clusters, 36 dc: 3 per side, with a chain-2 at each corner.)

Round 4: Chain 3, dc in each dc, (2 dc, chain 2, 2 dc) in each corner space. (16 clusters, 48 dc.)

Rounds 5–7: Continue the same way, adding one cluster per side each round — R5: 20 clusters (60 dc); R6: 24 (72); R7: 28 (84). Stop at your size (S R5, M R6, L R7) and fasten off, leaving a tail.

**Layout and joining:** Lay the fourteen squares flat — 7 wide and 2 tall — and join as you go: on the last round of each new square, join each side that touches a finished square with a slip stitch into the matching stitch — chain 1, slip stitch, chain 1 — instead of a plain chain space; at the corners, chain 1, slip stitch into the neighbour's corner, chain 1. Or sew: whip stitch through the back loops only.

![Close-up of a heart granny square in cream and dusty pink yarn, showing the heart centre and the square frame with chain corners](https://cozyloops.site/assets/heart-granny-square-shrug-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Folding into a shrug:** Fold the rectangle in half along the long centre line, wrong sides together — now 7 wide and 1 deep, doubled. Seam the outer 2 squares on each short end together through both layers: the sleeves. Leave the centre 3 squares open: the body opening.

**Cuffs and edging:** Work 2 rounds of sc in B around each sleeve opening, and 2 rounds around the whole body opening — front edges and neckline — so nothing curls.

## Styling and Care

Wear it open over a tee or a dress, hearts showing at the back. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat, reshaping the squares while damp. Block each square before joining, or the shrug will pull unevenly.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Can I make it a full sweater?** Yes — work 14 more squares as a second 7-by-2 panel below the body opening, and add 1 square to each sleeve end (4 squares). That is 32 squares in all.

**How do I size the squares?** By the round count in the table — each round adds about 2 cm, so a size S square has 5 rounds and measures about 13 cm. Check one square at Round 5: over 13.5 cm, go down half a hook size; under 12.5 cm, go up.

**What if my squares come out different sizes?** Block every square to the table size before joining — pin it out, steam lightly, let it dry. Joining unblocked squares is what makes a shrug pull to one side. If one square is still off, put it at the centre back.

**Can I make it in one colour?** Yes — the heart still shows as texture, though more quietly. Use the same yarn throughout, about 600 g for size M. A slow-changing variegated yarn works well too.

title: Coffee Cup Cozy with a Button: 30-Minute Crochet Gift
excerpt: Crochet a coffee cup cozy in 30 minutes — cotton worsted, a ribbed edge, and a button closure that fits standard takeaway cups.
image_alt: A handmade rust-red crochet coffee cup cozy with a wooden button on a white takeaway coffee cup, on a wooden table.
content:
A takeaway coffee is too hot to hold comfortably, and a paper sleeve is thrown away in minutes. A crochet cup cozy solves both problems: a band of cotton that slips around the cup, fastens with a button, and folds flat into a pocket when you are done. It takes about 30 minutes and a scrap of cotton yarn, which makes it the quickest gift on this calendar — one ball makes two, and a set of four takes an evening.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Half double crochet, a ribbed edge in front and back post stitches, and a chain button loop. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** medium about 22 cm around and 9 cm tall. **Time:** about 30 minutes.

Use cotton worsted yarn — cotton insulates against the heat and survives the washing machine, where acrylic goes limp and wool felts.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of rust-red cotton worsted yarn with a 4.5 mm crochet hook, a wooden button, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/coffee-cup-cozy-button-crochet-materials.webp)

Cotton worsted yarn (#4): about 25 g in one colour; a 4.5 mm crochet hook; one button about 2 cm across; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), half double crochet (hdc), front post double crochet (fpdc), back post double crochet (bpdc). **Gauge:** 14 hdc and 10 rows measure 10 cm with a 4.5 mm hook. Check your gauge after 3 rows — if 14 stitches measure more than 10.5 cm across, go down half a hook size.

## Sizes

Measure around your cup at the height the cozy will sit, about 8 cm up from the base — takeaway cups taper, so the top is wider than the bottom. The band is worked about 1 cm shorter than the cup on purpose: cotton half double crochet stretches to fit, and the button loop adds the last bit of reach.

| Cup | Cup around | Chain | Stitches | Band length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small, 8 oz / 240 ml | about 20 cm | 29 | 27 hdc | about 19 cm |
| Medium, 12 oz / 350 ml | about 23 cm | 33 | 31 hdc | about 22 cm |
| Large, 16 oz / 470 ml | about 25 cm | 36 | 34 hdc | about 24 cm |

All three sizes are 9 rows tall, about 9 cm.

## The Pattern

The numbers below are for size medium; the other sizes change only the starting chain.

**Band:** Chain 33. Row 1: hdc in the 3rd chain from the hook and across (31). Rows 2–9: chain 2, turn, hdc across (31). The band is now about 22 cm long and 9 cm tall. Do not fasten off.

**Ribbed edge:** Turn, and work along the top edge: chain 2, *fpdc in the next stitch, bpdc in the next stitch; repeat from * to the end — 16 fpdc and 15 bpdc. Fasten off. Join yarn at a bottom corner and work the same ribbed row along the foundation chain — 16 fpdc and 15 bpdc. The two ribbed edges grip the cup and stop the cozy sliding down.

![Close-up of a ribbed edge in rust-red cotton yarn on a coffee cup cozy, showing front post and back post half double crochet stitches](https://cozyloops.site/assets/coffee-cup-cozy-button-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Button loop:** Join yarn at a top corner of one short end. Chain 6, slip stitch into the same corner stitch — a loop that fits a 2 cm button. Fasten off.

**Button:** Sew the button at the top corner of the other short end, on the outside of the band. Wrap the band around the cup and push the button through the loop.

## Styling and Care

Slip the cozy on from the top of the cup and button it at the side, with the button clear of your fingers. It folds flat, so it fits in a coat pocket or a bag. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat — cotton can shrink a little on the first wash, so wash the cozy before you gift it and it will keep its fit. Do not tumble dry it: heat makes cotton tighten and the band will no longer stretch around the cup.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Will it fit my reusable cup?** Measure around the cup at the height the cozy sits, about 8 cm up from the base, and pick the size whose cup measurement matches. Between sizes, go down — the band stretches about 1 cm. Reusable cups vary a lot in taper, so measure first rather than guessing by ounces: a wide 12 oz travel mug can need the large size.

**How do I wash it?** Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat, reshaping it while it is damp. Cotton absorbs coffee drips and washes clean, but a hot wash or a tumble dryer will shrink it. If it does shrink, soak it in cool water, stretch it back around a cup, and let it dry on the cup.

**Can I make a set of four?** Yes — about 100 g of cotton makes four medium cozies. Work them in four colours from the same yarn range, or stripe the leftovers from other projects. Each one needs its own button, and matching buttons across the set make it look bought, not improvised.

**Can I make it without the button?** Yes — join the band into a tube instead: slip stitch the two short ends together and slip the cozy on from the top of the cup. It works the same way, but it no longer folds flat and you cannot adjust it, so check the fit against the cup before you join.

title: Mug Rug with a Heart Motif
excerpt: Crochet a mug rug with a heart in the middle — single crochet colourwork, a 9-by-7 heart chart, and a gift set of two.
image_alt: A handmade cream crochet mug rug with a dusty pink heart motif, with a white mug of coffee and a teaspoon on it, by a sunny window.
content:
A mug rug is a coaster with room to spare: big enough for a mug and a teaspoon, small enough to finish in under an hour from a scrap of cotton. This one has a heart worked into the middle in a second colour, and it makes a gift set of two — one for each end of the sofa, or one to keep and one to give away.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Single crochet colourwork, reading a chart written as text, and a single crochet border. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 15 cm wide and 11 cm tall. **Time:** about 45 minutes each.

Use cotton worsted yarn in two colours — cotton soaks up condensation and insulates against a hot mug, and the contrast colour makes the heart read clearly.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream and dusty pink cotton worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mug-rug-heart-motif-crochet-materials.webp)

Cotton worsted yarn (#4) in two colours — A main cream, B contrast dusty pink: about 25 g of A and 10 g of B per rug; a 4 mm hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Check your gauge after 5 rows — if 16 stitches measure more than 10.5 cm across, go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

**Base:** Chain 25. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (24). Rows 2–20: chain 1, turn, sc across (24). The rug is 15 cm wide and 11 cm tall.

**Heart:** The heart is worked in colour B over Rows 7–13, in the middle 9 stitches (stitches 8–16). Carry the unused colour loosely across the back of the work, or cut it and rejoin it on each row — either way, weave in the ends on the back so the front stays flat. Read the chart from the bottom up: Row 7 is the point of the heart, Row 13 is the top with its two lobes. Rows 1–6 and 14–20 are all in colour A.

- Row 7: A 11, B 1, A 12
- Row 8: A 10, B 3, A 11
- Row 9: A 9, B 5, A 10
- Row 10: A 8, B 7, A 9
- Row 11: A 7, B 9, A 8
- Row 12: A 7, B 9, A 8
- Row 13: A 8, B 2, A 3, B 2, A 9
