![Close-up of a heart motif in dusty pink cotton yarn on a cream crochet mug rug, showing single crochet colourwork stitches](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mug-rug-heart-motif-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Border:** Join colour B at any corner. Work 1 round of sc around all four sides, with 3 sc in each corner stitch, and join with a slip stitch — about 96 stitches in all. The border frames the heart and stops the edges curling. Fasten off and weave in the ends on the back.

## Styling and Care

Set the rug under a mug with the heart showing beside it, and leave room for a teaspoon — the rug is 15 cm wide, so a standard mug and a spoon sit side by side. Make two in swapped colours for a gift set: one cream with a pink heart, one pink with a cream heart. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat; cotton dries quickly and the colours stay true if you wash cold.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What size mug fits?** Any standard mug with a base up to about 9 cm across — the rug is 15 cm wide, so the mug sits in the middle with room for a teaspoon beside it. For an oversized mug, add 4 stitches for each 2.5 cm wider you need, and keep the heart in the middle 9 stitches.

**Will it protect a wooden table?** Yes, for a normal hot mug — cotton insulates and soaks up the condensation that rings a table. It is not a trivet: do not put a boiling pot or a casserole straight from the oven on it. For a very hot mug, fold a second rug underneath, or work the rug in two layers.

**Can I make it in other motifs?** Yes — any motif that fits the same 9-stitch by 7-row window in the middle of the rug: a star, an initial, a flower, a paw print. Keep the colour changes inside stitches 8–16 and Rows 7–13, and the rest of the pattern stays exactly the same.

**Can I make it bigger?** Yes — add 4 stitches for each 2.5 cm wider and 4 rows for each 2 cm taller, and centre the heart in the new size. A 19-stitch by 24-row rug makes a small placemat for a plate and a mug; allow about 15 g more of each colour.

title: Crochet Scrunchies: A Set of 3 in One Evening
excerpt: Crochet three scrunchies in one evening — a flat classic, a ruffle and a full ruffle, all worked in single crochet around a hair elastic.
image_alt: Three handmade crochet scrunchies in sage green, dusty pink and cream, stacked on a wooden table.
content:
A scrunchie is the fastest useful thing you can crochet: a ring of single crochet worked around a hair elastic, finished before a kettle boils. This set makes three in one evening — a flat classic, a ruffle and a full ruffle — all from DK scraps and three elastics. They are the quickest gift on this calendar, and a set of three looks like a proper present, not a leftover.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Working single crochet around a hair elastic, increasing for a ruffle, and keeping your tension even. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** flat scrunchie about 8.5 cm across; ruffle about 10 cm across. **Time:** about 15 minutes for the flat one, 20 minutes for each ruffle — the set of three takes about an hour.

Use DK yarn in three colours. Cotton or acrylic DK grips the elastic best; a slippery yarn slides around and the scrunchie loosens.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of sage green, dusty pink and cream DK yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, three black hair elastics, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-scrunchies-set-of-three-materials.webp)

DK yarn (#3): about 45 g in total — about 10 g for the flat scrunchie, 15 g for the ruffle, 20 g for the full ruffle — so one 50 g ball makes the whole set; a 4 mm crochet hook; three hair elastics, 5 cm across; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure.

Pick a seamless elastic with no metal join. A metal join snags the yarn and catches hair. A fabric-covered elastic grips the stitches well; a plain rubber band is too thin, snaps easily, and cuts through yarn — do not use one.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Increase:** 2 sc in one stitch. **Gauge:** 18 sc and 20 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Gauge matters less here — the elastic sets the size — but check after Round 1: the stitches should cover the elastic completely, with no bare elastic showing.

## Elastic Sizes

Match the elastic to the hair it will hold. The Round 1 stitch count changes with the elastic, and everything else stays the same.

| Hair | Elastic across | Round 1 stitches |
|---|---|---|
| Fine or thin | 4 cm | 40 |
| Most hair | 5 cm | 48 |
| Thick or curly | 6 cm | 56 |

The numbers below are for the standard 5 cm elastic with 48 stitches in Round 1.

## The Pattern

All three scrunchies start the same way. Work Round 1 around the elastic itself, not into a chain: insert the hook under the elastic, yarn over, pull up a loop, and finish the single crochet. Push the stitches together as you go so they bunch up and cover the elastic.

**Round 1 (all three):** Work 48 sc around the elastic. Join with a slip stitch to the first sc. (48)

**Scrunchie 1 — Classic flat:** Rounds 2–4: chain 1, sc in each stitch around (48), join with a slip stitch. Fasten off and weave in the ends. The band is about 2 cm wide and lies flat.

**Scrunchie 2 — Ruffle:** Round 2: chain 1, work 2 sc in each stitch around (96), join. Round 3: chain 1, sc in each stitch around (96), join. Fasten off. The extra stitches have nowhere to go, so the edge waves into a ruffle.

**Scrunchie 3 — Full ruffle:** Round 2: chain 1, work 2 sc in each stitch around (96), join. Round 3: chain 1, *sc in the next stitch, 2 sc in the next stitch; repeat from * around (144), join. Round 4: chain 1, sc in each stitch around (144), join. Fasten off. This one is twice as full as the ruffle and stands up on its own.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet scrunchie in dusty pink yarn, showing single crochet stitches worked around a hair elastic with a ruffled edge](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-scrunchies-set-of-three-closeup.webp)

If a ruffle curls under instead of waving out, turn the work inside out — the right side is the smooth side, and the ruffle opens up once it is the right way round.

## Styling and Care

Wear one on your wrist, or twist it twice around a ponytail or a bun. The flat one suits everyday wear; the ruffles suit a party or a gift box. Hand wash cold and dry flat, or machine wash on gentle inside a laundry bag. Do not tumble dry: heat weakens the elastic, and a scrunchie with a stretched elastic is just a ring of yarn.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Which elastic works best?** A seamless elastic with no metal join, 5 cm across for most hair. Fabric-covered elastics grip the stitches and hold a ponytail without sliding. Avoid thin rubber bands: they snap, they cut through yarn, and they pull hair.

**How do I stop the yarn slipping?** Push the Round 1 stitches tight together so no elastic shows, and work that round with a slightly firmer tension than usual. If the fabric still slides, sew three or four stitches through the elastic with the tail when you weave in the ends. Cotton or acrylic DK grips well; a silky or bamboo-blend yarn slides, so save that for another project.

**Can I sell them at markets?** Yes — they are quick, they cost very little to make, and they sell best as a set of three in matching colours. Price them to cover the yarn, the elastics and your time, and display them on a small card. Check your market's rules for handmade goods before your first stall.

**Can I use other yarn weights?** Yes — keep the elastic the same and change the stitch count. With worsted yarn and a 5 mm hook, work 40 sc around the elastic; with 4-ply yarn and a 3.5 mm hook, work 56 sc. The increase rounds stay the same: double the stitches for a ruffle, then add half again for a full ruffle.

title: Heart Keychain in Chenille Yarn
excerpt: Crochet a plush chenille heart keychain in under an hour — two lobes joined into a heart, with a chain loop for the ring.
image_alt: A handmade plush pink chenille heart keychain with a metal ring, on a wooden table beside keys.
content:
A plush chenille heart on a keychain ring is a small thing that gets a big reaction: soft, squishy, and finished in under an hour. It makes a party favour, a bag charm, or a last-minute gift, and it is made in batches — work a row of lobes, then a row of hearts, and a 100 g ball of chenille turns into eight or ten keychains.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A magic ring, single crochet increases and decreases, joining two lobes into a heart, and attaching a keychain ring. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 7 cm wide and 6.5 cm tall. **Time:** 30–45 minutes each.

Use chenille yarn in one colour for the heart and a metal split ring for the keychain. Chenille is a bulky yarn with a soft pile, so a 4 mm hook makes a tight fabric and the stuffing stays hidden.

## Materials and Tools

![A ball of blush pink chenille yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, a silver keychain split ring, a yarn needle, scissors and a small pile of toy stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/heart-keychain-chenille-yarn-crochet-materials.webp)

Chenille yarn (#5 bulky): about 10 g per heart; a 4 mm crochet hook; one keychain split ring, about 25 mm across; a large-eye blunt yarn needle — chenille needs a big eye and a blunt point so it does not split the pile; a small amount of toy stuffing; stitch markers; scissors.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Decrease:** sc2tog (pull up a loop in each of the next 2 stitches, yarn over, pull through all 3 loops). **Gauge:** 14 sc and 14 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook.

Chenille stitches are hard to see — the pile hides them. Count by feel, not by sight, and mark the first stitch of every round with a stitch marker. Work slowly and pull the yarn gently: chenille splits if you yank it, and you cannot rip it back cleanly.

## The Pattern

**Lobe (make 2):** The heart is two small cups joined together, so start with two identical lobes.

Round 1: Make a magic ring, work 6 sc into the ring, pull it closed. (6)

Round 2: Work 2 sc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *3 sc, 2 sc in the next stitch; repeat from * twice more. (15)

Fasten off the first lobe. Leave the second lobe on the hook — do not fasten it off.

**Joining the lobes:** Round 4: Work 15 sc around the first lobe, then 15 sc around the second lobe — 30 stitches in all. The dip between the two lobes is the top of the heart. If a small hole opens at the join, close it later with the tail.

Round 5: Sc in each stitch around. (30)

**Shaping the point:** Round 6: *3 sc, sc2tog; repeat from * around. (24)

Round 7: *2 sc, sc2tog; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 8: *sc, sc2tog; repeat from * around. (12) Stuff the heart lightly now — just enough to hold its shape, not so much that the stitches stretch open.

Round 9: sc2tog around. (6) Fasten off, thread the tail through the last 6 stitches, pull tight, and weave it in.

![Close-up of a handmade plush pink chenille crochet heart, showing soft fuzzy chenille single crochet stitches and the two lobes at the top](https://cozyloops.site/assets/heart-keychain-chenille-yarn-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Attaching the ring:** Join yarn at the dip between the two lobes. Chain 6, slip stitch into the same spot to form a small loop, and fasten off. Thread the split ring through the loop. The loop lets the ring swing freely; sewing the ring straight onto the heart makes it sit stiffly and wear through the yarn.

**Batch tips:** Work in batches — all the first lobes, then all the second lobes, then join and stuff them one after another. Keep a finished heart beside you as a size check. One 100 g ball of chenille makes about eight to ten hearts.

## Styling and Care

Clip the heart to keys, a bag, a backpack, or a zipper pull. Spot clean with a damp cloth and a little soap, and let it dry flat. Machine washing is possible on cold and gentle, but the pile can mat, so hand washing keeps it soft for longer. Do not tumble dry chenille.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Does chenille yarn split?** Yes — the soft pile can pull away from the core thread if you yank the yarn or rip stitches back. Pull gently, work slowly, and if you make a mistake, cut the yarn and rejoin it rather than frogging a whole round. If a stitch does split, work over it: the pile hides it once the next round is on.

**How do I attach the ring?** With a chain loop, not by sewing the ring on directly. Chain 6 at the dip between the lobes, slip stitch into the same spot to close the loop, and thread the split ring through it. The loop is stronger than a sewn join because the ring moves freely instead of sawing through one spot.

**Can I make them in other shapes?** Yes — the same rounds make other things. Work one lobe alone and continue with the decrease rounds for a round ball, which becomes a pumpkin in orange yarn with a short green stem, or a strawberry in red with a green top. Change the yarn colour and the loop stays the same.

**What if my heart comes out lopsided?** Count both lobes first — each one must have 15 stitches, and a lobe with 14 or 16 pulls the whole heart to one side. Then check the stuffing: push the same small amount into each lobe and pinch the point into shape while the heart is still soft. Block it if it still leans: pin it to shape, steam lightly, and let it dry.

title: Crochet Sunglasses Holder with a Strap
excerpt: Crochet a padded sunglasses holder with a wrist strap — cotton shell, fabric lining, and a fit guide for three common frame widths.
image_alt: A handmade cream crochet sunglasses holder with a wrist strap, with dark sunglasses tucked inside, on a wooden table.
content:
A pair of sunglasses lives at the bottom of a bag, scratched by keys. A crochet sunglasses holder fixes that: a padded pouch the glasses slide into whole, with a wrist strap. It is not a strap cover and not a phone pouch — the glasses go inside, lenses protected on both sides by a cotton shell with a fabric lining.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Single crochet worked flat in rows, folding and seaming, a fabric lining, and a wrist strap. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** standard about 17.5 cm wide and 8 cm tall, with a wrist strap loop about 25 cm around. **Time:** about 2 hours.

Use cotton worsted yarn — cotton is firm enough to hold its shape and soft enough not to scratch lenses, where a rough acrylic can leave marks.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream cotton worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, scissors, a tape measure, a wooden button and cotton lining fabric on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-sunglasses-holder-strap-materials.webp)

Cotton worsted yarn (#4): about 50 g in one colour; a 4 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure; a piece of cotton fabric about 17 by 16 cm for the lining; one button about 1.5 cm across (optional, for the button closure).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Check your gauge after 5 rows — if 16 stitches measure more than 10.5 cm across, go down half a hook size.

## Sizes

Measure your sunglasses folded flat, across the widest point, and pick the size whose holder is about 3 cm wider than the frames. The numbers below are for the shell; every size is worked 28 rows tall.

| Frames folded | Chain | Stitches | Holder width |
|---|---|---|---|
| Narrow, up to 13 cm | 27 | 26 | about 16 cm |
| Standard, up to 14.5 cm | 29 | 28 | about 17.5 cm |
| Wide, up to 16 cm | 33 | 32 | about 20 cm |

## The Pattern

The numbers below are for the standard size; the other sizes change only the starting chain.

**Shell:** Chain 29. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (28). Rows 2–28: chain 1, turn, sc across (28). The rectangle is now about 17.5 cm wide and 15.5 cm tall. Fasten off.

**Folding and seaming:** Fold the rectangle in half, wrong sides together, so the two short ends meet at the top. Whip stitch the two side edges together through both layers, from the fold up to the top edge — 14 rows each side. Turn the holder right side out so the seams sit inside. The pocket is now about 17.5 cm wide and 8 cm tall.

**Lining:** Fold the fabric in half and sew the two side edges with a 1 cm seam. Slip the lining inside the shell and fold its top edge down 1 cm, then whip stitch it to the top row of the shell, one stitch per sc, all the way around. The lining stops the glasses catching on the stitches and gives the holder its padded feel.

![Close-up of a handmade crochet sunglasses holder in cream cotton yarn, showing single crochet stitches and the thick padded double-layer edge with a wrist strap](https://cozyloops.site/assets/crochet-sunglasses-holder-strap-closeup.webp)

**Strap:** Chain 41. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (40). Row 2: chain 1, turn, sc across (40). Fasten off, leaving a long tail. The strap is about 25 cm long and 1 cm wide. Fold it in half to make a loop and sew both ends to the same top corner of the holder with the tail, through both layers of the shell.

**Button closure (optional):** Sew the button on the back top edge, about 4 cm from the corner. On the front top edge, opposite the button, join yarn and chain 4, then slip stitch into the same stitch to form a small loop. The loop slips over the button and keeps the glasses from sliding out.

## Styling and Care

Slide the glasses in lenses down, strap on your wrist, and the holder goes from bag to beach on its own. Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle and dry flat, reshaping the pocket while it is damp so it keeps its width. Do not tumble dry: heat makes cotton tighten and the pocket will no longer fit the glasses.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Will my sunglasses fit?** Measure the frames folded flat across the widest point and use the size table — the holder is about 3 cm wider than the frames. Between sizes, go up: a loose holder still protects, and a tight one bends the arms. Frames over 16 cm wide need the wide size with 2 extra stitches.

**Is the padding enough?** For everyday use, yes — the cotton shell plus the fabric lining cushions the lenses against keys and coins. It is not a hard case: do not sit on it or pack it under heavy books. For extra protection, add a second lining layer cut from felt.

**Can I add a button closure?** Yes — the pattern includes one: a button on the back top edge and a chain-4 loop on the front. A press stud works too, sewn through both layers. Skip it if the glasses stay in a bag; the strap alone is enough for carrying.

**Can I make it for reading glasses?** Yes — work the narrow shell with 4 fewer stitches: chain 23, 22 stitches across, about 14 cm wide, and the same 28 rows. Reading glasses are lighter, so the strap is optional; leave it off and the holder slips into a jacket pocket.

title: Mini Pouch with a Zipper: Step-by-Step
excerpt: Crochet a mini pouch with a zipper, sewn in step by step — pin, tack, sew — plus an optional lining and a size table.
image_alt: A handmade sage green crochet mini pouch with a zipper, on a wooden table beside coins and a lip balm.
content:
A zipper is the one skill that turns a crochet pouch from a pocket into a proper bag — and it is much easier than it looks. This mini pouch is a plain rectangle with a 15 cm zipper sewn in step by step: pin, tack, sew. No shaping, no gusset, just a pouch that closes. It is not a phone pouch and not a shaped bag — the whole point is the zipper, and the optional lining is what makes it feel finished.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A single crochet rectangle, whip-stitch seams, zipper insertion step by step, and an optional lining. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 16 cm wide and 9 cm tall. **Time:** about 2 hours, plus 30 minutes for the lining.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of sage green worsted yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, a dark green 15 cm zipper, floral cotton lining fabric, a yarn needle, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-pouch-zipper-crochet-pattern-materials.webp)

Worsted weight yarn (#4): about 40 g in one colour; a 4 mm crochet hook; one zipper, 15 cm long; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure; a sewing needle and thread to match the zipper; pins; a piece of lining fabric about 16 by 18 cm (optional).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Gauge:** 16 sc and 18 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Check your gauge after 5 rows — if 16 stitches measure more than 10.5 cm across, go down half a hook size, or the pouch will come out wider than the zipper.

## Sizes

The zipper sets the size: pick one about 1 cm shorter than the pouch is wide, so the tape ends tuck into the side seams.

| Zipper | Chain | Stitches | Rows | Pouch size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 cm | 21 | 20 | 26 | about 12.5 by 7 cm |
| 15 cm | 27 | 26 | 32 | about 16 by 9 cm |
| 18 cm | 31 | 30 | 36 | about 19 by 10 cm |

## The Pattern

The numbers below are for the 15 cm zipper; the other sizes change only the starting chain and the row count.

**Body:** Chain 27. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (26). Rows 2–32: chain 1, turn, sc across (26). The rectangle is now about 16 cm wide and 18 cm tall. Fasten off.

**Fold and seam:** Fold the rectangle in half, wrong sides together, and whip stitch the two side edges through both layers, from the fold to the top — 16 rows each side. Turn the pouch right side out. It is now about 16 cm wide and 9 cm tall.

**Zipper, step by step:**

1. **Pin.** Open the zipper and lay one tape along the inside of a top edge, teeth facing up and the slider at the right end. Pin the tape to the crochet every 2 cm, keeping the tape straight and the teeth just above the top row.
2. **Tack.** With the sewing needle and thread, run long basting stitches along the tape, about 5 mm from the teeth, from one end to the other. The basting holds the zipper exactly where the pins put it.
3. **Sew.** With the yarn needle and matching yarn, whip stitch through the tape and the top row of sc, one stitch per sc, 26 stitches in all. Keep the stitches small and even, about 5 mm from the teeth, so the slider runs free.
4. **Repeat.** Pin, tack and sew the other side of the zipper to the other top edge, with the slider at the same end.
5. **Test.** Pull out all the basting and test the zipper twice. If it catches, the stitches are too close to the teeth there — take out two or three and re-sew them a little further back.

![Close-up of a metal zipper sewn into the top edge of a sage green crochet mini pouch, showing single crochet stitches and neat whip stitches attaching the zipper tape](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-pouch-zipper-crochet-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Lining (optional):** Cut the fabric 16 by 18 cm, fold it in half and sew the two side edges with a 1 cm seam. Turn it right side out, slip it inside the pouch, fold its top edge down 1 cm and whip stitch it to the zipper tape just below the teeth. The lining hides the wrong side and stops small things catching on the stitches.

**Finishing:** Weave in all the ends on the inside and press the pouch flat with your hands — never iron a zipper, or the teeth can melt.

## Styling and Care

Coins, a lip balm, keys, earbuds: the pouch holds the small things that sink to the bottom of a bag. Machine wash cold on gentle inside a laundry bag, zipper closed, and dry flat. Do not tumble dry, and do not iron the zipper.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What zipper length do I need?** One about 1 cm shorter than the pouch is wide — 15 cm here, 12 cm for the small size, 18 cm for the large. A longer zipper will not sit flat, and a much shorter one leaves a gap at each end.

**How do I sew it without puckering?** Pin every 2 cm and tack before you sew — the basting stops the tape creeping while you work. Sew one stitch per sc and do not pull the thread tight. If it puckers, take the stitches out and re-pin the tape a little looser.

**Can I skip the lining?** Yes — the pouch is finished without it, and the zipper steps are exactly the same. The lining only hides the wrong side and keeps small things from catching on the stitches. Without it, weave in the ends neatly on the inside.

**Can I make it bigger?** Yes — use the size table: an 18 cm zipper needs chain 31, 30 stitches across and 36 rows, for a pouch about 19 by 10 cm. Allow about 10 g more yarn per size up.

title: Mini Cat Amigurumi: Pocket Size
excerpt: Crochet a pocket-size cat in one evening — a sitting amigurumi about 8 cm tall, with pointy ears, a curled tail and an optional keychain loop.
image_alt: A tiny handmade grey crochet cat sitting upright, with pink inner ears, a pink embroidered nose and a curled tail, on a wooden table.
content:
A pocket cat is the smallest useful amigurumi you can make in one evening: a sitting cat about 8 cm tall, worked in single crochet from a magic ring, with pointy ears, a curled tail and a keychain loop if you want one. It is a single standalone cat, not one of a set, and the only shaping is the same increase and decrease you already know.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A magic ring, single crochet increases and decreases, joining small pieces, and an embroidered face. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 8 cm tall sitting, ears included, and about 3.5 cm wide. **Time:** about 2 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of grey DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, two 6 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and a small pile of toy stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-cat-amigurumi-pocket-size-materials.webp)

DK yarn (#3): about 20 g in the main colour, plus a small amount in a contrast colour for the inner ears; a 3 mm crochet hook; two safety eyes, 6 mm across; a small amount of toy stuffing; a yarn needle; stitch markers; scissors; pink embroidery thread for the nose; one split ring, about 20 mm across (optional, for the keychain loop).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Increase (inc):** 2 sc in one stitch. **Decrease (dec):** sc2tog. **Gauge:** 22 sc and 24 rows measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Mark the first stitch of every round — one missed increase makes the whole cat lean.

## The Pattern

**Body:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 4: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (24)

Rounds 5–7: Sc in each stitch around. (24)

Round 8: *2 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 9: *Sc, dec; repeat from * around. (12) Stuff lightly now — firm enough to sit, not so full the stitches stretch open.

Round 10: Dec around. (6) Fasten off and close. The body is about 4 cm tall and 3.5 cm wide.

**Head:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 4: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (24)

Rounds 5–6: Sc in each stitch around. (24)

Round 7: *2 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (18) Place the safety eyes between Rounds 5 and 6, 6 stitches apart.

Round 8: *Sc, dec; repeat from * around. (12) Stuff lightly.

Round 9: Dec around. (6) Fasten off and close. Sew the head to the top of the body, centred, eyes facing forward.

**Ears (make 2):** Work Rounds 1–2 in the contrast colour for pink inner ears, then switch to the main colour.

Round 1: Magic ring, 4 sc. (4)

Round 2: *Sc, inc; repeat from * once more. (6)

Round 3: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * once more. (8)

Round 4: Sc in each stitch around. (8) Fasten off, flatten the ear, and sew it to the top of the head, pink side forward.

![Close-up of a tiny handmade grey crochet cat, showing single crochet stitches, a pink embroidered nose and pointy ears with pink inner ears](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-cat-amigurumi-pocket-size-closeup.webp)

**Tail:** Magic ring, 6 sc, then 4 rounds of sc around (6). The tube is about 2 cm long. Fasten off and sew it to the back of the body, curving it up toward the head.

**Legs (make 2):** Magic ring, 6 sc, then 2 rounds of sc around (6). Fasten off and sew them to the front of the body, side by side, so the cat sits upright on its flat base.

**Face:** With pink thread, stitch a small triangle nose between the eyes, two short lines for the mouth, and three short whiskers on each side.

**Keychain loop (optional):** Chain 12, slip stitch into the top of the head between the ears to form a loop about 5 cm around. Thread the split ring through it — the loop lets the ring move freely instead of sawing through one spot.

## Styling and Care

The cat sits on a desk, a shelf, or a keychain. Hand wash cold and dry flat, reshaping the ears while it is damp. Do not tumble dry: heat makes the stuffing clump and the cat goes lopsided. Safety eyes are not for children under 3 — for a baby gift, embroider the eyes instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How small can I make it?** Use 4-ply yarn and a 2.5 mm hook with the same round counts, and the cat comes out about 6–7 cm tall. Go smaller than that and the safety eyes no longer fit — use 5 mm eyes, or embroider them. Do not just work tighter with the same yarn: tight stitches with a 3 mm hook make a stiff cat that will not sit flat.

**Can I put it on a keychain?** Yes — the pattern includes a chain-12 loop at the top of the head and a 20 mm split ring. Sew the loop through both layers of the head so it cannot pull out, and use a proper split ring, not a jump ring that can bend open.

**What yarn keeps the shape?** Cotton or acrylic DK. Cotton holds its shape best and the stitches stay crisp; acrylic is softer and a little springier. Avoid bamboo blends and chenille: they are too soft, the ears flop, and the cat will not sit up. Whatever you use, stuff firmly — a soft cat slumps, a firm cat sits.

**Can I make it in other colours?** Yes — the same rounds make any cat. For a tabby, change colour every 2 rounds on the body and head; for a calico, work the head in one colour and the body in another; for a black cat, use a light colour for the nose and whiskers so the face shows.

title: Mini Octopus Amigurumi with Curly Tentacles
excerpt: Crochet a mini octopus with curly tentacles — one dome head and eight spiral tentacles, each one a chain that curls itself.
image_alt: A tiny handmade coral crochet octopus with a round dome head, eight curly spiral tentacles, safety eyes and an embroidered smile, on a wooden table.
content:
Eight tentacles sounds like eight times the work, but a mini octopus is one of the fastest amigurumi you can crochet: a single dome for the head and eight identical tentacles, each one a chain that curls itself. The curl is not a trick you have to learn — it happens because every chain gets two stitches, and the extra stitches have nowhere to go but round into a spiral. This is a single standalone octopus, in one colour or two, and the whole thing fits in your hand.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A magic ring, single crochet increases and decreases, chain-curl tentacles, and joining pieces. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 9 cm tall, with a head about 5 cm across. **Time:** about 2 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of coral DK yarn with a 3.5 mm crochet hook, two 8 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and a small pile of toy stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-octopus-amigurumi-curly-tentacles-materials.webp)

DK yarn (#3): about 25 g in the main colour, plus about 15 g in a contrast colour (optional, for the tentacles); a 3.5 mm crochet hook; two safety eyes, 8 mm across; a small amount of toy stuffing; a yarn needle; stitch markers; scissors; black embroidery thread for the smile.

Chenille works too — same counts with a 4 mm hook, about 1 cm bigger — but the stitches are hard to see, so count by feel.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Increase (inc):** 2 sc in one stitch. **Decrease (dec):** sc2tog. **Gauge:** 20 sc and 22 rows measure 10 cm with a 3.5 mm hook.

## The Pattern

**Head:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 4: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (24)

Round 5: *3 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (30)

Rounds 6–10: Sc in each stitch around. (30)

Round 11: *3 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (24)

Round 12: *2 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (18) Place the safety eyes between Rounds 8 and 9, 8 stitches apart. Stuff firmly now — a soft head dents where the tentacles pull.

Round 13: *Sc, dec; repeat from * around. (12)

Round 14: Dec around. (6) Fasten off and close. The head is about 6.5 cm tall and 5 cm across.

**The curl, in one paragraph:** Chain 16. Work 2 sc in the 2nd chain from the hook, then 2 sc in every chain across — 30 stitches in all. The chain underneath is only 15 stitches long, so the row of 30 has to fold, and it folds into a tight spiral about 4 cm long. That is the whole technique: two stitches per chain makes a curl, one per chain stays flat, three per chain makes a corkscrew so tight it tangles. If a tentacle comes out straight, you missed the increases — count them: 30, not 15.

![Close-up of a handmade coral crochet octopus tentacle, showing a tight spiral curl made from two single crochet stitches in every chain](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-octopus-amigurumi-curly-tentacles-closeup.webp)

**Tentacles (make 8):** Chain 16, then 2 sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and 2 sc in each chain across (30). Fasten off, leaving a long tail. Work them one at a time and lay each one flat — piled up, they tangle before you sew one on. Hold the head upside down and sew them around the bottom edge, 3 stitches apart, one at a time: sew one on, lay it flat, sew the next, so they never cross.

**Two colours:** Work four tentacles in the main colour and four in the contrast colour, alternating them around the head. Join the new colour at the base of each tentacle — carrying yarn up the chain leaves a stripe down its back.

**Face:** With black thread, stitch a small smile below the eyes: two short curved lines, about 1 cm long, meeting in the middle. Keep it small — a big smile on a 5 cm face looks worried, not happy.

## Styling and Care

The octopus sits flat on its tentacles, so it stands on a desk or a shelf without rolling away. Hand wash cold and dry flat, reshaping the tentacles into their curls while it is damp. Do not tumble dry: heat makes the stuffing clump and the head goes lopsided. For a child under 3, embroider the eyes instead of safety eyes.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I make the tentacles curl?** Work 2 sc in every chain — 30 stitches on a 15-chain base. The curl comes from the increases, not from blocking or steaming. If a tentacle comes out straight, count it: 15 stitches means you worked one per chain, and it needs to be 30. For a tighter corkscrew, work 3 sc in every chain; for a gentle wave, alternate 2 sc and 1 sc down the chain.

**Can I make it in two colours?** Yes — the pattern is written for it. Work four tentacles in each colour and alternate them around the head, or work the head in one colour and all eight tentacles in another. Join the new colour at the base of each tentacle; carrying yarn up the chain leaves a stripe down the tentacle.

**Is it a good desk toy?** Yes — it sits flat on its tentacles and is about 9 cm tall, soft enough to squeeze and small enough for a desk corner. It is not a baby toy as written: safety eyes are not for children under 3, so embroider the eyes instead for a little one. Keep it out of direct sun, or the colour fades.

**Can I make it bigger?** Yes — use worsted yarn and a 4.5 mm hook with the same round counts, and the octopus comes out about 12 cm tall. Or keep the same yarn and add two straight rounds to the head (Rounds 6–12 instead of 6–10) for a taller dome. Do not just add tentacles: eight fits evenly around the bottom edge, 3 stitches apart.

title: Mini Frog Amigurumi with a Crown
excerpt: Crochet a mini frog with a crown in one evening — a sitting amigurumi about 9 cm tall, with eye bumps, a gold crown and an embroidered smile.
image_alt: A tiny handmade green crochet frog sitting upright, with two round eye bumps, a small gold crochet crown and an embroidered smile, on a wooden table.
content:
A frog with a crown is a desk friend with a story: a small green frog sitting upright, two round eye bumps on top of its head, and a tiny gold crown perched between them. It is a single standalone frog, not one of a set. The crown is worked flat, folded into a ring, and sewn on — no glue, no wire.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A magic ring, increases and decreases, joining small pieces, a flat crown, and an embroidered face. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 9 cm tall sitting, crown included, and about 4 cm wide. **Time:** about 2 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of green DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, a small ball of gold DK yarn, two 8 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and a small pile of toy stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-frog-amigurumi-crown-pattern-materials.webp)

Green DK yarn (#3): about 25 g; gold DK yarn, a small amount, for the crown; a 3 mm crochet hook; two safety eyes, 8 mm across; a small amount of toy stuffing; a yarn needle; stitch markers; scissors; black embroidery thread for the mouth; pink thread for the cheeks (optional).

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Increase (inc):** 2 sc in one stitch. **Decrease (dec):** sc2tog. **Gauge:** 22 sc and 24 rows measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Mark the first stitch of every round — one missed increase makes the whole frog lean.

## The Pattern

**Body:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 4: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (24)

Round 5: *3 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (30)

Rounds 6–8: Sc in each stitch around. (30)

Round 9: *3 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (24)

Round 10: *2 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (18) Stuff firmly now — a soft body will not hold the head up.

Rounds 11–12: *Sc, dec* (12), then dec around (6). Fasten off and close. The body is about 5 cm tall and 4 cm wide — flatten the base so it sits flat.

**Head:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 4: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (24)

Rounds 5–7: Sc in each stitch around. (24)

Rounds 8–10: *2 sc, dec* (18), *sc, dec* (12), dec around (6). Stuff lightly at Round 8. Fasten off and close. Sew the head to the top of the body, centred, facing forward.

**Eye bumps (make 2):** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Rounds 3–4: Sc in each stitch around. (12) Fasten off, leaving a long tail. Push a safety eye through the centre of each bump, fasten the washer inside, and sew the bumps to the top of the head, 4 stitches apart, eyes forward.

![Close-up of a tiny handmade green crochet frog, showing single crochet stitches, two round eye bumps with safety eyes, and a small gold crochet crown between them](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-frog-amigurumi-crown-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Front legs (make 2):** Magic ring, 6 sc, then 3 rounds of sc around (6). The tube is about 1.5 cm long. Fasten off and sew them to the front of the body, side by side, pointing down like little arms.

**Back feet (make 2):** Round 1: Magic ring, 8 sc. (8)

Round 2: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (12)

Round 3: Sc in each stitch around. (12) Fasten off, flatten the foot, and sew it to the base of the body, one on each side, so the frog sits on its feet.

**Crown:** Worked flat in gold yarn. Chain 13. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across (12). Row 2: chain 1, turn, sc across (12). Row 3 (points): slip stitch in the first stitch, *chain 3, skip 1 stitch, slip stitch in the next stitch; repeat from * 4 more times, then slip stitch in the last stitch — 5 points. Fasten off, sew the short ends together into a ring, and sew the crown between the eye bumps, through its bottom row at four points around the ring.

**Face:** With black thread, stitch a wide smile below the eyes: one long curved line, about 3 cm across. Add pink cheeks if you like — a French knot on each side.

## Styling and Care

The frog sits on a desk, a shelf, or a windowsill. Hand wash cold and dry flat, reshaping the crown points while it is damp. Do not tumble dry: heat makes the stuffing clump and the frog goes lopsided. Safety eyes are not for children under 3 — for a baby gift, embroider the eyes instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I make the crown stay on?** Sew it, don't glue it: sew through the bottom row of the crown and into the head at four points around the ring, pulling each stitch snug. Glue comes off in the wash. If the crown slides, the ring is too loose — work Row 1 with one fewer chain (chain 12, 11 stitches).

**Will it sit upright?** Yes, if the body is stuffed firmly and the base is flat: press the base flat after stuffing, and sew the feet at the front so they prop the body up. If it leans, the head is off-centre — re-sew it level.

**Can I make a prince and a princess?** Yes. The prince wears the gold crown as written; the princess wears a pink or lilac crown, with a small bow beside it: chain 8, work 2 rows of sc, pinch the middle and wrap yarn around it. Or leave the crown off for a plain frog.

**Can I make it in other colours?** Yes. A tree frog is bright green with a cream belly; a bullfrog is dark green with a brown back; a dart frog is red or blue with black spots embroidered on the body. Keep the crown gold — it suits every colour.

title: Mini Turtle Amigurumi with a Shell Pattern
excerpt: Crochet a mini turtle with a ring-patterned shell — one dome in four shell colourways, with a small head, flippers and tail.
image_alt: A tiny handmade crochet turtle with a domed shell of concentric brown, green and cream rings, a green head and little flippers, on a wooden table.
content:
A turtle is all shell: a dome with a real colourwork pattern, worked in rings of colour so the shell looks like it grew that way. This one is a single standalone turtle, not one of a set, and it comes in four shell colourways — change the colours, keep the rounds.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** A magic ring, increases and decreases, changing colours in rounds, and joining pieces. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 8 cm long and 5 cm tall. **Time:** about 2 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of green, brown and cream DK yarn with a 3 mm crochet hook, two 8 mm safety eyes, a yarn needle, scissors and a small pile of toy stuffing on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-turtle-amigurumi-shell-pattern-materials.webp)

Green DK yarn (#3): about 20 g; brown DK yarn, about 15 g; cream DK yarn, about 10 g; a 3 mm crochet hook; two safety eyes, 8 mm across; a small amount of toy stuffing; a yarn needle; stitch markers; scissors; black thread for the smile.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Increase (inc):** 2 sc in one stitch. **Decrease (dec):** sc2tog. **Gauge:** 22 sc and 24 rows measure 10 cm with a 3 mm hook. Count the stitches at the end of every increase round — a missed increase makes the shell lopsided.

## Shell Colourways

Pick one colourway and work the shell rounds in its colours — keep the contrast between the rings.

| Colourway | Rounds 1–2 | Rounds 3–4 | Rounds 5–6 | Rounds 7–10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic | brown | green | brown | cream |
| Forest | dark green | sage green | dark green | cream |
| Desert | tan | cream | tan | brown |
| Ocean | teal | sand | teal | cream |

## The Pattern

**Shell:** The numbers below are for the classic colourway (brown, green, brown, cream).

Rounds 1–2 (brown): Magic ring, 6 sc, then inc in each stitch around. (12)

Rounds 3–4 (green): *Sc, inc* (18), then *2 sc, inc* (24).

Rounds 5–6 (brown): *3 sc, inc* (30), then *4 sc, inc* (36).

Rounds 7–8 (cream): Sc in each stitch around. (36)

Rounds 9–10 (cream): *4 sc, dec* (30), then *3 sc, dec* (24). Stuff the shell lightly, just enough to hold its dome, and fasten off, leaving a long tail.

Change colour on the last yarn-over of the last stitch of the old colour: work the stitch until the last yarn-over, drop the old colour, yarn over with the new colour and pull through. Carry the unused colour up the inside of the shell instead of cutting it.

**Body:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Round 4: *2 sc, inc; repeat from * around. (24)

Rounds 5–6: Sc in each stitch around. (24)

Round 7: *2 sc, dec; repeat from * around. (18) Stuff firmly now — a soft body will not hold the shell up.

Rounds 8–9: *Sc, dec* (12), then dec around (6). Fasten off and close. Flatten the body slightly so the shell sits level.

**Head:** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: Inc in each stitch around. (12)

Round 3: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (18)

Rounds 4–5: Sc in each stitch around. (18) Place the safety eyes between Rounds 4 and 5, 4 stitches apart.

Rounds 6–7: *Sc, dec* (12), then dec around (6). Stuff lightly at Round 6. Fasten off and close. Sew the head to the front of the body, tilted slightly up.

![Close-up of a tiny handmade crochet turtle shell, showing concentric rings of brown, green and cream single crochet stitches](https://cozyloops.site/assets/mini-turtle-amigurumi-shell-pattern-closeup.webp)

**Flippers (make 4):** Round 1: Magic ring, 6 sc. (6)

Round 2: *Sc, inc; repeat from * around. (9)

Rounds 3–4: Sc in each stitch around. (9) Fasten off, flatten the flipper, and sew two to each side of the body, pointing outwards.

**Tail:** Magic ring, 4 sc, then 2 rounds of sc around (4). Fasten off and sew it to the back of the body, pointing down.

**Assembly:** Sew the shell to the top of the body all the way around its open edge, pulling each stitch snug so no stuffing shows. Then sew on the head, flippers and tail, and stitch a small smile below the eyes with black thread.

## Styling and Care

The turtle sits on a desk or a shelf, where the light catches the rings. Hand wash cold and dry flat, reshaping the shell while it is damp. Do not tumble dry: heat makes the stuffing clump and the shell goes lopsided. Safety eyes are not for children under 3 — for a baby gift, embroider the eyes instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I change shell colours?** Change on the last yarn-over of the last stitch of the old colour, and carry the unused colour up the inside of the shell instead of cutting it. Cut only when a colour is finished for good, and weave the end in on the inside.

**Can I make it bigger?** Yes — use worsted yarn and a 4 mm hook with the same round counts, and the turtle comes out about 10 cm long. Or keep the same yarn and add one more increase round to the shell (Round 7: *5 sc, inc*, 42 stitches) and one more straight round to the body, or the shell will overhang.

**What stuffing works best?** Polyester toy stuffing, teased apart into small pieces so it fills evenly. Stuff the body firmly — it holds the shell up — and the shell lightly, just enough to hold its dome. Avoid cotton wool: it clumps when washed and goes hard. Avoid rice or dried beans: they are not washable, and they make the turtle heavy.

**Can I make it in other colours?** Yes — the pattern is written for four colourways (classic, forest, desert, ocean), and any three colours that sit well together work. Pick a dark centre, a mid-tone ring, and a pale rim — the contrast is what makes the rings read as a shell.

title: Baby Santa Hat with a Pom-Pom (Newborn–12 Months)
excerpt: Crochet a baby Santa hat with a pom-pom — a soft red cone with a white ribbed brim, in four sizes from newborn to 12 months.
image_alt: A handmade red crochet baby Santa hat with a white ribbed brim and a white pom-pom, on a wooden table.
content:
A baby's first Christmas hat should be soft above all: no scratchy yarn against a baby's cheek, no stiff brim, nothing that pulls. This classic Santa hat is a red cone in soft DK yarn, with a white ribbed brim and a white pom-pom on the floppy tip, worked top-down from the tip — no sewing except the pom-pom. The site's baby animal hats guide covers bear, bunny and frog ears; this is the plain Christmas hat that guide skips, in four sizes, newborn to 12 months.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Half double crochet in the round, increasing to shape a cone, a ribbed brim, and a pom-pom. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** newborn 34 cm around, 13 cm long; 0–3 months 37.5 cm, 14 cm; 3–6 months 41 cm, 15 cm; 6–12 months 45 cm, 16 cm. **Time:** 2–3 hours.

Use soft DK yarn in red and white. It sits against a baby's skin, so pick a soft, smooth DK labelled baby-safe or machine-washable, in acrylic or cotton. Wool can irritate, and a scratchy yarn will not be worn twice.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of red and white soft DK yarn with a 4 mm crochet hook, a yarn needle, scissors, a tape measure and a pom-pom maker on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/baby-santa-hat-pom-pom-crochet-materials.webp)

Soft DK yarn (#3): about 50 g in red and 20 g in white for the largest size — one 100 g ball of red and one 50 g ball of white makes any size; a 4 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure; a pom-pom maker, or two cardboard rings about 6 cm across.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), half double crochet (hdc), front and back post double crochet (fpdc, bpdc). **Increase (inc):** 2 hdc in one stitch. **Gauge:** 16 hdc and 20 rows measure 10 cm with a 4 mm hook. Check your gauge after 5 rounds — if 16 stitches measure more than 10.5 cm across, go down half a hook size.

## Baby-safe yarn — read this first

Use a soft, smooth yarn and nothing that sheds: no eyelash or fuzzy yarns, no chenille, no yarn that leaves fibres on your hands. There are no buttons, beads or small sewn-on parts in this pattern, and the pom-pom is sewn on, never glued: sew it through the tip at least four times, pull each stitch snug, and tug it hard before the hat is worn. If it moves, sew it again.

## Sizes

Measure the baby's head around the widest part, above the eyebrows and over the ears. The hat is worked 1–2 cm smaller.

| Size | Head | Hat around | Stitches |
|---|---|---|---|
| Newborn | about 35 cm | about 34 cm | 54 |
| 0–3 months | about 38 cm | about 37.5 cm | 60 |
| 3–6 months | about 41 cm | about 41 cm | 66 |
| 6–12 months | about 44 cm | about 45 cm | 72 |

## The Pattern

Numbers are for the 0–3 months size. Work in red until the brim; *…* means repeat to the end of the round.

**Tip and increases:** R1: Magic ring, 6 hdc (6). R2: Inc around (12). R3: *Hdc, inc* (18). R4: *2 hdc, inc* (24). R5: *3 hdc, inc* (30). R6: *4 hdc, inc* (36). R7: *5 hdc, inc* (42). R8: *6 hdc, inc* (48). R9: *7 hdc, inc* (54). R10: *8 hdc, inc* (60). R11: *9 hdc, inc* (66). R12: *10 hdc, inc* (72). Stop at your size: newborn R9, 0–3 months R10, 3–6 months R11, 6–12 months R12. The narrow tip flops over — that is the shape, not a mistake.

**Straight rounds:** Work hdc around to your size's length: newborn Rounds 10–26 (17 rounds, 13 cm); 0–3 months Rounds 11–28 (18, 14 cm); 3–6 months Rounds 12–30 (19, 15 cm); 6–12 months Rounds 13–32 (20, 16 cm). Join with a slip stitch and chain 2 to start the next round; the chain does not count as a stitch.

![Close-up of a handmade red crochet baby Santa hat, showing half double crochet stitches and the white ribbed brim folded up](https://cozyloops.site/assets/baby-santa-hat-pom-pom-crochet-closeup.webp)

**Brim (white):** Change to white. Round 1: hdc around. Rounds 2–5: *fpdc, bpdc; repeat from * around (every size has an even stitch count, which the ribbing needs). Round 6: hdc around. The brim is about 3 cm tall; fold it up about 2 cm so the ribbing shows as a white band.

**Pom-pom:** Make a white pom-pom about 5 cm across with the pom-pom maker, or wind yarn around two cardboard rings about 6 cm across, tie it tightly, cut the loops and trim it round. Sew it to the tip with the tail, through both layers, at least four times. Tug it hard — if it moves, sew it again.

## Styling and Care

If it is soft enough, the hat stays on after the photos. Machine wash cold on gentle and dry flat, reshaping the brim while it is damp. Do not tumble dry: heat makes the pom-pom clump. Check the pom-pom before every wear.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What yarn is safe for babies?** A soft, smooth DK labelled baby-safe or machine-washable, in acrylic or cotton. Avoid wool for sensitive skin, and avoid anything that sheds: no eyelash yarn, no chenille.

**How do I measure a baby's head?** With a soft tape measure around the widest part, above the eyebrows and over the ears. Measure twice and use the larger number. Between sizes, go up: the hat is worked 1–2 cm smaller than the head.

**Can I make it without the pom-pom?** Yes — just weave in the starting tail at the tip and the hat is a plain pointed baby hat. Some parents prefer no pom-pom for a newborn.

**How do I keep the brim from stretching out?** Work the brim with a hook half a size smaller (3.5 mm), and always fold the brim up when the hat is worn — the fold doubles the band and holds it in shape. If the brim still stretches, work Round 1 of the brim in single crochet instead of hdc.

title: Chunky Crochet Pillow Cover with Bobbles
excerpt: Crochet a chunky pillow cover with bobbles — a 45 cm cover with a button back, no zipper, in about 300 g of chunky yarn.
image_alt: A handmade chunky crochet pillow cover in cream yarn with bobble texture, on a sofa cushion.
content:
A pillow cover is the fastest way to change a room for Christmas: one cover, no new pillow, and the sofa looks dressed. This one is chunky and soft, with bobbles all over the front and a button back, so there is no zipper to sew. It is the cozy-home finale of this calendar, and it uses the bobble stitch from Day 10's bobble Christmas trees — if you made those, you already know it. The cover fits a 45 cm square insert and closes with three buttons.

## Quick Project Overview

**What you will learn:** Bobble stitch in rows, working a front panel and two overlapping back pieces, buttonholes, and joining panels with a round of single crochet. **Skill level:** Easy. **Terminology:** US. **Finished size:** about 45 cm square, to fit a 45 cm pillow insert. **Time:** about 5 hours.

## Materials and Tools

![Balls of cream chunky yarn with a 6 mm crochet hook, three large wooden buttons, a yarn needle, scissors and a tape measure on a wooden table](https://cozyloops.site/assets/chunky-crochet-pillow-cover-bobbles-materials.webp)

Chunky yarn (#5): about 300 g in one colour — the front panel takes about 170 g and the two back pieces about 130 g between them; a 6 mm crochet hook; a yarn needle; scissors; a tape measure; three buttons about 2.5 cm across; a 45 cm square pillow insert.

## Stitches and Gauge

**Stitches used:** chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), single crochet (sc). **Bobble:** (yarn over, insert the hook, yarn over, pull up a loop, yarn over, pull through 2 loops) 5 times in the same stitch, then yarn over and pull through all 6 loops. **Gauge:** 11 sc and 12 rows measure 10 cm with a 6 mm hook. Check your gauge after 5 rows — if 11 stitches measure more than 10.5 cm across, go down half a hook size.

## The Pattern

**Front panel:** Chain 51. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across. (50)

Rows 2–54: turn at the end of each row. Plain rows: chain 1, turn, sc across. (50) Bobble rows: Rows 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48 and 52 — 13 in all.

Bobble row: chain 1, turn, sc 2, *bobble in the next stitch, sc 4; repeat from * 8 more times, bobble in the next stitch, sc 2. (50 stitches, 10 bobbles)

Push each bobble to the front as you work it, so the bobbles pop on the right side. They sit in columns — 10 across, 13 rows down, 130 in all — with 2 plain stitches at each edge and 4 between bobbles. Fasten off when the panel measures 45 cm tall, after Row 54.

**Back pieces (make 2):** Each back piece is a plain rectangle. Chain 51. Row 1: sc in the 2nd chain from the hook and across. (50) Rows 2–30: chain 1, turn, sc across. (50) Each piece is about 45 cm wide and 25 cm tall.

**Buttonholes:** On one back piece — the top piece — work the buttonholes on Row 29 instead of a plain row: sc 8, chain 2, skip 2 stitches, sc 14, chain 2, skip 2 stitches, sc 14, chain 2, skip 2 stitches, sc 8. (50 stitches, 3 buttonholes) Row 30: chain 1, turn, sc across, working 2 sc into each chain-2 space. The buttonholes sit over stitches 9–10, 25–26 and 41–42.

![Close-up of a handmade chunky crochet pillow cover in cream yarn, showing bobble stitches and single crochet stitches](https://cozyloops.site/assets/chunky-crochet-pillow-cover-bobbles-closeup.webp)

**Buttons:** Sew the three buttons to the other back piece — the bottom piece — about 4 cm below its top edge, at stitches 10, 26 and 42, so they line up with the buttonholes when the pieces overlap. Sew each button on firmly and knot it on the wrong side.

**Assembly:** Lay the front panel right side down. Lay the two back pieces on top, wrong sides down, overlapping by 5 cm in the middle, with the top piece's buttonhole edge on top. Join with a round of single crochet through both layers: one sc in each stitch along the top and bottom, one sc in each row-end along the sides — about 208 stitches in all. Fasten off, turn the cover right side out through the button opening, push out the corners, slip in the pillow and button it closed.

## Styling and Care

The cover goes on the sofa, the armchair, or the bed. It suits a plain insert in cream or grey — the bobbles catch the light. Machine wash cold on gentle, buttoned closed and inside out, and dry flat. Do not tumble dry: heat flattens the bobbles and the cover goes limp.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What pillow insert fits?** A 45 cm square insert for a snug fit — the cover is worked to the same size as the insert. For a plumper look, use a 47 cm insert: the cover is 1–2 cm smaller than the insert. Do not use a 40 cm insert — the cover will hang loose and the bobbles will sag.

**Can I wash the cover?** Yes — machine wash cold on gentle, buttoned closed and inside out, inside a laundry bag if you have one. Dry flat, reshaping the cover to 45 cm square while it is damp. Do not tumble dry and do not iron: heat flattens the bobbles.

**How do I stop the bobbles flattening?** Reshape them while the cover is damp: push each bobble out from the inside with a finger. If a bobble still sits flat, hold a steam iron a few centimetres above the wrong side — never press it — and push the bobble out while the yarn is warm.

**Can I make it in other sizes?** Yes — the front panel is a rectangle. For a 40 cm cover, chain 45 (44 stitches) and work 48 rows; for a 50 cm cover, chain 56 (55 stitches) and work 60 rows. Keep the bobble rows every 4th row and the bobbles 5 stitches apart, and make each back piece half the cover height plus 2.5 cm — 27 rows for the 40 cm cover, 33 rows for the 50 cm cover — so the overlap stays 5 cm.
